sentences.zh: 張繼庚，字炳垣，江蘇江寧人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jigeng, courtesy name Bingyuan, was a native of Jiangning in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jigeng, courtesy name Bingyuan, was a native of Jiangning in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父介福，道光六年進士，湖南保靖縣知縣。

translations.literal: His father Jiefu was a jinshi of the sixth year of Daoguang and served as magistrate of Baojing County in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiefu passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of the Daoguang reign (1826) and served as magistrate of Baojing County in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 繼庚少有志節，補諸生，幕遊湖南。

translations.literal: Jigeng from youth had lofty resolve; he became a licentiate and traveled to Hunan as a secretary in someone's staff.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jigeng was a man of firm principle; he qualified as a licentiate and went to Hunan to serve on a magistrate's staff.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，從布政使潘鐸守長沙。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he followed Provincial Administration Commissioner Pan Duo in defending Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng (1853) he joined Provincial Administration Commissioner Pan Duo in the defense of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 圍既解，料賊必東竄，辭歸省母。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, he judged that the rebels would surely flee eastward, took leave, and returned home to visit his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege was raised, he judged that the rebels would drive eastward, resigned his post, and went home to see his mother.

sentences.zh: 江寧布政使祁宿藻方籌守禦，稔其才，招與謀。

translations.literal: The Jiangning Provincial Administration Commissioner Qi Suzao was then planning defenses; knowing his talent, he recruited him to counsel together.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Suzao, provincial administration commissioner of Jiangning, was then organizing the city's defenses; impressed by Jigeng's ability, he brought him in to plan with him.

sentences.zh: 繼庚慮兵不足，增募壯勇，舉諸生李翼棠等統之。

translations.literal: Jigeng, fearing troops were insufficient, additionally recruited stalwart braves and put the licentiate Li Yitang and others in command of them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the garrison was too weak, Jigeng raised more militia and placed the licentiate Li Yitang and others in command.

sentences.zh: 明年，賊至，請仿古火城法，於城內開壕積薪，城上築兩牆，為孔以出火器。

translations.literal: The next year, when rebels arrived, he requested to follow the ancient fire-city method: inside the city dig trenches and pile firewood; on the wall build double parapets with holes to discharge firearms.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the rebels arrived, he proposed reviving the ancient "fire-city" tactic: trenches and fuel stores within the walls, double parapets above with embrasures for firearms.

sentences.zh: 城下兩旁設牛皮柵，伏精兵以堵賊。

translations.literal: Below the wall on both sides he set hide palisades and hid picked troops to block the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Along both flanks below the wall he erected hide palisades and stationed elite troops to intercept the enemy.

sentences.zh: 時宿藻已卒，總督不能用。

translations.literal: By then Suzao had already died, and the governor-general would not adopt the plan.
translations.idiomatic: By then Qi Suzao had died, and the governor-general would not put the plan into effect.

sentences.zh: 二月，城陷，繼庚率眾巷戰，從弟繼辛及李翼棠、侯敦詩等皆死。

translations.literal: In the second month the city fell; Jigeng led the crowd in street fighting; his younger cousin Jixin and Li Yitang, Hou Dunshi, and others all died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the city fell. Jigeng led his men in street fighting; his younger cousin Jixin, Li Yitang, Hou Dunshi, and others were all killed.

sentences.zh: 繼庚赴水不沉，旋陷賊中，為書算。

translations.literal: Jigeng threw himself into the water but did not sink; soon he fell into rebel hands and served as a bookkeeper.
translations.idiomatic: Jigeng threw himself into the water but did not drown; he was soon taken by the rebels and put to work as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 自念死誌已決，欲將有所為，乃以母託戚友，變姓名為葉芝發，陽與賊暱，盡得其虛實。

translations.literal: Reflecting that his resolve to die was already fixed yet wishing to accomplish something, he entrusted his mother to kinsmen and friends, changed his name to Ye Zhifa, pretended intimacy with the rebels, and learned all their strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: Resolved to die if he must but determined still to act, he placed his mother in the care of relatives and friends, took the alias Ye Zhifa, feigned loyalty to the rebels, and learned their dispositions in full.

sentences.zh: 會欽差大臣向榮軍至，因與諸生週葆濂、夏家銑及錢塘人金樹本謀結賊為內應，而使金和、李鈞祥、何師孟出報大營。

translations.literal: When Imperial Commissioner Xiang Rong's army arrived, he accordingly joined the licentiate Zhou Baoqian, Xia Jiayin, and the Qiantang native Jin Shuben in plotting to turn rebels into an inner response, and sent Jin He, Li Junxiang, and He Shimeng out to report to the main camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Imperial Commissioner Xiang Rong's army arrived, he joined the licentiate Zhou Baoqian, Xia Jiayin, and Jin Shuben of Qiantang in a plot for an inside rising, dispatching Jin He, Li Junxiang, and He Shimeng to carry word to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 有張沛澤者，悍賊也，同謀而中悔，首其事，家銑死之，繼庚以偽名免。

translations.literal: There was one Zhang Peize, a fierce rebel who had joined the plot but repented midway and informed on it; Jiayin died for it, while Jigeng escaped under his false name.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce rebel named Zhang Peize had joined the plot but turned informer midway; Jiayin was executed, while Jigeng survived under his assumed name.

sentences.zh: 九月，復遣人上書向榮，言：「水西門賊所不備，有船可用，太平門近紫金山，越城亦易為力，緣城賊壘皆受約束。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month he again sent men to memorialize Xiang Rong, saying: "At the Water Gate the rebels are unprepared and boats may be used; Taiping Gate lies near Purple Gold Mountain and scaling the wall there is also easy; along the wall the rebel stockades are all under agreement."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he again sent men to write Xiang Rong: "At the Water Gate the rebels are off guard and boats can be used; Taiping Gate is near Purple Gold Mountain and the wall can be taken there as well; rebel stockades around the circuit are all pledged to our plan."

sentences.zh: 既得報，益結死士​​張士義、劉隆舒、呂萬興、硃碩齡等，以待大軍。

translations.literal: Having received a reply, he further bound death-dedicated men Zhang Shiyi, Liu Longshu, Lü Wanxing, Zhu Shuoling, and others to await the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Once word came back, he rallied still more men sworn to die—Zhang Shiyi, Liu Longshu, Lü Wanxing, Zhu Shuoling, and others—to hold themselves ready for the main force.

sentences.zh: 書七上，屢約屢爽。

translations.literal: He sent seven letters; appointments were made again and again, and again and again broken.
translations.idiomatic: Seven letters went up; again and again a date was set, and again and again it was missed.

sentences.zh: 城中人情洶洶，事垂洩，繼庚泣謂其友曰：「事急矣！」

translations.literal: Sentiment in the city was turbulent; the affair was on the verge of leaking; Jigeng wept and said to his friends: "The matter is urgent!"
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread through the city and the plot was near exposure; weeping, Jigeng told his friends, "Time is running out!"

sentences.zh: 夜縋入營，痛哭自請師期，諸將皆感動。

translations.literal: By night he was lowered by rope into camp, wept bitterly, and begged in person for a day of attack; all the generals were moved.
translations.idiomatic: That night he was let down by rope into the camp, wept as he pleaded for a fixed day of assault, and moved every general present.

sentences.zh: 張國樑欲留之，繼庚不可，歸而大軍復以雨雪不果至。

translations.literal: Zhang Guoliang wished to detain him, but Jigeng would not agree; he returned, and again the great army failed to come because of rain and snow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang wanted to keep him, but Jigeng refused; he went back inside, and once more the main army failed to arrive, halted by rain and snow.

sentences.zh: 他日繼庚出，遇沛澤於途，唶曰：「此葉芝發也！」

translations.literal: Another day Jigeng went out and met Peize on the road, who exclaimed: "This is Ye Zhifa!"
translations.idiomatic: One day Jigeng went out and met Peize on the road, who cried, "There is Ye Zhifa!"

sentences.zh: 執赴賊所，施嚴刑，不為動，徐曰：「我張炳垣，書生耳，焉預他事？

translations.literal: He was seized and taken to the rebels, subjected to severe torture without flinching, and said slowly: "I am Zhang Bingyuan, a mere scholar—how would I meddle in other affairs?
translations.idiomatic: He was dragged to the rebel headquarters and tortured without yielding, then said calmly, "I am Zhang Bingyuan, only a scholar—what other business would I be in?

sentences.zh: 沛澤食鴉片，懼我發之，乃誣我耶？」

translations.literal: Peize eats opium and fears I will expose him—is this why he falsely accuses me?"
translations.idiomatic: Peize is an opium eater and fears I will expose him—is that why he frames me?"

sentences.zh: 賊搜之，信，遂殺沛澤，繼庚被縶不得出。

translations.literal: The rebels searched and believed him, then killed Peize; Jigeng was bound and could not get out.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels investigated and believed him; they executed Peize, but Jigeng was held fast and could not leave the city.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，金和等引官兵易賈人服入城，與諸生賈鍾麟等伏神策門，殺巡更賊，以斧斷木柵，毀其半，賊驚走。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, Jin He and others led government troops disguised as merchants into the city; with the licentiate Jia Zhonglin and others they lay in wait at the Divine Strategy Gate, killed the watch rebels, and with axes broke the wooden palisade, destroying half of it; the rebels fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year Jin He and others led imperial troops into the city dressed as merchants; with the licentiate Jia Zhonglin and others they ambushed at the Divine Strategy Gate, killed the night watch, and with axes smashed half the wooden palisade, sending the rebels fleeing.

sentences.zh: 亟舉砲，六品軍功田玉梅及敢死士張鴉頭先眾上城，斬守賊十餘人，援賊麕至，玉梅跳免。

translations.literal: They hurriedly raised cannon; Tian Yumei, holder of sixth-rank military merit, and the dare-to-die man Zhang Yatou scaled the wall ahead of the crowd, beheaded more than ten defending rebels; relieving rebels swarmed up; Yumei leaped down and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Cannon were fired at once; Tian Yumei, a sixth-rank military merit holder, and the daredevil Zhang Yatou climbed the wall ahead of the rest and cut down more than a dozen defenders; rebel reinforcements poured in, and Yumei leaped down and got away.

sentences.zh: 大索城中，鴉頭被獲，窮詰不得主名，乃益搒掠繼庚，楚毒備至。

translations.literal: A great search was made in the city; Yatou was captured; though pressed with questioning they could not obtain the mastermind's name; they therefore increased the flogging of Jigeng, tortures of every Chu sort being applied.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels searched the city; Yatou was taken but would not name his master under torture, so they redoubled the beating of Jigeng with every cruelty.

sentences.zh: 時廬州知府胡元煒降賊在坐，繼庚躍起謂曰：「若官江南，寧不知江南人孱弱，非老兄弟合謀，誰敢為內應者？」

translations.literal: At the time Luzhou prefect Hu Yuanwei, who had surrendered to the rebels, was present; Jigeng sprang up and said: "You were an official in Jiangnan—can you not know that Jiangnan men are weak? Without the Old Brothers plotting together, who would dare act as inside responders?"
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yuanwei, prefect of Luzhou who had defected to the rebels, was present; Jigeng leapt up and said, "You served in Jiangnan—do you not know how frail Jiangnan men are? Without the Old Brothers in on it together, who would dare rise inside the walls?"

sentences.zh: 老兄弟，賊中呼楚、粵人之悍勇者也。

translations.literal: "Old Brothers" was what rebels called the fierce and brave men of Chu and Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: "Old Brothers" was rebel slang for the fierce fighters from Hunan and Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 賊信其言，繼庚索賊官冊一一指，賊輒殺之，橫屍東門者三十四人。

translations.literal: The rebels believed his words; Jigeng demanded the rebel officer register and pointed out each one by one; the rebels at once killed them; thirty-four corpses lay across the East Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels believed him; Jigeng had the rebel roster brought and denounced man after man, and each was killed on the spot—thirty-four bodies piled at the East Gate.

sentences.zh: 賊旋悟，曰：「中汝計矣！」

translations.literal: The rebels soon understood and said: "We have fallen into your scheme!"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon saw through it and cried, "We have been taken in!"

sentences.zh: 令速殺之。

translations.literal: They ordered him killed at once.
translations.idiomatic: They ordered him killed immediately.

sentences.zh: 繼庚臨死，色不變，呼天者三，成絕命詞，有云：「拔不去眼中鐵，嘔不盡心頭血，吁嗟窮途窮，空抱烈士烈。

translations.literal: Facing death Jigeng's countenance did not change; he called to Heaven three times and composed a death poem, saying in part: "The iron in the eye cannot be pulled out; the blood in the heart cannot be vomited clean; alas, the road's end, the road's end—empty I embrace the martyr's blaze.
translations.idiomatic: As he faced death his color never changed; thrice he cried to Heaven and composed a final poem: "The iron in my eye I cannot pluck out; the blood in my heart I cannot vomit away; alas, the end of the road—only a martyr's fire held in vain.

sentences.zh: 殺賊苦無權，罵賊猶有舌。」

translations.literal: To kill rebels I bitterly lack power; to curse rebels I still have a tongue."
translations.idiomatic: Powerless to slay the rebels, I still have a tongue to curse them."

sentences.zh: 遂車裂以死。

translations.literal: He was then torn apart by chariots and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was then executed by dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈國子監典籍，建專祠，予世職。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, he was posthumously granted Recorder of the Imperial Academy, a dedicated shrine was built, and a hereditary office was awarded.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously made Recorder of the Imperial Academy; a private shrine was erected and a hereditary rank granted.

sentences.zh: 張士義，乳名鴉頭，江寧人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shiyi, milk name Yatou, was a native of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shiyi, childhood name Yatou, was a native of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 故無賴而有肝膽，能急人之急。

translations.literal: Formerly a ruffian yet possessing guts, he could hurry to others' emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: Once a street tough, he had nerve and always rushed to help others in need.

sentences.zh: 在賊中與所素狎者醉歌，若無事然。

translations.literal: Among the rebels he drank and sang with those he had long known, as if nothing were amiss.
translations.idiomatic: Inside rebel lines he drank and sang with old acquaintances as though nothing were wrong.

sentences.zh: 繼庚遣劉隆舒招之，袖短刀二授之，曰：「汝能殺賊，當以功名顯。」

translations.literal: Jigeng sent Liu Longshu to recruit him, slipped two short knives from his sleeve and gave them to him, saying: "If you can kill rebels, you should win fame and office."
translations.idiomatic: Jigeng sent Liu Longshu to win him over, drew two short knives from his sleeve, and said, "If you can kill rebels, glory and rank will be yours."

sentences.zh: 士義慨然曰：「我何人，張先生義士乃下交，誓必殺賊，富貴非所望也！」

translations.literal: Shiyi said impassionedly: "What sort of man am I that Master Zhang, a man of righteousness, should condescend to befriend me? I swear I will kill rebels—wealth and honor are not what I seek!"
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi answered fervently, "Who am I, that the righteous Master Zhang should stoop to know me? I swear I will kill rebels—riches and rank are nothing to me!"

sentences.zh: 繼庚獄急，趣士義速圖。

translations.literal: Jigeng's imprisonment was urgent; he urged Shiyi to act quickly.
translations.idiomatic: With Jigeng in prison and time short, he pressed Shiyi to move at once.

sentences.zh: 眾請於大營，遣田玉梅等八人入城助之。

translations.literal: The crowd petitioned the main camp, which dispatched Tian Yumei and seven others into the city to assist.
translations.idiomatic: His companions petitioned headquarters, which sent Tian Yumei and seven others into the city to help.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年二月二十二日夜，士義與劉隆舒、呂長興、硃碩齡等凡五十七人，乘晦登城。

translations.literal: On the night of the twenty-second day of the second month of the fourth year of Xianfeng, Shiyi with Liu Longshu, Lü Changxing, Zhu Shuoling, and others—fifty-seven in all—took advantage of darkness to scale the wall.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the twenty-second of the second month, fourth year of Xianfeng (1854), Shiyi, Liu Longshu, Lü Changxing, Zhu Shuoling, and fifty-three others climbed the wall under cover of darkness.

sentences.zh: 遇一賊手紅燈，騰身斫之，擲首城外以為信。

translations.literal: They met a rebel holding a red lantern, leaped up and struck him down, and threw his head outside the wall as a signal.
translations.idiomatic: They met a rebel carrying a red lantern, sprang upon him and cut him down, and hurled his head outside the wall as a signal.

sentences.zh: 复殺賊十餘人，而官軍終不進。

translations.literal: They again killed more than ten rebels, yet the government army in the end did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: They killed more than ten rebels besides, but the imperial troops never came forward.

sentences.zh: 乃下斬關，柵堅不可啟，擲火燒之，不燃。

translations.literal: They then went down to cut the barrier gate; the palisade was solid and could not be opened; they threw fire to burn it, but it would not ignite.
translations.idiomatic: They went down to force the gate, but the palisade would not give; they tried to burn it with torches, and it would not catch.

sentences.zh: 柵內賊起，抽矛刺之，環城賊皆起，角嗚嗚然，眾知事不濟，遂遁。

translations.literal: Rebels inside the palisade rose, drew spears and stabbed at them; rebels all around the wall rose; horns sounded woo-woo; the crowd knew the affair would not succeed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels inside the palisade rallied and thrust with spears; rebels all along the wall answered; horns blared; seeing the attempt had failed, they scattered.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊閉門大索，有沈獸醫者首之，士義等被執，窮其主使。

translations.literal: The next day the rebels closed the gates and searched widely; one Shen the veterinarian informed on them; Shiyi and the others were seized and pressed for their mastermind.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels shut the gates and searched house by house; a veterinarian surnamed Shen informed on them; Shiyi and his comrades were seized and interrogated for their leader.

sentences.zh: 士義叱曰：「欲殺​​則殺，主使不可得也！

translations.literal: Shiyi shouted: "If you want to kill, then kill—the mastermind you will not get!
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi shouted, "Kill me if you will—you will never get our leader!

sentences.zh: 天下人皆欲殺汝，獨我哉？」

translations.literal: All under Heaven wish to kill you—is it I alone?"
translations.idiomatic: Everyone under Heaven wants you dead—do you think it is only I?"

sentences.zh: 遂與隆舒、長興、碩齡俱死。

translations.literal: He then died together with Longshu, Changxing, and Shuoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died together with Longshu, Changxing, and Shuoling.

sentences.zh: 是時繼庚以諸生舉義，鄉里士慷慨相從者：夏家銑，字季質，江寧人。

translations.literal: At this time Jigeng as a licentiate raised righteousness; among township gentlemen who generously followed him: Xia Jiayin, courtesy name Jizhi, a native of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: When Jigeng as a licentiate took up the cause, among the local men who rallied to him was Xia Jiayin, courtesy name Jizhi, of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 工詩文。

translations.literal: He was skilled in poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: He was accomplished in poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 城陷，賊挾充書記，作詩罵賊，賊搜得之。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the rebels forced him to serve as secretary; he composed poems cursing the rebels, and the rebels searched them out.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell the rebels pressed him into clerical service; he wrote poems reviling them, and the rebels found the verses.

sentences.zh: 時繼庚內應事泄，賊疑家銑知其謀，拷掠無所承，不知家銑實與聞也。

translations.literal: At the time Jigeng's inner-response affair leaked; the rebels suspected Jiayin knew their plot; under torture he confessed nothing—they did not know Jiayin had in fact been privy.
translations.idiomatic: Jigeng's inside plot had just been exposed; the rebels suspected Jiayin knew of it and tortured him, but he confessed nothing, though he had in truth been in on the scheme.

sentences.zh: 賊誘之曰：「汝有父母妻子，以為質，則釋汝。」

translations.literal: The rebels tempted him, saying: "You have father, mother, wife, and children—if you give them as hostages, we will release you."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels coaxed him: "Name your parents and wife and children as hostages, and we will let you go."

sentences.zh: 家銑時昏憊，遽以母妻對。

translations.literal: Jiayin was then dazed and exhausted and hastily answered with mother and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Dazed and worn out, Jiayin blurted out his mother and wife.

sentences.zh: 賊至家，其妻蔡匿母，罵家銑曰：「汝母死且十年，何處得汝母耶？」

translations.literal: The rebels came to his home; his wife Cai hid his mother and cursed Jiayin: "Your mother has been dead these ten years—where would you get a mother?"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came to his house; his wife Cai hid his mother-in-law and reviled him: "Your mother has been dead ten years—where do you expect them to find her?"

sentences.zh: 遂與妻俱被戮死。

translations.literal: She then was killed together with his wife.
translations.idiomatic: She and his wife were both put to death.

sentences.zh: 同預翻城之舉而未死者：金和，字亞匏，上元人。

translations.literal: Those who shared in the plan to overturn the city yet did not die: Jin He, courtesy name Yapao, a native of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Others who took part in the plot to turn the city but survived included Jin He, courtesy name Yapao, of Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 性兀傲，工詩賦，好聲色。

translations.literal: By nature proud and aloof, skilled in fu poetry, fond of music and women.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and unconventional by nature, he was skilled in fu and fond of wine, women, and song.

sentences.zh: 縱酒，飲輒數斗。

translations.literal: He drank freely; each time he drank several dou.
translations.idiomatic: He drank heavily, often several dou at a sitting.

sentences.zh: 江寧失守，陷於賊，衣短後衣，與賊兵轟飲相爾汝，因廉得賊情。

translations.literal: When Jiangning was lost he fell among rebels, wore short jackets, drank boisterously with rebel soldiers calling each other familiarly, and thereby came to know rebel intelligence in detail.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangning fell he was trapped among the rebels; dressed in short jackets he caroused with rebel soldiers on familiar terms and so learned their secrets in detail.

sentences.zh: 繼庚為其妻弟，與和通謀。

translations.literal: Jigeng was his wife's younger brother; he plotted together with He.
translations.idiomatic: Jigeng was his brother-in-law, and the two conspired together.

sentences.zh: 和與賊稔，出入無所問，孑身叩向榮軍門，請以身質，家在賊中不顧也。

translations.literal: He was intimate with rebels and went in and out unquestioned; alone he knocked at Xiang Rong's camp gate and offered his own person as hostage, heedless that his family remained among rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Intimate with the rebels, he came and went unchallenged; he went alone to Xiang Rong's camp and offered himself as hostage, though his family remained inside the city.

sentences.zh: 事敗，和以質得脫。

translations.literal: When the affair failed, He escaped because of the hostage he had given.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot failed, he got out because he had given himself as surety.

sentences.zh: 有秋蟪吟館集。

translations.literal: He left the collection Autumn Cicada Chanting Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works titled Autumn Cicada Chanting Hall.

sentences.zh: 孫文川，字澂之，上元人。

translations.literal: Sun Wenchuan, courtesy name Chengzi, was a native of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wenchuan, courtesy name Chengzi, was a native of Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 敏悟，工詩賦。

translations.literal: Quick and perceptive, skilled in fu poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted, he was accomplished in fu.

sentences.zh: 洪秀全據金陵，以計奉母間道出，復入，與繼庚謀翻城應外兵。

translations.literal: When Hong Xiuquan held Jinling, by stratagem he escorted his mother out by a secret route, re-entered, and with Jigeng plotted to overturn the city in response to outside troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Xiuquan held Nanjing, he contrived to escort his mother out by a secret route, slipped back in, and with Jigeng plotted to open the city to the besieging army.

sentences.zh: 終日芒鞋手一筐如丐，奔走近賊地，不避風雪。

translations.literal: All day in straw sandals, a basket in hand like a beggar, he ran near rebel territory without avoiding wind and snow.
translations.idiomatic: All day he went in straw sandals with a basket like a beggar, running close to rebel posts through wind and snow.

sentences.zh: 得賊中曲折，具以報官軍，因是屢捷，而翻城事卒無成。

translations.literal: He obtained twists and turns within the rebels and reported them fully to government troops; thereby there were repeated victories, yet the affair of overturning the city in the end did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He learned the rebels' inner workings and reported them in full to the imperial army, which won repeated victories on his intelligence, though the rising inside the walls never succeeded.

sentences.zh: 嗣習互市案牘，知外人情偽。

translations.literal: Later he studied treaty-port case documents and knew foreigners' truth and falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Later he mastered treaty-port paperwork and came to know foreigners' ways and motives.

sentences.zh: 英人李泰國購輪舶助李鴻章戰，既乃要挾索費，不受中國進止。

translations.literal: The Englishman Lay bought steam vessels to assist Li Hongzhang in war; afterward he extorted fees and would not accept China's control.
translations.idiomatic: The Englishman Horatio Nelson Lay bought steamships to aid Li Hongzhang's campaigns, then demanded payment and refused to take orders from the Chinese government.

sentences.zh: 鴻章聞文川才，薦入都，盡發泰國陰謀，朝廷褫泰國總稅務司職，遣船回國，事得解。

translations.literal: Hongzhang heard of Wenchuan's talent, recommended him to the capital, fully exposed Lay's secret schemes; the court stripped Lay of Inspector General of Customs and sent the ships back to his country; the affair was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang, hearing of Wenchuan's ability, recommended him to the capital; he exposed Lay's whole scheme, the court dismissed Lay as Inspector General of Customs and sent the fleet home, and the crisis was settled.

sentences.zh: 以功洊擢知府。

translations.literal: For merit he was repeatedly promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was promoted step by step to prefect.

sentences.zh: 著讀雪齋集。

translations.literal: He authored the collection Reading Snow Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the collected works Reading Snow Studio.

sentences.zh: 週葆濂，字還之，江寧人。

translations.literal: Zhou Baoqian, courtesy name Huanzhi, was a native of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Baoqian, courtesy name Huanzhi, was a native of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 詩才清麗。

translations.literal: His poetic talent was clear and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was clear and refined.

sentences.zh: 陷城中，與內應事，謀洩，脫歸。

translations.literal: Trapped in the city, he joined the inner-response affair; the plot leaked and he escaped back.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped in the city, he took part in the inside plot; when it was exposed he got out alive.

sentences.zh: 選寶應訓導。

translations.literal: He was selected as director of studies at Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of studies at Baoying.

sentences.zh: 著且巢詩存。

translations.literal: He authored the surviving poems of the Temporary Nest.
translations.idiomatic: He left the poetry collection Temporary Nest.

sentences.zh: 汪汝桂，字燕山，上元人。

translations.literal: Wang Rugui, courtesy name Yanshan, was a native of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rugui, courtesy name Yanshan, was a native of Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 幼負奇力，或勸入伍及應武童試，皆不可。

translations.literal: From youth he possessed unusual strength; some urged him to join the army or take the military child examination—he would not agree to either.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he had unusual strength; people urged him to enlist or sit for the military licentiate exam, but he refused both.

sentences.zh: 初陷賊中，追者至，手批殺一賊，擲過壕而免。

translations.literal: When he first fell among rebels and pursuers arrived, with his hand he struck and killed one rebel and threw him over the moat, thereby escaping.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first trapped among the rebels and pursuers caught up, he killed one with his bare hands, hurled the body over the moat, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 田玉梅入城，汝桂與俱往還。

translations.literal: When Tian Yumei entered the city, Rugui went back and forth with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Yumei went into the city, Rugui went in and out with him.

sentences.zh: 習繪事，畫仕女尤工。

translations.literal: He studied painting and was especially skilled at painting court ladies.
translations.idiomatic: He studied painting and was especially skilled at figures of ladies.

sentences.zh: 吳復成，字蔚堂，上元人。

translations.literal: Wu Fucheng, courtesy name Weitang, was a native of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fucheng, courtesy name Weitang, was a native of Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 性慷慨，賈於粵久，咸豐初始歸。

translations.literal: By nature generous, he traded in Guangdong for a long time and first returned at the beginning of Xianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Generous by nature, he had traded in Guangdong for many years and returned home at the start of the Xianfeng reign.

sentences.zh: 賊陷金陵，與人語多不辨，惟復成解之，以是為賊所信。

translations.literal: When bandits seized Jinling, in conversing with people they mostly could not make themselves understood; only Fucheng could interpret, and for this he was trusted by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels took Nanjing, they could scarcely understand anyone they spoke with—only Wu Fucheng could interpret for them, and on that account the rebels trusted him.

sentences.zh: 因說賊設機杼，織緞匹，用匠十萬人，文弱陷賊者得以免；

translations.literal: Thereupon he persuaded the bandits to set up looms and weave silk bolts, employing a hundred thousand craftsmen; the frail and weak among those trapped by bandits were thereby spared;
translations.idiomatic: He then persuaded the rebels to establish looms and weave bolts of silk, putting a hundred thousand craftsmen to work so that the frail and weak among those trapped in the city were spared slaughter;

sentences.zh: 又說賊造船運柴薪，賊稱其能。

translations.literal: Again he persuaded the bandits to build ships to transport firewood; the bandits praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: He also persuaded them to build ships to haul firewood and fuel, and the rebels praised his resourcefulness.

sentences.zh: 婦嬰緣是遁者又六七千人。

translations.literal: Women and infants who by this means escaped numbered another six or seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to these schemes, another six or seven thousand women and children were able to escape.

sentences.zh: 既，與繼庚謀內應，事泄，奔向榮軍，不知重也。

translations.literal: Afterward he plotted internal response with Jigeng; the affair was exposed and he fled to Xiang Rong's army, not knowing the gravity of it.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Zhang Jigeng in plotting an internal rising; when the plot was exposed, he fled to Xiang Rong's camp without fully grasping how grave the danger had become.

sentences.zh: 及曾國籓欲諜賊虛實，或以復成薦，因蓄髮入賊中，得曲折以告。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan wished to spy on the bandits' strengths and weaknesses, someone recommended Fucheng; he therefore let his hair grow and entered among the bandits, learning the twists and turns and reporting them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan sought intelligence on rebel strength and dispositions, someone recommended Fucheng; he let his hair grow long again, slipped back among the rebels, learned their movements in detail, and reported them.

sentences.zh: 曾國荃圍金陵，李秀成自蘇州來援，賊掘地道出攻，復成偵得之，報國荃為備，遂大破賊。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guoquan besieged Jinling, Li Xiucheng came from Suzhou to relieve it; the bandits dug tunnels to sally out in attack. Fucheng detected this and reported to Guoquan to prepare; the bandits were thereupon greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guoquan besieged Nanjing, Li Xiucheng marched from Suzhou to relieve the city and the rebels tunneled out to attack. Fucheng discovered the plan, warned Guoquan to prepare, and the rebels were routed.

sentences.zh: 以功敘縣丞，不就，卒以賈終。

translations.literal: For merit he was registered as county assistant magistrate, but did not take office and ended as a merchant.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was nominated for the rank of county assistant magistrate, but he declined the appointment and lived out his life as a merchant.

sentences.zh: 胡恩燮，字煦齋，江寧人。

translations.literal: Hu Enshe, style Xuzhai, was a native of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Enshe, courtesy name Xuzhai, was a native of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 與繼庚謀內應，出入賊中者三十六次。

translations.literal: Plotting internal response with Jigeng, he went in and out among the bandits thirty-six times.
translations.idiomatic: Working with Zhang Jigeng on the internal rising, he entered and left rebel-held territory thirty-six times.

sentences.zh: 破衣草履，溷跡如丐。

translations.literal: Wearing tattered hemp and straw sandals, he mingled in filth like a beggar.
translations.idiomatic: Dressed in ragged hemp and straw sandals, he hid in squalor disguised as a beggar.

sentences.zh: 往往伏壕內，或潛立橋下堅冰中，屢瀕於危。

translations.literal: Often he hid in trenches, or stood stealthily beneath bridges in solid ice, repeatedly on the brink of danger.
translations.idiomatic: He often lay in ditches or stood hidden beneath bridges in the frozen ice, repeatedly close to death.

sentences.zh: 母陷賊中，以奇計脫之。

translations.literal: His mother was trapped among the bandits; by an ingenious stratagem he freed her.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was trapped among the rebels; he rescued her with an ingenious ruse.

sentences.zh: 後以功敘知府。

translations.literal: Later, for merit, he was registered as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his service, he was nominated for the rank of prefect.

sentences.zh: 田玉梅，字鼎臣，四川酉陽州人。

translations.literal: Tian Yumei, style Dingchen, was a native of Youyang Prefecture in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yumei, courtesy name Dingchen, was a native of Youyang Prefecture in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 入應事起，求敢內成者，吳復成以書抵玉梅，玉梅裹紅巾挺身從復成行。

translations.literal: When the internal-response affair arose and men were sought who dared collude within, Wu Fucheng sent a letter to Yumei; Yumei wrapped a red turban and threw himself into following Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot for an internal rising began and men were sought bold enough to act inside the walls, Wu Fucheng wrote to Tian Yumei; Yumei bound on a red turban and threw in his lot with Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 數日，出言賊情如繪，向榮乃信任之。

translations.literal: After several days, his words on bandit conditions were vivid as a painting, and Xiang Rong thereupon trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Within days his reports on rebel dispositions were as vivid as a painted map, and Xiang Rong came to trust him.

sentences.zh: 奪門既無成，明日賊殺張士義等百餘人，不得主名，則令領石達開憑帖，無者逮訊。

translations.literal: The gate-seizing having already failed, the next day the bandits killed Zhang Shiyi and more than a hundred others. Unable to obtain the mastermind's name, they ordered all to produce passes under Shi Dakai's authority; those without were seized and interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: The attempt to seize a gate had already failed; the next day the rebels executed Zhang Shiyi and more than a hundred others. Unable to learn the ringleader's name, they ordered everyone to produce passes bearing Shi Dakai's authorization—anyone without one was arrested and questioned.

sentences.zh: 復成領數百紙貽諸同志。

translations.literal: Fucheng distributed several hundred such papers to his comrades.
translations.idiomatic: Fucheng handed out several hundred of these passes to his comrades.

sentences.zh: 玉梅手一紙立通衢，發短言異，見賊往來反詰之，賊竟無知者，乃偕八人者俱出。

translations.literal: Yumei held one sheet and stood in a public thoroughfare, uttering brief, odd remarks; seeing bandits coming and going, they questioned him in turn, yet the bandits knew nothing. He then left together with eight others.
translations.idiomatic: Yumei took one pass and stood in a busy street, speaking brief, cryptic words; rebels passing by questioned him in turn, yet none caught on. He and eight companions walked out together.

sentences.zh: 後以功敘河南同知直隸州，補太康縣知縣。

translations.literal: Later, for merit, he was registered as sub-prefect of Henan in Zhili Prefecture and appointed magistrate of Taikang County.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his service, he was nominated as acting sub-prefect of Henan in Zhili Prefecture and appointed magistrate of Taikang County.

sentences.zh: 十年，英、法國聯軍犯天津，京師戒嚴，請濟師勤王，大府不許。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the allied armies of Britain and France attacked Tianjin; the capital was placed on alert, and he requested troops to relieve the throne. The provincial authorities did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the British and French allied armies attacked Tianjin and the capital was placed on alert; he asked permission to march to the emperor's relief, but the provincial authorities refused.

sentences.zh: 自帥所部至汝陽沙官橋，為捻匪所阻，憤極死戰，被戕。

translations.literal: He himself led his command to Shaguan Bridge in Ruyang, where Nian bandits blocked the way; in utmost fury he fought to the death and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He led his own troops to Shaguan Bridge in Ruyang, where Nian rebels blocked the road; fighting in a rage to the last, he was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 卹贈太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: Posthumous compensation granted him Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 諸人於是役皆冒死為之，例得附書，以竟事之本末。

translations.literal: All these men in this affair faced death recklessly; by regulation they could be recorded in the chronicle, to complete the account from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: All these men in this affair risked their lives without hesitation; by regulation they could be recorded here to bring the full story to its close.

sentences.zh: 趙振祚，字伯厚，江蘇武進人，順天宛平籍。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhenzuo, style Bohou, was a native of Wujin in Jiangsu, with household registration in Wanping, Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhenzuo, courtesy name Bohou, was a native of Wujin in Jiangsu, registered in Wanping, Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 兩遇大考皆前列，二十二年，遷詹事府贊善。

translations.literal: In both major palace examinations he ranked among the leaders; in the twenty-second year he was promoted to Junior Mentor in the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He placed at the top in both major palace examinations; in the twenty-second year he was promoted to Junior Mentor in the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，寇陷金陵，蘇、常震動，振祚上書當事，原歸本籍辦團練。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, when bandits seized Jinling and Suzhou and Changzhou were shaken, Zhenzuo submitted a memorial to the authorities, offering to return to his native place to organize local militia.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng, when rebels took Nanjing and Suzhou and Changzhou were thrown into turmoil, Zhenzuo petitioned the authorities for leave to return home and organize local defense.

sentences.zh: 奏請，報可，遂歸。

translations.literal: He memorialized and received approval, then returned.
translations.idiomatic: His request was approved and he went home.

sentences.zh: 集貲置保衛局，募兵購械，仿行保甲，人心以安。

translations.literal: He raised funds to establish a defense bureau, recruited soldiers and purchased weapons, and followed the model of the baojia system; popular sentiment settled.
translations.idiomatic: He raised funds to set up a defense bureau, recruited troops and bought arms, and organized the populace on the baojia model until the region grew calm.

sentences.zh: 常州北門瀕江，焦湖船屢出剽掠，積為民患。

translations.literal: Changzhou's north gate bordered the river; boats from Jiao Lake often came out to plunder, a long-standing affliction on the people.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou's north gate lay on the river, and boats from Jiao Lake often raided upstream—a chronic scourge on the people.

sentences.zh: 振祚乃擇要隘口岸立稽查卡房，並設水師戰艦，嚴備以待，境獲寧輯。

translations.literal: Zhenzuo therefore chose strategic passes and river mouths to erect inspection stations, and also deployed naval war junks, keeping strict readiness until the region was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzuo chose key crossings and river mouths for inspection stations and stationed armed war junks on patrol until the district was secure again.

sentences.zh: 六年，賊艎蔽江下，鎮江幾不守，避難者絡繹。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, rebel war junks covered the river southward; Zhenjiang nearly could not be held, and refugees streamed in unbroken succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year rebel fleets filled the river driving south; Zhenjiang nearly fell, and refugees poured in without cease.

sentences.zh: 振祚固結人心，訓練士卒，率眾詣丹陽，會督師者赴援，圍乃解。

translations.literal: Zhenzuo solidified popular resolve, trained soldiers, and led the crowd to Danyang, where they joined the commander in going to the relief; the siege was then lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzuo steadied public morale, drilled his troops, and led a force to Danyang to join the commander in relieving the city; the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 賞花翎，加翰林院侍讀銜。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with a peacock feather and the additional title of Hanlin Academy Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He was awarded a peacock feather and the additional Hanlin title of Reader.

sentences.zh: 時總督何桂清駐常州，郡人編修趙曾向出其門，振祚素輕之，以是常訐其短於桂清，遇事齮齕。

translations.literal: At the time Governor-General He Guiqing was stationed at Changzhou; the local compiler Zhao Zengxiang had been his student. Zhenzuo had always looked down on him and for this often denounced his faults to Guiqing, and matters went against him at every turn.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General He Guiqing was then at Changzhou; the local compiler Zhao Zengxiang had been his protégé. Zhenzuo had always held Zengxiang in contempt and often denounced him to Guiqing, so that at every turn his affairs were obstructed.

sentences.zh: 嗣曾向被命佐常州團練，益掣其肘，不得已，請解事，保衛局遂廢。

translations.literal: Later Zengxiang was ordered to assist in Changzhou militia training, which further hampered his efforts; having no recourse, he requested to be relieved of duty, and the defense bureau was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Zengxiang was later ordered to share command of Changzhou's militia, the interference grew worse; Zhenzuo had no choice but to resign, and the defense bureau was dissolved.

sentences.zh: 十年，和春軍潰丹陽，常州大警，桂清宵遁，曾向亦舉室渡江而北，於是紳民復請振祚出督團勇。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, He Chun's army was routed at Danyang and Changzhou was greatly alarmed; Guiqing fled by night, and Zengxiang moved his whole household north across the river. The gentry and people thereupon again invited Zhenzuo to command the militia.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year He Chun's army was shattered at Danyang and panic seized Changzhou; Guiqing fled by night and Zengxiang moved his entire family north across the Yangtze. The local gentry and populace again begged Zhenzuo to take command of the militia.

sentences.zh: 是時兵單糧絕，寇氛日迫，事已不可為，复毅然誓眾固守，並率所練五十人出城招集潰勇。

translations.literal: At this time troops were few, grain exhausted, and the enemy pressed daily nearer; the situation was already beyond saving. Yet he again took a solemn oath before the people to hold firm, and led his trained fifty men out of the city to gather scattered fugitives from defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were few, supplies gone, and the enemy closed in day by day—the city was already beyond saving. Even so he swore before the people to hold on and led his fifty trained men outside the walls to rally scattered fugitives from the rout.

sentences.zh: 會北鄉石堰土盜蜂起，遂領眾往捕，以眾寡不敵，戰失利，力竭，死之。

translations.literal: When bandits rose like bees in Shiyan in the northern countryside, he led his force to capture them; outnumbered, the fight went badly, his strength gave out, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits swarmed at Shiyan in the northern countryside, he led his men to suppress them; outnumbered, his force was beaten, his strength failed, and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 常州亦旋陷。

translations.literal: Changzhou fell soon after.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou fell soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈太僕寺卿，予世職。

translations.literal: When word came, he was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Imperial Stud with a hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: When the news reached court, he was posthumously made Grand Master of the Imperial Stud and granted a hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，李鴻章疏稱：「其六世祖尚書趙申喬為康熙時名臣，子姓分居蘇、常。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi, Li Hongzhang memorialized: "His sixth-generation ancestor, Minister Zhao Shenqiao, was a renowned minister of the Kangxi reign; descendants were scattered through Suzhou and Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongzhi, Li Hongzhang memorialized: "His sixth-generation ancestor, Minister Zhao Shenqiao, was a celebrated statesman of the Kangxi era; the clan's branches were scattered through Suzhou and Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 江、​​浙淪陷，男女死者四十三人，其弟浙江經歷振禋亦死於難。」

translations.literal: When Jiangsu and Zhejiang fell, forty-three men and women of the clan died; his younger brother Zhentun, a bureau clerk in Zhejiang, also died in the calamity."
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangsu and Zhejiang were overrun, forty-three men and women of the family perished; his younger brother Zhentun, a bureau clerk in Zhejiang, also died in the disaster."

sentences.zh: 得旨，予振祚常州建祠，餘附祀。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript granted Zhenzuo a temple in Changzhou, with the rest enshrined there in affiliation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered a temple built for Zhenzuo in Changzhou, with the others enshrined there as associated spirits.

sentences.zh: 振祚忼爽重節介，口素吃，遇不平事，憤懣謾罵，期期不避人，故多遭怨。

translations.literal: Zhenzuo was forthright and prized integrity, had a stammer, and when he encountered injustice would burst into angry curses, stammering without avoiding others; therefore he incurred much resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzuo was blunt and high-minded, with a stammer; when he met injustice he would burst into furious curses, stammering in public without restraint, and so made many enemies.

sentences.zh: 然好獎借人才，人亦以此多之。

translations.literal: Yet he delighted in commending talent, and people for this reason also esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved to praise able men, and for that people also held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 善詩、古文詞，精漢學，著有明堂考一卷，文、詩集若干卷。

translations.literal: Skilled in poetry and ancient-style prose, precise in Han learning, he authored one fascicle of Investigations of the Bright Hall and several fascicles of literary and poetic collections.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at poetry and ancient-style prose and was a fine scholar of Han learning; his works included one fascicle of Investigations of the Bright Hall and several fascicles of essays and poems.

sentences.zh: 同族起，道光舉人。

translations.literal: [Zhao] Qi of the same clan passed the provincial examination in the Daoguang reign.
translations.idiomatic: A clansman, Zhao Qi, passed the provincial examination in the Daoguang reign.

sentences.zh: 同時城守。

translations.literal: At the same time he helped defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: He defended the city alongside Zhenzuo.

sentences.zh: 城陷，命合室婦女自沉園池，遂整衣冠坐廳事。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he ordered the women of the household to drown themselves in the garden pool, then straightened his robes and cap and sat in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he ordered the women of his household to drown themselves in the garden pool, then straightened his robes and cap and seated himself in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 賊至，有識起者，勸令自全，大聲叱賊，引刀自剄。

translations.literal: When rebels arrived, some who recognized Qi urged him to save himself; he loudly berated the rebels, drew a blade, and cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels arrived, some who knew him urged him to save himself; he shouted curses at them, drew a blade, and cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 子諸生曾寅以身衛父，刃賊數人，被害。

translations.literal: His son, licentiate Zengyin, shielded his father with his body, cut down several rebels, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: His son, the licentiate Zengyin, shielded his father with his body, killed several rebels, and was slain.

sentences.zh: 兄子浙江候補知縣祿保，罵賊，死尤烈。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Lubao, an expectant magistrate in Zhejiang, cursed the rebels and died with especial fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother's son Lubao, an expectant magistrate in Zhejiang, cursed the rebels and died with especial ferocity.

sentences.zh: 馬善，字遇皋，長洲人，世居蘇垣北鄉。

translations.literal: Ma Shan, style Yugao, was a native of Changzhou; his family had long lived in the northern countryside of the Suzhou quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shan, courtesy name Yugao, was from Changzhou; his family had long lived in the northern countryside outside Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 有智略，膂力過人。

translations.literal: He had stratagem and courage, and his physical strength surpassed ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: He was resourceful and brave, with strength beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年閏三月，金陵大營潰，總督遁，賊席捲而南。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month of the tenth year of Xianfeng, the great camp at Jinling collapsed, the governor-general fled, and bandits swept southward.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month of the tenth year of Xianfeng the great camp at Nanjing collapsed, the governor-general fled, and the rebels rolled south.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丁丑，蘇州陷。

translations.literal: On dingchou day in the fourth month of summer, Suzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day in the fourth month of summer, Suzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 善先受檄主黃土橋團練，集七圖義勇三千人，朝夕訓練，庀水陸戰守具。

translations.literal: Shan had first received orders to command militia at Huangtu Bridge; he gathered three thousand volunteers from seven tu, drilling them morning and evening and preparing equipment for battle on land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Shan had already been ordered to command militia at Huangtu Bridge; he mustered three thousand volunteers from seven districts, drilling them day and night and equipping them for war on land and water.

sentences.zh: 聞變，嚴陣以待。

translations.literal: On hearing of the disaster, he drew up in battle array to await them.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard what had happened, he formed battle lines and waited.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊果至，迎擊金巷橋。

translations.literal: The next day the bandits indeed came; he met them in battle at Jinxian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels came as expected; he met them at Jinxian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 又明日，賊大掠八字橋，又趣援之。

translations.literal: The next day again the bandits plundered heavily at Bazigiao Bridge, and he hastened again to their relief.
translations.idiomatic: The day after, the rebels looted heavily at Bazigiao Bridge, and he hurried there again to drive them off.

sentences.zh: 越四日，賊分兩路至，一出齊門至宜橋，一出閶門至禪定橋。

translations.literal: After four days the bandits came in two columns—one from Qi Gate to Yi Bridge, one from Chang Gate to Chanding Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Four days later the rebels advanced in two columns—one from Qi Gate toward Yi Bridge, one from Chang Gate toward Chanding Bridge.

sentences.zh: 善率勇千人自當宜橋，遣子安瀾率勇數百當禪定橋，先後均有斬獲。

translations.literal: Shan led a thousand braves himself to face Yi Bridge and sent his son Anlan to lead several hundred braves against Chanding Bridge; at both places they cut heads and took captives.
translations.idiomatic: Shan led a thousand militiamen himself at Yi Bridge and sent his son Anlan with several hundred to hold Chanding Bridge; at both places they killed rebels and took prisoners.

sentences.zh: 賊將竄常熟，夜遣安瀾率千人潛至八字橋，盡括岸側灰窯遺棄磚瓦塞遠近橋下，居民已空，無知者。

translations.literal: When the bandits were about to flee toward Changshu, at night he sent Anlan with a thousand men stealthily to Bazigiao Bridge and swept up all discarded bricks and tiles from ash kilns along the banks to block bridges far and near. The residents had already fled and none knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were about to slip toward Changshu, he sent Anlan at night with a thousand men to Bazigiao Bridge to gather discarded bricks and tiles from riverside lime kilns and choke the bridges for miles around. The inhabitants had already fled, and no one knew what they were doing.

sentences.zh: 越數日，賊船至，不得過。

translations.literal: After several days rebel boats arrived and could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Days later rebel boats arrived and could not get through.

sentences.zh: 城賊約滸關至青黛湖，合宜橋、禪定橋三路並進，善分兵拒之，而自擊青黛湖，失利，賊旋退。

translations.literal: City rebels arranged from Hukou Pass to Qingdai Lake to combine three routes from Yi Bridge and Chanding Bridge and advance together. Shan divided his troops to resist them and himself struck Qingdai Lake; he was defeated, but the bandits soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels inside the city planned a joint advance from Hukou Pass to Qingdai Lake along three roads through Yi Bridge and Chanding Bridge. Shan split his force to meet them and personally attacked at Qingdai Lake; he was beaten back, but the rebels soon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 已而賊大至，善設伏青黛湖畔，遣弟增及安瀾誘賊入湖，伏發勝之，獲賊船十，俘賊首攀大福，梟其首，賊為奪氣。

translations.literal: Before long bandits came in force. Shan set an ambush on the shore of Qingdai Lake and sent his younger brother Zeng and Anlan to lure the enemy into the lake. When the ambush was sprung they were victorious; they seized ten rebel boats, captured the rebel chieftain Pan Dafu, displayed his head, and the bandits' spirit was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels came in strength. Shan laid an ambush on the shore of Qingdai Lake and sent his brother Zeng and Anlan to bait the enemy into the lake; when the trap closed they won a great victory, seized ten rebel boats, captured the chieftain Pan Dafu, and displayed his head until rebel morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 偽忠王李秀成憤不得逞，大舉來攻，善盡銳御之，自辰至午，殺傷相當。

translations.literal: The false Loyal King Li Xiucheng, furious that he could not prevail, launched a major attack. Shan mustered his elite to withstand them; from the hour of chen until wu, killings and wounds were about equal.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiping Loyal King Li Xiucheng, enraged at his failure, launched a major assault. Shan threw in every able fighter; from mid-morning until noon the killing was even on both sides.

sentences.zh: 賊退，團勇歸局午食，賊遽掩至，善率親兵迎戰，手刃騎馬賊三人，傷於胸，猶疾呼殺賊，飛鏃中頭角而踣。

translations.literal: The bandits withdrew; the militia returned to the station for the midday meal, and the bandits suddenly fell upon them. Shan led his personal guard to meet the fight, himself cutting down three mounted bandits. Wounded in the chest, he still shouted urgently to kill bandits; a flying bolt struck his temple and he fell.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pulled back; the militia returned to camp for the midday meal when the enemy suddenly rushed them. Shan led his bodyguard into the fight and personally cut down three mounted rebels. Wounded in the chest, he still roared for his men to kill the enemy until a flying bolt struck his temple and he fell.

sentences.zh: 安瀾方赴常熟請軍火，馳歸斂之，面色如生。

translations.literal: Anlan had gone to Changshu for munitions; he raced back to lay out the body, whose complexion was as in life.
translations.idiomatic: Anlan had gone to Changshu for munitions; he galloped back to recover the body, which looked as though he were still alive.

sentences.zh: 當是時詔舉團練，吳人脆弱，賊至則靡，獨善以能殺賊聞。

translations.literal: At that time an edict called for raising local militia; the people of Wu were frail—when bandits came they scattered—yet Shan alone was known for being able to kill bandits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had gone out calling for local militia, yet the people of Wu were soft—when rebels came they fled—while Shan alone was famed for standing his ground and killing rebels.

sentences.zh: 卹贈知州銜，給世職。

translations.literal: Posthumous compensation granted him the rank of prefect and a hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of prefect and a hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 安瀾後從巡撫李鴻章軍，鄉導得力，卒復甦州。

translations.literal: Anlan later followed Governor Li Hongzhang's army, serving ably as a local guide, and in the end recovered Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Anlan later served under Governor Li Hongzhang as a trusted local guide and took part in the recovery of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 陳克家，字子剛，元和人。

translations.literal: Chen Kejia, style Zigang, was a native of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kejia, courtesy name Zigang, was a native of Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 道光二十四年舉人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 少英異，為桐城姚瑩所器重。

translations.literal: From youth he was outstanding; Yao Ying of Tongcheng prized him highly.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed exceptional talent, and Yao Ying of Tongcheng held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 抗心希古，落落寡合。

translations.literal: Upright in heart and aspiring to antiquity, aloof and little inclined to company.
translations.idiomatic: Upright in spirit and drawn to antiquity, he stood apart and kept few companions.

sentences.zh: 文章自許北宋，儷體宗六朝，詩學黃庭堅。

translations.literal: In prose he claimed the Northern Song for himself; in parallel prose he took the Six Dynasties as his model; in poetry he studied Huang Tingjian.
translations.idiomatic: In prose he modeled himself on the Northern Song; in parallel prose he looked to the Six Dynasties; in poetry he followed Huang Tingjian.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，挑教職。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he was selected for the teaching service.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng he was selected for an educational post.

sentences.zh: 時金陵為賊據，欽差大臣向榮駐師城外，翼長福興阿聘克家入幕。

translations.literal: At the time Jinling was held by bandits; Imperial Commissioner Xiang Rong's army was stationed outside the city, and Wing Commander Fuxing'a engaged Kejia for his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing was then in rebel hands; Imperial Commissioner Xiang Rong's army lay outside the walls, and the wing commander Fuxing'a took Kejia onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 福遷去，江南提督張國樑复聘之。

translations.literal: When Fu was transferred away, Jiangnan Military Governor Zhang Guoliang again engaged him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuxing'a was transferred, Jiangnan Military Governor Zhang Guoliang engaged him in turn.

sentences.zh: 十年閏三月，國樑檄克家主健勇營事，十五日，賊大至，督弁勇迎戰，兵敗死之。

translations.literal: Intercalary third month, tenth year: Guoliang ordered Kejia to oversee affairs of the Valiant Braves camp. On the fifteenth day bandits came in force; supervising officers and soldiers met them in battle; the army was defeated and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month of the tenth year Guoliang put him in charge of the Valiant Braves camp; on the fifteenth day the rebels attacked in force, officers and men met them in battle, the line broke, and Kejia was killed.

sentences.zh: 克家之死也，營中大亂，求屍不得。

translations.literal: At Kejia's death the camp fell into great disorder, and his corpse could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: When Kejia fell the camp collapsed in chaos and his body could not be recovered.

sentences.zh: 克家祖鶴，熟精明代事，為明紀一書，用通鑑義法，崇禎三年後猶闕，克家續成之，合為十六卷。

translations.literal: Kejia's grandfather He was thoroughly versed in Ming history and wrote a book on the dynasty using the method of the Comprehensive Mirror; after the third year of Chongzhen it was still incomplete, and Kejia finished it, making sixteen fascicles in all.
translations.idiomatic: Kejia's grandfather He was a deep student of Ming history and had begun a dynastic chronicle in the style of the Comprehensive Mirror; the portion after the third year of Chongzhen was still unfinished, and Kejia completed it for a total of sixteen fascicles.

sentences.zh: 馬釗，字遠林，長洲人。

translations.literal: Ma Zhao, style Yuanlin, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhao, courtesy name Yuanlin, was a native of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 與克家同歲舉人。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in the same year as Kejia.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the same year as Kejia.

sentences.zh: 治經學有名。

translations.literal: Renowned for studying the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed for his classical scholarship.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，前江蘇巡撫許乃釗副向榮統兵金陵，釗入許營時，有川、楚兵所帶餘丁，率驍勇，而蘇垣空虛，釗建議募為一軍，得千餘人，號曰撫勇。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, former Jiangsu Governor Xu Naiding served as deputy to Xiang Rong in commanding troops at Jinling. When Zhao entered Xu's camp, there were surplus soldiers among the Sichuan and Huguang troops—mostly bold fighters—and as the Suzhou quarter lay empty, Zhao proposed recruiting them as a single army; more than a thousand were obtained, titled the Pacifying Braves.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng the former Jiangsu governor Xu Naiding served as Xiang Rong's deputy at Nanjing. When Zhao joined Xu's command, he found spare men among the Sichuan and Huguang contingents—seasoned fighters—and with Suzhou undefended proposed recruiting them as one corps; more than a thousand were mustered under the name Pacifying Braves.

sentences.zh: 粵匪劉麗川反嘉定，土匪周立春繼之，連陷青浦等六縣。

translations.literal: Cantonese rebels Liu Lichuan rose at Jiading; local bandits led by Zhou Lichun followed; together they seized six counties including Qingpu.
translations.idiomatic: The Cantonese rebels under Liu Lichuan rose at Jiading; local bandits under Zhou Lichun followed, and together they overran six counties including Qingpu.

sentences.zh: 向榮檄釗率撫勇卷甲赴之，至青浦，夜半，銜枚薄城，克之，獎內閣中書銜。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong ordered Zhao to lead the Pacifying Braves in full armor to the scene. Reaching Qingpu at midnight, they took the city with muffled advance; he was rewarded with the nominal title of Vice Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong ordered Zhao to march the Pacifying Braves to the scene in full kit. They reached Qingpu at midnight, stormed the city in silence, and Zhao was rewarded with the nominal title of Vice Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 事定，重赴金陵。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he returned again to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis was over he returned to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 十年春，浙江告急，偕總兵熊天喜赴援，复四安鎮、廣德州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year Zhejiang reported emergency; together with commander Xiong Tianxi he went to the relief and recovered Sian Town and Guangde Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year Zhejiang called for aid; he marched with Commander Xiong Tianxi, recovered Sian Town and Guangde Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 奉調馳回，遇賊丹陽，戰白塔灣，中槍死。

translations.literal: On orders he galloped back, encountered bandits at Danyang, fought at Baitawan, was shot, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled in haste, he met rebels at Danyang, fought at Baitawan, was shot, and died.

sentences.zh: 二人以文士從軍，卒死於陣，吳人稱之。

translations.literal: The two men, literary scholars who took up arms, died in battle in the end; the people of Wu spoke of them.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were scholars who took up arms and died in battle; the people of Wu still speak of them.

sentences.zh: 臧紓青，字牧菴，江蘇宿遷人。

translations.literal: Zang Shuqing, style Mu'an, was a native of Suqian in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Shuqing, courtesy name Mu'an, was a native of Suqian in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光十一年舉人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Daoguang he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Daoguang reign he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 自少倜儻好談兵，所交多不羈之士。

translations.literal: From youth he was free and bold, fond of discussing military affairs; those he associated with were mostly unrestrained men.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was bold and unconventional, loved to talk of war, and kept company mostly with rough, free-spirited men.

sentences.zh: 當英吉利入寇，紓青見武備廢弛，人不知兵，寇至多被殘害，因團練鄉兵，凡萬人。

translations.literal: When England invaded, Shuqing saw that military preparations had fallen into ruin and people did not understand warfare; when the invaders came many were cruelly harmed. He therefore organized local militia, ten thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Britain invaded, Shuqing saw how neglected the defenses were and how little the people knew of war; when the enemy came many were slaughtered. He therefore raised a local militia of ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 嗣入靖逆將軍幕府，將軍主和，紓青獨主戰，後以和議成，奏獎同知銜，不受，曰：「以和受賞，不亦恥乎？」

translations.literal: Thereafter he entered the staff of the Pacification General; the general favored peace, while Shuqing alone favored war. Later, when peace negotiations succeeded, a memorial recommended awarding him the nominal rank of subprefect; he refused, saying: "To accept reward for making peace—is that not shameful?"
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the Pacification General's staff. The general favored peace; Shuqing alone pressed for war. When peace was concluded, a memorial recommended him for the nominal rank of subprefect, but he refused, saying, "To take reward for peace—would that not be shameful?"

sentences.zh: 嘗以邳州知州勒捐案被牽涉，查辦大臣週天爵雪之。

translations.literal: He was once implicated in the Peizhou magistrate's coerced-donation case; investigating Commissioner Zhou Tianjue cleared him.
translations.idiomatic: He was once drawn into the Peizhou magistrate's forced-donation scandal; the investigating commissioner Zhou Tianjue exonerated him.

sentences.zh: 時粵逆陷安慶，據江寧，淮南北捻匪乘釁為亂，聚黨多者至數千人，與粵逆互為聲勢。

translations.literal: At that time the Taiping rebels had taken Anqing and held Jiangning; Nian bandits north and south of the Huai seized the opportunity to rise in revolt, bands of several thousand at most, and they reinforced each other with the Taiping rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiping rebels had then taken Anqing and held Nanjing; Nian bandits north and south of the Huai seized the moment to revolt, some bands numbering thousands, and they bolstered one another with the Taiping forces.

sentences.zh: 天爵因疏請紓青練勇剿匪，且聽自成一隊。

translations.literal: Tianjue accordingly memorialized asking that Shuqing train braves to suppress bandits and be allowed to command a separate detachment.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjue memorialized asking that Shuqing drill militia to suppress the bandits and be permitted to command his own column.

sentences.zh: 匪素懾紓青威名，稱之曰「老虎兵」。

translations.literal: Bandits had long feared Shuqing's reputation and called his troops "Tiger Soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: The bandits had long feared Shuqing's name and called his men the Tiger Troops.

sentences.zh: 所至撲滅解散，多原歸附效死者。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he stamped them out or dispersed them; many willingly submitted and were ready to die in his service.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he marched he crushed or dispersed them; many came over willingly and were ready to die for him.

sentences.zh: 天爵卒，副都御史袁甲三繼任，亦深倚之。

translations.literal: When Tianjue died, Vice Censor-in-chief Yuan Jiasan succeeded him and also relied on him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianjue died, Vice Censor-in-chief Yuan Jiasan took his post and leaned on him just as heavily.

sentences.zh: 累擢通判，賞四品銜。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to deputy prefect and awarded fourth-rank nominal status.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to deputy prefect and granted fourth-rank nominal rank.

sentences.zh: 先是桐城以三年十月失陷，士民先後乞援於圍廬州提督和春、圍舒城提督秦定三，幾一年，皆不應。

translations.literal: Earlier Tongcheng had fallen in the tenth month of the third year; gentry and people repeatedly begged aid from Commissioner He Chun, besieging Luzhou, and Commissioner Qin Dingsan, besieging Shucheng—for nearly a year neither responded.
translations.idiomatic: Tongcheng had fallen in the tenth month of the third year; for nearly a year its gentry and commoners pleaded in turn to Commissioner He Chun at the siege of Luzhou and Commissioner Qin Dingsan at the siege of Shucheng, and neither answered.

sentences.zh: 甲三時駐兵臨淮，念桐人請救之殷，又欲取安慶以截江路，自請進剿。

translations.literal: Jiasan was then stationed at Linhuai; mindful of the Tong people's earnest pleas and wishing to take Anqing and cut the river route, he asked to advance in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Jiasan was then encamped at Linhuai. Mindful of how urgently Tong had called for help, and wishing to seize Anqing and sever the river line, he volunteered to advance in suppression.

sentences.zh: 文宗以臨淮扼南北之要，不許。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong, holding that Linhuai commanded the vital passage between north and south, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong held that Linhuai guarded the vital link between north and south and would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 甲三於是疏請檄紓青剿辦，允之。

translations.literal: Jiasan then memorialized asking that an order be sent to Shuqing to undertake suppression, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Jiasan then memorialized asking that orders go to Shuqing to conduct the suppression, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 時侍郎曾國籓已克復武昌，破田家鎮，順流東下，使提督塔齊布、道員羅澤南進攻廣濟、黃梅。

translations.literal: By then Vice-President Zeng Guofan had recovered Wuchang, broken Tianjiazhen, and was marching east downriver, sending Commander Taqibu and Intendant Luo Zenan to attack Guangji and Huangmei.
translations.idiomatic: By then Vice-President Zeng Guofan had retaken Wuchang, smashed Tianjiazhen, and was driving east down the Yangtze, sending Commander Taqibu and Intendant Luo Zenan against Guangji and Huangmei.

sentences.zh: 朝廷既允甲三請，復以國籓兵屢捷，於是命紓青速進兵潛、太接應。

translations.literal: The court having approved Jiasan's request, and moreover because Zeng Guofan's army had won repeated victories, it ordered Shuqing to advance swiftly into Qian and Tai to link up.
translations.idiomatic: The court having granted Jiasan's request, and with Zeng Guofan's army winning victory after victory, it ordered Shuqing to hurry into Qianshan and Taihu to make contact.

sentences.zh: 時和春、秦定三軍皆久無功，詔旨切責​​，令速破賊以圖會剿。

translations.literal: At that time the armies of He Chun and Qin Dingsan had long been without success; the imperial edict sternly reproached them and ordered them to break the rebels quickly for a joint campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun's and Qin Dingsan's armies had then long gone without success; an edict sharply rebuked them and ordered them to rout the rebels at once for a combined campaign.

sentences.zh: 紓青又得國籓書相期會，於是疾馳至桐，兩敗賊於大關、呂亭驛，追至城下，時四年十一月六日也。

translations.literal: Shuqing also received Zeng Guofan's letter arranging a rendezvous; he therefore galloped to Tong, twice defeated rebels at Daguan and Lüting Post, pursued to the wall—this was the sixth day of the eleventh month of the fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: Shuqing also had Zeng Guofan's letter fixing a rendezvous; he galloped to Tong, twice routed the rebels at Daguan and Lüting Post, and chased them to the walls—on the sixth day of the eleventh month of the fourth year.

sentences.zh: 紓青以舒、廬圍師率離城十餘裡，不斷賊出入餉道，以故久無功。

translations.literal: Shuqing saw that the besieging forces at Shu and Lu camped more than ten li from the cities and did not cut the rebels' supply routes; hence they had long been fruitless.
translations.idiomatic: Shuqing saw that the armies investing Shucheng and Luzhou kept camp more than ten li from the walls and never severed the rebels' supply lines—hence their long stalemate.

sentences.zh: 桐之南門通安慶，賊來援則當其衝，遂自率兵勇圍之，而令參將劉玉豹、同知李安中圍東門。

translations.literal: Tong's south gate opened toward Anqing; when rebels came to relieve the siege they would strike that point. He therefore personally led braves to invest it and ordered Brigade-General Liu Yubao and Subprefect Li Anzhong to invest the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's south gate faced Anqing; rebel relief would have to meet that thrust. He took the braves himself to invest it and set Brigade-General Liu Yubao and Subprefect Li Anzhong on the east gate.

sentences.zh: 時攻城之器未具，城堅不可猝拔。

translations.literal: At the time siege engines were not ready; the walls were strong and could not be taken in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Siege engines were not yet in place; the walls were stout and could not be carried in a rush.

sentences.zh: 賊既敗於湖北，又懼桐城或破，則與湘軍成夾擊勢，悉力來援。

translations.literal: The rebels, defeated in Hubei, also feared that if Tongcheng fell they would be caught in a pincer with the Hunan Army, and threw all their strength into relief.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated in Hubei, the rebels also feared that if Tongcheng fell they would be caught between two fires by the Hunan Army, and threw everything into relief.

sentences.zh: 紓青先後迎擊於王林莊、掛車河，皆勝之，追至陶衝驛，擒斬既多，獲械無算。

translations.literal: Shuqing met them in succession at Wanglin Village and Guache River, winning both times; pursuing to Taochong Post he captured and slew many and took arms beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Shuqing met them in turn at Wanglin Village and Guache River and won both fights; chasing to Taochong Post he killed and captured a great host and took arms beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 卒以舒、廬軍不予接應，又不急攻城以分賊勢，賊用是得專事援桐。

translations.literal: In the end, because the Shu and Lu armies gave no support and did not press the siege to divide rebel strength, the rebels were thus able to devote themselves wholly to relieving Tong.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the Shu and Lu armies neither supported him nor pressed their sieges to split rebel strength, so the rebels could throw their whole weight into saving Tong.

sentences.zh: 玉豹、安中又性懦，無能當賊，紓青至以「諸君不能戰，不能攻，又不能守，事事須我一人」誚之，弗卹也。

translations.literal: Yubao and Anzhong were moreover timid by nature and could not face the rebels; Shuqing went so far as to mock them: "You gentlemen cannot fight, cannot assault, and cannot defend—everything falls on me alone"—yet they took no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Yubao and Anzhong were timid besides and could not stand against the rebels; Shuqing even mocked them—"You cannot fight, cannot storm, cannot hold—everything rests on me alone"—but they paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 十七日，賊援大至，玉豹、安中卻走，城賊复突出西門焚營。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day rebel reinforcements came in force; Yubao and Anzhong fell back, and rebels in the city burst from the west gate and burned the camp.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth rebel relief arrived in strength; Yubao and Anzhong pulled back, and rebels in the city sallied from the west gate and burned the camp.

sentences.zh: 紓青與諸生張勛殊死戰，殺三百餘賊，以後無繼者，賊伏遽起，紓青胸面間中二十餘創，死焉。

translations.literal: Shuqing and the licentiate Zhang Xun fought to the death, slaying more than three hundred rebels; when no one followed up, rebels lying in ambush suddenly rose; Shuqing received more than twenty wounds on chest and face and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shuqing and the licentiate Zhang Xun fought to the death and killed more than three hundred rebels; when no one came up behind them, men in ambush sprang up; Shuqing took more than twenty wounds to chest and face and fell.

sentences.zh: 紓青既死，賊復得志，武昌再陷。

translations.literal: After Shuqing's death the rebels again had their way, and Wuchang fell once more.
translations.idiomatic: With Shuqing dead the rebels had their way again, and Wuchang fell a second time.

sentences.zh: 紓青治兵有紀律，初，賊以土匪目官兵以惑民聽，至是一洗此恥。

translations.literal: Shuqing governed troops with discipline; at first the rebels had called the government troops "bandit soldiers" to mislead the people, but by this he washed away that shame.
translations.idiomatic: Shuqing kept strict discipline among his men; at first the rebels had smeared the imperial troops as bandit soldiers to turn the people, but he washed away that stain.

sentences.zh: 桐城破後，凡先以助餉團練，賊皆甘心焉。

translations.literal: After Tongcheng fell, all who had earlier aided funds or led militia—the rebels bore them bitter grudges.
translations.idiomatic: After Tongcheng fell, the rebels nursed a settled hatred for everyone who had helped fund or train the militia.

sentences.zh: 民以紓青來，秋毫無犯，雖被禍，無不感泣思之。

translations.literal: When the people saw Shuqing come, not a hair was harmed; though they suffered disaster, none failed to weep and remember him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuqing came the people were not harmed in the least; though disaster struck, none failed to weep for him and keep him in mind.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜三品卿銜，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, he was granted third-rank chamberlain status and the hereditary office of Chief Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne he was granted third-rank chamberlain rank and the hereditary office of Chief Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後有竇元灝。

translations.literal: Later there was Dou Yuanhao.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Dou Yuanhao.

sentences.zh: 元灝，邳州人，咸豐元年舉人，援例為員外郎，分刑部。

translations.literal: Yuanhao, a native of Peizhou, provincial graduate in the first year of Xianfeng, entered office by purchase as a department secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao was a native of Peizhou, a provincial graduate of the first year of Xianfeng, who bought office as an outer secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 八年，捻賊大熾，竄徐州，邳當其衝，元灝集鄉團，先後偕知州畢培貞、周力城，都司濮楓等堵剿，擊斬甚多。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Nian bandits grew very strong, raided Xuzhou; Peizhou lay in their path; Yuanhao gathered local militia and, with Magistrate Bi Peizhen, Zhou Licheng, Garrison Commander Pu Feng, and others, blocked and suppressed them in succession, killing many.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Nian bandits flared up and swept into Xuzhou; Peizhou lay in their path. Yuanhao raised local militia and, with Magistrate Bi Peizhen, Zhou Licheng, Garrison Commander Pu Feng, and others, blocked and hunted them in turn, killing a great many.

sentences.zh: 十年，州城被圍，守禦四晝夜，城賴以全。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the prefectural city was besieged; he defended four days and four nights, and the city was preserved intact.
