translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the prefectural seat was besieged; he held it four days and four nights, and the city stood.

sentences.zh: 賊結幅匪大舉，由蘭、郯渡河，元灝與參將於殿甲合剿，被圍，力竭死。

translations.literal: Rebels joined allied bandit hosts in a major advance, crossing the river from Lan and Tan; Yuanhao joined Brigade-General Yu Dianjia in joint suppression, was surrounded, and died when his strength was spent.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels allied with bandit hosts in a great rising and crossed the river from Lan and Tan; Yuanhao and Brigade-General Yu Dianjia fought them together, were surrounded, and he died when his strength gave out.

sentences.zh: 贈太僕寺卿銜，賞世職。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Court of Imperial Stud nominal rank and a hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given Grand Master of the Court of the Imperial Stud nominal rank and a hereditary commission.

sentences.zh: 馬三俊，字命之，​​桐城人。

translations.literal: Ma Sanjun, style Mingzhi, was a native of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sanjun, courtesy name Mingzhi, was a native of Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 祖宗璉，父瑞辰，皆進士，以經學顯名。

translations.literal: Ancestor Zonglian and father Ruichen were both metropolitan graduates famed for classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zonglian and his father Ruichen were both metropolitan graduates renowned for classical scholarship.

sentences.zh: 三俊能世其家，顧屢困鄉舉。

translations.literal: Sanjun could inherit the family's tradition, yet repeatedly failed the provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Sanjun carried on the family tradition, yet repeatedly failed the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，以優行第一貢太學，又舉孝廉方正制科。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng, ranked first in superior conduct and presented to the Imperial Academy; he was also selected for the Filial and Incorrupt special examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he topped the superior-conduct list and entered the Imperial Academy, and was also chosen for the Filial and Incorrupt special examination.

sentences.zh: 三年，安慶失守，桐人恟懼，知縣遁去，奸民蜂起。

translations.literal: In the third year Anqing fell; the people of Tong were panic-stricken; the magistrate fled, and evil men rose like bees.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Anqing was lost; the people of Tong were terrified; the magistrate fled, and ruffians swarmed up everywhere.

sentences.zh: 官兵往來境上，亦乘亂為患。

translations.literal: Government troops passing through the border also took advantage of disorder to make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial troops passing through the district also preyed on the chaos.

sentences.zh: 獨縣學生張勛誓死不避，三俊亦急起而坐鎮之，擒斬為首者十數人。

translations.literal: Only the county student Zhang Xun swore not to flee; Sanjun also rose in haste to sit in command, seized and beheaded a dozen or so ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Only the county student Zhang Xun swore he would not flee; Sanjun too rose at once to take command, seized a dozen-odd ringleaders, and had them beheaded.

sentences.zh: 又偕勳立法，勸富家給散貧者，亂稍定。

translations.literal: He also joined Xun in enacting laws, urging wealthy families to distribute to the poor; the disorder eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xun also set rules in law, urging wealthy households to give out grain to the poor, and the turmoil eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 賊既陷安慶，盡趨江寧，諸統帥皆遠避，置安慶、蕪湖不堵截。

translations.literal: After the rebels took Anqing they all rushed toward Jiangning; the various commanders kept their distance, leaving Anqing and Wuhu unblocked.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels held Anqing they all pressed on Nanjing; the commanders kept far off and left Anqing and Wuhu unguarded.

sentences.zh: 三俊知賊之必回竄也，日夜在明倫堂訓練鄉兵，又時與勳往四鄉聯合團眾。

translations.literal: Sanjun knew the rebels would surely raid back; day and night he drilled local troops in the Hall of Bright Ethics, and often went with Xun to the four townships to unite militia.
translations.idiomatic: Sanjun knew the rebels would surely raid back; day and night he drilled militia in the Hall of Bright Ethics, and often went with Xun through the four townships to rally the militia.

sentences.zh: 於是桐城練勇，名聞江南北。

translations.literal: Thus Tongcheng's trained braves became famed north and south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Tongcheng's drilled braves became a name known north and south of the river.

sentences.zh: 賊犯太湖，與勳揚兵堵境上，賊莫測虛實，莫敢逼。

translations.literal: When rebels invaded Taihu, he and Xun raised banners to block the border; the rebels could not gauge strength or weakness and dared not press close.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels struck Taihu, he and Xun showed force along the border; the rebels could not tell real from feigned strength and dared not press in.

sentences.zh: 已而賊攻江西，不克，回據安慶，修守備，桐人大恐。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels attacked Jiangxi without success, returned to hold Anqing and repair defenses; the people of Tong were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels attacked Jiangxi without success, fell back to Anqing, and strengthened its defenses; the people of Tong were terrified.

sentences.zh: 巡撫李嘉瑞駐廬州，前按察使張熙宇駐集賢關，皆畏安慶不敢至。

translations.literal: Governor Li Jiarui was stationed at Luzhou; former Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Xiyu was at Jixian Pass—both feared Anqing and did not approach.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Li Jiarui held Luzhou; former Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Xiyu held Jixian Pass—both feared Anqing and would not come near.

sentences.zh: 三俊上書巡撫，其略謂：「制寇之道，必能攻而後可守；

translations.literal: Sanjun memorialized the governor, the gist saying: "The way to control rebels must be able to attack before one can defend;
translations.idiomatic: Sanjun wrote the governor, in substance: "To master rebels one must be able to attack before one can defend;

sentences.zh: 守御之策，必先據要害而後可保城池。

translations.literal: the policy of defense must first hold vital points before cities can be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: the policy of defense must seize the vital points before the cities can be held.

sentences.zh: 全州不守，禍及湖南；

translations.literal: If Quanzhou is not held, disaster reaches Hunan;
translations.idiomatic: If Quanzhou is not held, Hunan is threatened;

sentences.zh: 岳州不守，禍及武昌；

translations.literal: if Yuezhou is not held, disaster reaches Wuchang;
translations.idiomatic: if Yuezhou is not held, Wuchang is threatened;

sentences.zh: 小孤不守，禍及安慶；

translations.literal: if Xiaogu is not held, disaster reaches Anqing;
translations.idiomatic: if Little Orphan Hill is not held, Anqing is threatened;

sentences.zh: 安慶不守，然後禍及江寧、鎮江、揚州、大江南北。

translations.literal: if Anqing is not held, then disaster reaches Jiangning, Zhenjiang, Yangzhou, and all north and south of the Great River.
translations.idiomatic: if Anqing is not held, then Nanjing, Zhenjiang, Yangzhou, and all the lands north and south of the Yangtze are lost.

sentences.zh: 此明驗也。

translations.literal: This is clear proof.
translations.idiomatic: That is plain proof.

sentences.zh: 自粵西起事以來，賊之所破，多不守而破，非因守而破也；

translations.literal: Since the rising in western Guangdong, of cities the rebels have taken, most fell because they were not defended, not because defense broke them;
translations.idiomatic: Since the rising in western Guangdong, most places the rebels have taken fell because no one held them, not because holding failed;

sentences.zh: 賊之所敗，多不戰而敗，非力戰而敗也。

translations.literal: of defeats the rebels have suffered, most came without fighting, not from hard battle.
translations.idiomatic: most defeats the rebels have suffered came without a fight, not from hard battle.

sentences.zh: 觀桂林、長沙、南昌、開封四省城，苟能死守，賊未有陷之者。

translations.literal: Consider the four provincial capitals Guilin, Changsha, Nanchang, and Kaifeng—if they could be held to the death, the rebels have never yet taken one.
translations.idiomatic: Look at Guilin, Changsha, Nanchang, and Kaifeng—wherever a provincial capital has been held to the death, the rebels have never yet taken it.

sentences.zh: 六合小邑，殺賊數千，而賊不敢至。

translations.literal: Liuhe, a small town, killed several thousand rebels, and the rebels did not dare come.
translations.idiomatic: Liuhe, a small county, killed thousands of rebels, and the rebels did not dare approach.

sentences.zh: 江浦、含山、許州皆以守而得全，不大可見乎？

translations.literal: Jiangpu, Hanshan, and Xuzhou all were preserved by holding—is this not abundantly clear?
translations.idiomatic: Jiangpu, Hanshan, and Xuzhou all stood because they were held—is the lesson not plain enough?

sentences.zh: 今江北全勢完固，虛實未為賊覺，而安慶之賊，又皆江西殘敗之餘，且未齊集。

translations.literal: Now the whole position north of the river is sound, and our strength and weakness have not yet been discovered by the rebels; moreover the rebels at Anqing are all remnants defeated in Jiangxi and are not yet fully gathered.
translations.idiomatic: North of the river our whole position is still sound, and the rebels do not yet know our real strength; the rebels at Anqing are only the broken remnants from Jiangxi and are not yet fully gathered.

sentences.zh: 望於此時迅速進攻，而分兵守桐，以為接應。

translations.literal: I hope at this time to advance swiftly in attack, while dividing troops to hold Tong as a link.
translations.idiomatic: I urge a swift attack now, with a detachment left to hold Tong as the link.

sentences.zh: 如安慶不利，當可退守桐城，以為舒、廬之障。

translations.literal: If Anqing goes ill, one may fall back to hold Tongcheng as a screen for Shu and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: If Anqing goes badly, we can fall back and hold Tongcheng as a shield for Shucheng and Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 此機一失，賊或竄桐、舒，以入廬州，則與北匪勾結，河南北東西、畿輔之地危矣。」

translations.literal: Once this chance is lost, rebels may raid through Tong and Shu into Luzhou; then they will join northern bandits, and the lands of Henan, north, east, west, and the capital region will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Miss this chance and the rebels may slip through Tong and Shucheng into Luzhou, join the northern bandits, and put Henan, the north, east, west, and the capital districts in peril."

sentences.zh: 巡撫韙其言，遣總兵恆興與熙宇合軍堵剿，實不前進。

translations.literal: The governor approved his words and sent Commander Heng Xing to join Zhang Xiyu's army in blocking suppression—but in fact they did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The governor approved his argument and sent Commander Heng Xing to join Xiyu's force in blocking the rebels—but in truth they never advanced.

sentences.zh: 十月，賊大至，熙宇、恆興兵皆卻走，三俊獨與勳率鄉團數百人拒之，不利。

translations.literal: In the tenth month rebels came in force; Xiyu's and Heng Xing's troops all fell back; Sanjun alone with Xun led several hundred militia to resist—without success.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the rebels came in strength; Xiyu's and Heng Xing's men all pulled back; Sanjun and Xun alone led several hundred militiamen to meet them and failed.

sentences.zh: 賊遂道桐城以入舒城，陷廬州，渡河而北，蔓延千里，皆如三俊所料。

translations.literal: Rebels then passed through Tongcheng to enter Shucheng, took Luzhou, crossed the river northward, and spread a thousand li—all as Sanjun had foretold.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then marched through Tongcheng into Shucheng, took Luzhou, crossed the river north, and spread disaster for a thousand li—just as Sanjun had warned.

sentences.zh: 城陷時，三俊父被執不屈死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Sanjun's father was seized and died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell his father was taken and died refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 三俊以不孝不忠自責，誓復仇報國。

translations.literal: Sanjun blamed himself for unfiliality and disloyalty and swore to take revenge and serve the state.
translations.idiomatic: Sanjun blamed himself as unfilial and disloyal and swore to avenge his father and serve the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，與前任桐城知縣成福、六安參將慶麟，招集義勇於霍山，請助官軍殺賊，且言「事成不邀功賞，事敗則以身死之」。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year, with former Tongcheng Magistrate Cheng Fu and Luzhou Brigadier Qing Lin, he gathered volunteers at Huoshan, asked to aid government troops in killing rebels, and said: "If we succeed I seek no reward; if we fail I die for it."
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year he joined former Tongcheng magistrate Cheng Fu and Luzhou brigadier Qing Lin to raise volunteers at Huoshan, asked to aid the imperial army against the rebels, and said, "If we succeed I want no reward; if we fail I will die for it."

sentences.zh: 於是上三路進兵策，而自任桐城一路。

translations.literal: Thereupon he presented the plan of a three-route advance and took the Tongcheng route himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a plan for a three-pronged advance and took the Tongcheng column himself.

sentences.zh: 先頓兵中梅河以俟，而提督秦定三軍之圖舒城者，延期不進。

translations.literal: He first halted at Zhongmei River to wait; but Qin Dingsan's army for investing Shucheng delayed and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: He first camped on the Zhongmei River to wait, but Qin Dingsan's army at the siege of Shucheng lagged and would not move.

sentences.zh: 三俊既孤軍深入，恥不肯退。

translations.literal: Sanjun had penetrated deep with a lone army and was shamed to refuse retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Sanjun had pushed deep with a lone column and was too ashamed to pull back.

sentences.zh: 至周瑜城，援絕餉匱，奸民構賊夜襲營，力戰死之。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhouyu Fort, supplies cut off and provisions exhausted, evil men colluded with rebels to raid the camp by night; he fought to exhaustion and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhouyu Fort his relief was cut and his stores gone; local ruffians turned the rebels on the camp by night, and he fought until he fell.

sentences.zh: 勳，字小嵩，與三俊同縣人。

translations.literal: Xun, style Xiaosong, was from the same county as Sanjun.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, courtesy name Xiaosong, was a fellow townsman of Sanjun.

sentences.zh: 家貧，好倡舉義行。

translations.literal: Poor in family, he loved to lead righteous undertakings.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, but he loved to lead acts of public righteousness.

sentences.zh: 嘗搜羅桐城節孝貞烈婦女二千餘人無力上聞者，匯請旌表，著總旌錄四卷。

translations.literal: He once gathered more than two thousand chaste and martyred women of Tongcheng who could not afford to report upward, submitted memorials seeking commendation, and compiled four fascicles of a General Commendation Record.
translations.idiomatic: He once gathered more than two thousand chaste and martyred women of Tongcheng who could not afford to petition the throne, submitted them for imperial commendation, and compiled four fascicles of the General Commendation Record.

sentences.zh: 桐城既破，三俊起義兵霍山，與之定計，即往見秦定三，以急擊舒城，與襲桐之師相應說之，定三不應，事遂敗。

translations.literal: After Tongcheng was lost, Sanjun raised loyal troops at Huoshan; with him he made plans, then went to see Qin Dingsan, urging a swift strike on Shucheng to coordinate with the force raiding Tong—but Dingsan did not agree and the plan failed.
translations.idiomatic: After Tongcheng fell Sanjun raised loyal troops at Huoshan; with him Xun laid plans, then went to Qin Dingsan and urged a swift strike on Shucheng to match the column striking Tong—but Dingsan would not listen and the plan came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 嗣聞紓青統兵至桐，往六安迎之，謂紓青曰：「桐近日賊勢與前不類，兵單援寡，難操勝算。

translations.literal: Later hearing Shuqing commanded troops at Tong, he went to Lu'an to meet him and said to Shuqing: "Tong's rebel situation of late is not like before; few troops, scant aid—hard to secure victory.
translations.idiomatic: Later, hearing Shuqing had brought troops to Tong, he went to Lu'an to meet him and said, "The rebel strength at Tong lately is not what it was; you have few men and little help—it will be hard to win.

sentences.zh: 不如先助攻舒，舒破，與秦軍合，事乃有濟。」

translations.literal: Better first to join in attacking Shu; when Shu falls and you unite with Qin's army, the affair can succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Better join the attack on Shucheng first; when Shucheng falls and you unite with Qin's army, the plan may work."

sentences.zh: 又數以書勸定三，卒不應，紓青亦不肯往。

translations.literal: He also several times wrote to urge Dingsan; in the end there was no response, and Shuqing also would not go.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote again and again to urge Dingsan, but in the end there was no answer, and Shuqing would not go either.

sentences.zh: 十一月十七日，遂隨紓青督戰，死之。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day of the eleventh month he followed Shuqing to direct the battle and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth of the eleventh month he followed Shuqing into battle and died there.

sentences.zh: 隨死者有吳文謨。

translations.literal: One who died with him was Wu Wenmo.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wenmo died with him.

sentences.zh: 文謨，字翼甫，亦同縣人。

translations.literal: Wenmo, style Yifu, was also from the same county.
translations.idiomatic: Wenmo, courtesy name Yifu, was from the same county.

sentences.zh: 年少負氣，與三俊子復震為友。

translations.literal: Young and spirited, he befriended Sanjun's son Fuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Young and high-spirited, he befriended Sanjun's son Fuzhen.

sentences.zh: 三俊死，文謨不告其子，獨冒險往獲其屍。

translations.literal: After Sanjun died, Wenmo did not tell his son but went alone at risk to recover his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: When Sanjun fell, Wenmo did not tell his son but went alone through danger to bring back the body.

sentences.zh: 勳重其人，遂隨勳奔走，請兵不倦，殉節時年二十有一。

translations.literal: Xun valued the man and then followed Xun in ceaseless efforts to seek troops; he died for the cause at twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Xun prized him and kept him at his side, running everywhere to beg for troops without rest; he died for the cause at twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 吳廷香，字奉璋，廬江人。

translations.literal: Wu Tingxiang, style Fengzhang, was a native of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tingxiang, courtesy name Fengzhang, was a native of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 敏博沈毅，與桐城戴鈞衡、馬三俊友，以文章風節相砥礪。

translations.literal: Keen, broad, and resolute, he befriended Dai Junheng and Ma Sanjun of Tongcheng, honing each other in letters and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-minded, learned, and steady, he befriended Dai Junheng and Ma Sanjun of Tongcheng and sharpened one another in letters and moral resolve.

sentences.zh: 以優貢生舉咸豐初元孝廉方正。

translations.literal: Presented to the Academy on superior conduct and selected in the first Xianfeng cycle for Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Presented to the Academy on superior conduct, he was chosen in the first Xianfeng cycle for the Filial and Incorrupt examination.

sentences.zh: 上書論時事，有國士之目。

translations.literal: He memorialized on current affairs and was regarded as a man of national stature.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on affairs of state and was spoken of as a man of national caliber.

sentences.zh: 三年，粵賊東下，陷安慶，廬江土寇應之，駸駸迫城下。

translations.literal: In the third year Taiping rebels drove east, took Anqing; Lujiang local bandits responded; they pressed the walls ever closer.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Taiping rebels drove east, took Anqing, and local bandits in Lujiang rose in answer, pressing ever closer to the walls.

sentences.zh: 邑團練鄉兵推廷香為督，擊寇，擒其渠，斬之，盡破其黨。

translations.literal: The county militia pushed Tingxiang as commander; he struck the marauders, captured their chief, beheaded him, and utterly broke their faction.
translations.idiomatic: The county militia chose Tingxiang as commander; he struck the bandits, seized their chief, beheaded him, and broke their faction utterly.

sentences.zh: 尋，粵賊棄安慶去，長驅薄金陵，踞其城。

translations.literal: Soon the Taiping rebels abandoned Anqing and marched in a long drive to Jinling, occupying the city.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Taiping rebels left Anqing and marched in a long drive on Nanjing, seizing the city.

sentences.zh: 是年夏，復遣悍酋沿江西犯，再陷安慶，皖北震動。

translations.literal: That summer they again sent fierce chieftains along Jiangxi to invade, took Anqing again, and north Anhui trembled.
translations.idiomatic: That summer they again sent fierce chieftains up the Jiangxi route, retook Anqing, and north Anhui shook.

sentences.zh: 廷香复倡義募鄉勇六百人，自率之守梅山黃姑閘，遏江路。

translations.literal: Tingxiang again led a drive to recruit six hundred volunteers and personally led them to guard the Huanggu Pass at Meishan, blocking the river route.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxiang again led the call to raise six hundred volunteers and took them himself to hold Huanggu Pass at Meishan and block the river line.

sentences.zh: 時賊張甚，官吏兵民所在迸散。

translations.literal: At the time rebels were rampant; officials, soldiers, and people scattered wherever they were.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were then at their height; officials, soldiers, and commoners fled wherever they stood.

sentences.zh: 賊自桐城北擾，舒、巢、無為相繼淪沒，獨廬江賴廷香固扼得全。

translations.literal: Rebels raided north from Tongcheng; Shu, Chao, and Wuwei fell in succession; only Lujiang, thanks to Tingxiang's firm hold, was kept intact.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels raided north from Tongcheng; Shucheng, Chaohu, and Wuwei fell one after another; only Lujiang, by Tingxiang's stubborn hold on the pass, was kept whole.

sentences.zh: 十一月，廬州陷，巡撫江忠源死之，官軍、團練望風逃潰。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Luzhou fell; Governor Jiang Zhongyuan died there, and government troops and militia fled at the mere rumor of approach.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Luzhou fell. Governor Jiang Zhongyuan died in the fighting, and regular troops and militia broke and ran at the first alarm.

sentences.zh: 十二月，廬江亦不守。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Lujiang also could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: By the twelfth month Lujiang too was lost.

sentences.zh: 廷香時在防次，扼腕慷慨，誓必得當以報國。

translations.literal: Tingxiang was then at his defensive post; he wrung his wrists in anguish and swore he must repay the country as duty required.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxiang was still on the line. He clenched his fists in grief and swore he would find some fitting way to serve the state.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，提督和春敗賊於廬州；

translations.literal: In the fourth year, second month, Commissioner He Chun defeated rebels at Luzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, the second month, Commissioner He Chun defeated the rebels at Luzhou;

sentences.zh: 七月，提督秦定三大捷於舒城；

translations.literal: seventh month, Commissioner Qin Dingsan won a great victory at Shucheng;
translations.idiomatic: in the seventh month Commissioner Qin Dingsan won a great victory at Shucheng;

sentences.zh: 舟師復自海道入扼東西梁山，斷賊歸路。

translations.literal: the fleet again entered by the sea route to hold East and West Liang Mountains, cutting the rebels' line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: the river force again came in by sea to seize East and West Liang Mountains and sever the rebels' retreat.

sentences.zh: 賊悉眾北趨，諸州縣守賊少，曾國籓复率大軍下武昌。

translations.literal: The rebels concentrated all their forces heading north; garrisons in the prefectures and counties were thin; Zeng Guofan again led a great army down on Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels massed and drove north. With so few men left to hold the counties, Zeng Guofan again marched a great host down on Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 廷香聞則奮然起，言於眾，謂：「誠以此時出賊不意复邑城，益與江上、下諸路軍相應，合謀以圖皖中，賊可殲也。」

translations.literal: When Tingxiang heard, he sprang up and said to the crowd: "If at this moment we strike the rebels unawares and recover the county seat, and moreover coordinate with the armies on the upper and lower river routes, joining plans to take central Anhui—the rebels can be annihilated."
translations.idiomatic: When Tingxiang heard this he rose at once and told the assembly, "Strike now, while the rebels do not expect it, retake the county seat, and link arms with the armies upriver and down. Plot together for central Anhui, and the rebels can be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 乃召募三千人，與外委熊允升將之趨縣門，兼密約舊時勇目居城中者為內應。

translations.literal: He then recruited three thousand men and, with external appointee Xiong Yunsheng leading them, rushed to the county gate, while secretly arranging with former brave chiefs still in the city to act as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: He raised three thousand men. With the external appointee Xiong Yunsheng in command they hurried to the county gate, and quietly won over the old militia leaders still inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 八月，大破守賊，賊渠任大剛走，追斬之，遂復廬江。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he shattered the garrison rebels; rebel chieftain Ren Dagang fled, was pursued and beheaded, and Lujiang was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he broke the rebel garrison. The chieftain Ren Dagang fled, was run down and beheaded, and Lujiang was retaken.

sentences.zh: 大江東、西以鄉兵敗賊克城，蓋自廷香始。

translations.literal: East and west of the great river, to defeat rebels and recover cities with militia—this began with Tingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: For militia east and west of the Yangtze to beat rebels and retake a city—this began with Tingxiang.

sentences.zh: 既，賊知廬江無援，合安慶、桐城諸路來攻，廷香出擊，屢有斬獲，而賊聚益眾，江中賊亦逼城下。

translations.literal: Soon the rebels knew Lujiang had no reinforcement; they combined forces from Anqing, Tongcheng, and other routes to attack. Tingxiang sallied and repeatedly cut heads, but rebels gathered ever more numerous, and rebels on the river also pressed below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon saw that Lujiang had no help. They united columns from Anqing, Tongcheng, and elsewhere. Tingxiang went out again and again and took heads, but the enemy swelled, and river rebels closed under the walls.

sentences.zh: 廷香豫乞救廬、舒大營，久未報。

translations.literal: Tingxiang had beforehand begged relief from the great camps at Luzhou and Shucheng, but for long there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxiang had already pleaded with the main camps at Luzhou and Shucheng. For a long time no answer came.

sentences.zh: 及賊大至，何桂珍檄蔡萼、沈承貽以六百人自六安赴援，至邑，則縱兵大掠，遇賊反走，賊益焚四野，火光燭天。

translations.literal: When rebels came in force, He Guizhen ordered Cai E and Shen Chengyi with six hundred men from Lu'an to reinforce. When they reached the county they let their troops plunder greatly, met rebels and fled back, and rebels all the more burned the four outskirts until firelight lit the sky.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels came in strength, He Guizhen ordered Cai E and Shen Chengyi forward from Lu'an with six hundred men. They reached the town and turned their men loose to plunder. They met the rebels and ran. The enemy burned the countryside until the sky glowed.

sentences.zh: 廷香夜登陴，望救不至，拊膺泣曰：「吾志清逆亂，不克，而重禍鄉里。

translations.literal: Tingxiang at night climbed the walls, saw rescue did not come, clutched his chest weeping: "My aim was to clear rebellion and disorder; I could not, yet bring heavy calamity on my home county.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxiang climbed the wall at night. No relief came. He beat his breast and wept, "I meant to put down rebellion. I failed, and brought ruin on my own county.

sentences.zh: 勢窮援絕，來者非人。

translations.literal: Strength exhausted, aid cut off—the ones coming are not men.
translations.idiomatic: We are spent, and no one is coming—only men who are not men.

sentences.zh: 吾死此，分耳，亂將若之何？」

translations.literal: I die here—that is my portion; what will become of the disorder?"
translations.idiomatic: I die here. That is my share. What will become of the chaos?"

sentences.zh: 數日，糧竭，萼、承貽引遁，城遂再陷。

translations.literal: After several days grain was exhausted; E and Chengyi withdrew in flight, and the city was lost again.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the grain was gone. Cai E and Shen Chengyi slipped away, and the city fell again.

sentences.zh: 廷香率死士巷戰，自午夜至黎明，從者僅三人，力盡死之，允升同及於難。

translations.literal: Tingxiang led doomed warriors in street fighting from midnight till dawn; followers were only three; strength spent, he died; Yunsheng met the same calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxiang led his last men in the lanes from midnight to dawn. Only three followed him. He fought until he fell. Yunsheng died in the same disaster.

sentences.zh: 初，廷香將倡義，或危其事，尼之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tingxiang would lead a righteous drive, some warned the matter was dangerous and held him back.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingxiang first called men to arms, some called the venture too risky and tried to stop him.

sentences.zh: 廷香從容曰：「如若言，亂將誰拯耶？」

translations.literal: Tingxiang calmly said: "As you speak, who will save the disorder?
translations.idiomatic: Tingxiang answered calmly, "If that is so, who will save us from chaos?

sentences.zh: 其人悚然退。

translations.literal: The man recoiled and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The man shrank back and left.

sentences.zh: 及事急，將自裁，或奪​​刀掖之行，廷香抗聲曰：「复城守城，雖非吾責，吾義也。

translations.literal: When affairs grew urgent and he would take his own life, someone seized the knife and pulled him along. Tingxiang cried out: "Recovering the city and holding the city—though not my appointed duty, it is my right conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When things turned desperate he meant to kill himself. Someone snatched the blade and pulled him away. Tingxiang shouted, "To retake the city and hold it was never my office alone, but it is my duty.

sentences.zh: 城危而走，義何居焉？

translations.literal: When the city is perilous and one flees—where does righteousness dwell?
translations.idiomatic: When the walls are failing and you run—where is honor then?

sentences.zh: 出郭一步，非死所也！」

translations.literal: One step beyond the outer wall—that is not a place to die!
translations.idiomatic: One pace outside the gate is no place for a man to die!

sentences.zh: 比戰歿，邑人求得其屍，藁葬之。

translations.literal: When the battle ended he perished; townsmen found his corpse and buried it in straw rites.
translations.idiomatic: He fell in the fight. The townspeople found his body and buried him in a simple grave.

sentences.zh: 詔建專祠廬江，予世職。

translations.literal: An edict built a dedicated shrine at Lujiang and granted a hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered a private shrine at Lujiang and a hereditary post for his line.

sentences.zh: 子長慶繼其志，累官至提督，以功顯。

translations.literal: His son Changqing continued his purpose, rose repeatedly to commissioner, and won distinction by merit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changqing took up his cause, rose to commissioner by repeated promotion, and won fame in the field.

sentences.zh: 孫家泰，字引恬，壽州人。

translations.literal: Sun Jiatai, style Yintian, was a native of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiatai, courtesy name Yintian, came from Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 大父有善行，仁宗嘗書「盛世醇良」四字顏其門。

translations.literal: His grandfather had good conduct; Emperor Renzong once wrote four characters "Pure Integrity in a Flourishing Age" for his gate tablet.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was known for virtue. Emperor Renzong once wrote four characters, "Pure Integrity in a Flourishing Age," for the lintel of their gate.

sentences.zh: 家泰生有殊禀，嬉戲異群兒。

translations.literal: Jiatai was born with unusual gifts; in play he differed from other children.
translations.idiomatic: Jiatai seemed marked from birth. Even in play he was unlike other boys.

sentences.zh: 每出語，長老驚若成人。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke, elders were startled as at a grown man.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke, village elders started as if he were already a man.

sentences.zh: 未冠，補諸生。

translations.literal: Before his cap he became a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He became a licentiate before he came of age.

sentences.zh: 道光二十九年，入貲為員外郎，分刑部廣西司，治牘明決，為上官所器。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang he purchased office as an outer department director, assigned to the Guangxi Department of Punishments, judged documents clearly, and was valued by superiors.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang he bought office as an outer director in the Ministry of Punishments, Guangxi Bureau. His papers were sharp and clear, and his superiors prized him.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵寇竄擾江、皖，工部侍郎呂賢基奉命回籍督辦團練，請以家泰從。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng the Taiping rebels ran riot in Jiang and Wan; Vice Minister of Works Lü Xianji was ordered home to supervise militia training and requested Jiatai accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng Taiping rebels ravaged Jiangnan and Anhui. Vice Minister Lü Xianji was sent home to raise militia and asked Jiatai to go with him.

sentences.zh: 時皖南北郡邑相繼不守，官吏望風避走，群盜蜂起。

translations.literal: At that time prefectures and counties north and south of Wan fell in succession; officials fled at rumor; bandits rose like bees.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties across the region fell one after another. Officials fled at a whisper. Bandits swarmed up everywhere.

sentences.zh: 定遠陸遐齡倡亂據城，道路梗塞。

translations.literal: Lu Xiangling of Dingyuan led disorder and held the city; roads were blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiangling of Dingyuan raised revolt and seized the city. The roads were cut.

sentences.zh: 朝命再起週天爵為安徽巡撫，天爵就詢策略，家泰密為擘畫，數旬之間，遐齡父子就擒，脅從解散，餘盜斂跡，壽春兵以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: The court ordered Zhou Tianjue reappointed Anhui governor; Tianjue sought his counsel. Jiatai secretly plotted; within weeks father and son of Xiangling were captured, coerced followers dispersed, remaining bandits shrank away, and Shouxian troops became known for fierce bravery.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled Zhou Tianjue as governor of Anhui. Tianjue asked Jiatai for a plan. In a few weeks the Xiangling father and son were taken, their followers scattered, the rest of the bandits faded, and the Shouxian troops won a name for hard fighting.

sentences.zh: 軍興，徵調四出，留鎮者少，又乏食，巡撫檄家泰勸捐募兵為固圉計。

translations.literal: With warfare, levies went everywhere; few remained to garrison; food was lacking; the governor ordered Jiatai to urge donations and recruit troops to strengthen defense.
translations.idiomatic: War drew troops away on every side. Little was left to guard the walls, and food ran short. The governor ordered Jiatai to raise funds and recruit men to hold the district.

sentences.zh: 壽故繁庶，富家大賈務厚藏，鮮遠識，無應者。

translations.literal: Shou was formerly populous; rich merchants hoarded and lacked foresight; none responded.
translations.idiomatic: Shou had once been rich. Great merchants hoarded their wealth and could not see ahead. No one answered the call.

sentences.zh: 家泰則盡貨其貲產以濟用，所募皆敢死士。

translations.literal: Jiatai then sold all his property to meet needs; those he recruited were all men ready to die.
translations.idiomatic: Jiatai sold everything he owned to pay for the effort. Every man he raised was ready to die.

sentences.zh: 明賞罰，嚴簡練，一軍肅然。

translations.literal: Clear rewards and punishments, strict drilling—one army was sternly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments were plain, drill was tight, and the whole force stood in order.

sentences.zh: 廬、鳳、潁、六安諸寇憚其強，不敢窺。

translations.literal: Rebels of Lu, Feng, Ying, and Lu'an feared his strength and dared not peer in.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels around Luzhou, Fengyang, Yingzhou, and Lu'an dared not test him.

sentences.zh: 尋，天爵卒於潁州，舒城再陷，呂賢基死之。

translations.literal: Soon Tianjue died at Yingzhou, Shucheng fell again, and Lü Xianji died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tianjue died at Yingzhou, Shucheng fell again, and Lü Xianji was killed.

sentences.zh: 家泰失所隸，勢遂孤。

translations.literal: Jiatai lost his affiliation; his strength was isolated.
translations.idiomatic: Jiatai lost his patron. His position stood alone.

sentences.zh: 尋為人所構，吏議落職。

translations.literal: Soon framed by others, officials deliberated to remove him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon enemies framed him, and the civil officers moved to strip him of rank.

sentences.zh: 家泰語人曰：「時事糜爛，守土之吏，畏賊如虎狼，而視民如魚肉，是驅良入於暴也，吾無死所矣！」

translations.literal: Jiatai said to people: "Affairs are in rotten confusion; the officials holding land fear rebels like tigers and wolves yet view the people as fish on the chopping block—this drives the good into violence; I have no place to die!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiatai told others, "The times are rotten. Men who should guard the soil fear rebels like tigers and wolves, yet treat the people like meat on the block. That drives the good to violence. There is no decent place left for me to die!"

sentences.zh: 自是杜門家居，口不言兵事。

translations.literal: From then he shut his gate at home and would not speak of military matters.
translations.idiomatic: After that he shut his door and never spoke of war again.

sentences.zh: 既毀家佐軍，貧甚，菽水養親，晏如也。

translations.literal: Having ruined his family to aid the army, he was very poor, yet nourished his parents with beans and water serenely.
translations.idiomatic: He had ruined his house to help the army and was very poor, yet he fed his parents on plain fare and was content.

sentences.zh: 既，賊氛益熾，諸州縣團練，多陰附賊，而鳳臺苗沛霖所部尤橫桀不可製。

translations.literal: Soon the rebel atmosphere grew fiercer; militia of many prefectures and counties secretly sided with rebels, and especially the forces of Fengtai's Miao Peilin were overbearing and uncontrollable.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels grew bolder. Militia in many counties secretly joined them. Worst of all were the men of Miao Peilin in Fengtai—proud, violent, and beyond control.

sentences.zh: 初，沛霖為諸生，請於知州金光箸欲練鄉團，而自為練總，光箸不之許。

translations.literal: Initially Peilin was a licentiate; he asked Prefect Jin Guangzhu to drill rural corps with himself as drill chief; Guangzhu did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Peilin had been a licentiate. He asked Prefect Jin Guangzhu to let him train a rural corps under his own command. Guangzhu refused.

sentences.zh: 沛霖遂聚群不逞為亂，鄰邑豪猾多歸之。

translations.literal: Peilin then gathered unruly crowds for disorder; bold fellows of neighboring counties mostly joined him.
translations.idiomatic: Peilin then gathered ruffians and rose in revolt. Bold men from nearby counties flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 官軍畏其眾，遣人招撫，授以官，為羈縻計。

translations.literal: Government troops feared his numbers, sent men to offer pacification and grants of office, as a plan to restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Regular troops feared his numbers. They sent envoys to pacify him and gave him office, hoping to leash him.

sentences.zh: 數年累薦至川北道，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: Over several years he was repeatedly recommended to Sichuan North Circuit Intendant, with nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year he was promoted until he held the Sichuan North circuit and nominal rank as provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 沛霖不奉命，南據正陽關，北扼下蔡，繼襲懷遠，陷之，號稱苗練，駸駸逼壽州。

translations.literal: Peilin did not obey orders, held Zhengyang Pass in the south, choked Xia'ai in the north, then raided Huaiyuan and took it, styled himself Miao Militia, and pressed ever closer on Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Peilin would not obey. He seized Zhengyang Pass in the south and blocked Xia'ai in the north, then stormed Huaiyuan and held it. He called his force the Miao Militia and closed on Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 壽人恟懼，謀聚保，眾議非家泰莫屬，辭不獲，強起。

translations.literal: The people of Shou were terrified and planned mass defense; public opinion said none but Jiatai would do. He declined but could not, and was forced to rise.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shou were afraid and talked of mass defense. Everyone said only Jiatai would do. He refused until he could refuse no more, and was pressed to lead.

sentences.zh: 號召部曲，上書軍帥，力主剿，未報。

translations.literal: He called up his old followers, memorialized army commanders, and strongly urged extermination, but there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied his old troops and wrote to the commanders urging all-out suppression. No answer came.

sentences.zh: 沛霖遣諜入壽州，家泰殺之，沛霖益怒，盡發其黨來攻，守者恐不敵。

translations.literal: Peilin sent spies into Shouzhou; Jiatai killed them. Peilin grew angrier and sent all his faction to attack; defenders feared they could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: Peilin sent spies into Shouzhou. Jiatai had them killed. Peilin raged and sent his whole party against the town. The defenders feared they could not stand.

sentences.zh: 忌家泰者，乃倡言獻家泰與其副蒙時中於賊，以紓壽禍。

translations.literal: Those jealous of Jiatai then advocated handing over Jiatai and his deputy Meng Shizhong to the rebels to ease Shou's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Men who envied Jiatai began to say the town should hand him and his deputy Meng Shizhong to the enemy to buy peace.

sentences.zh: 有司迫行，眾大譁，將以力抗。

translations.literal: Local officials pressed to carry it out; the crowd uproared and was about to resist by force.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrates tried to force it through. The people roared in protest and were ready to fight.

sentences.zh: 家泰夷然曰：「吾昔募健兒刺苗逆悍將，今又戮其諜，欲甘心者我也。

translations.literal: Jiatai calmly said: "I once recruited brave men to assassinate the Miao rebels' fierce generals; now again I killed their spy—those who want my life are set on it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiatai said calmly, "I once raised bold men to strike down the Miao rebels' fiercest captains. Now I have killed their spy again. The men who want my blood are fixed on me.

sentences.zh: 守土非其人，順逆不明至此，事之不濟，天也。

translations.literal: Those holding the land are not the right men; loyalty and rebellion are unclear to this point—the affair's failure is Heaven's.
translations.idiomatic: The wrong men hold the land. Loyalty and treason are confused. If we fail, that is Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 吾身許國矣，吾死而城安，其又奚卹？」

translations.literal: My body is pledged to the state; if I die and the city is safe—what more is there to grieve?"
translations.idiomatic: I have given my body to the state. If I die and the city stands, what is left to mourn?"

sentences.zh: 遂仰藥死。

translations.literal: He then took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: He drank poison and died.

sentences.zh: 既歿，按察使張學醇复縛時中付賊寨，並遇害。

translations.literal: After his death, Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhang Xuechun again bound Shizhong and handed him to the rebel camp; both met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: After he was gone, Provincial Commissioner Zhang Xuechun bound Shizhong too and sent him to the rebel camp. Both were killed.

sentences.zh: 是年九月，沛霖卒陷壽州，家泰家屬被執，不屈，皆死之。

translations.literal: That year, in the ninth month, Peilin finally took Shouzhou; Jiatai's household were seized, would not yield, and all died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of that year Peilin took Shouzhou at last. Jiatai's family were seized, refused to submit, and all died.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，科爾沁親王僧格林沁督師至，沛霖敗死，壽州平。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi, Prince Sengge Rinchen of Horqin supervised the army; Peilin was defeated and died; Shouzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongzhi Prince Sengge Rinchen of Horqin led the army. Peilin was beaten and killed, and Shouzhou was recovered.

sentences.zh: 聞家泰一門死事狀於朝，詔贈四品卿，照陣亡例賜卹，建祠壽州。

translations.literal: Hearing report of Jiatai's whole family's martyrdom, an edict posthumously awarded fourth-rank chamberlain, condolence by battle-death precedent, and built a shrine at Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the court heard how Jiatai's whole household had died, it posthumously made him a fourth-rank chamberlain, granted battle-death rites, and raised a shrine at Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 父贈祖，弟家彥、家德，子傳洙，咸卹贈有差。

translations.literal: His father was posthumously promoted to grandfather rank; brothers Jiayan and Jiade and son Chuanzhu all received graded posthumous condolence.
translations.idiomatic: His father was raised in posthumous rank. His brothers Jiayan and Jiade and his son Chuanzhu received graded honors.

sentences.zh: 江圖悃，字汝華，旌德人。

translations.literal: Jiang Tukun, style Ruhua, was a native of Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Tukun, courtesy name Ruhua, came from Jingde.

sentences.zh: 富膽略。

translations.literal: He was rich in daring and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 經商，寓舒城。

translations.literal: He engaged in trade and lodged at Shucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was a merchant and lived at Shucheng.

sentences.zh: 侍郎呂賢基辦團勦賊，過舒城，與圖悃一見相契，特命帶鄉團，扼守舒城衝要，賊不敢過。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Lü Xianji handled militia suppression of rebels; passing Shucheng he met Tukun and at once they were in accord. He specially ordered Tukun to lead rural corps, hold Shucheng's strategic passage, and rebels dared not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Lü Xianji was organizing militia to fight rebels. He passed through Shucheng, met Tukun, and took to him at once. He put Tukun in charge of local troops to hold the town's vital points, and rebels did not dare pass.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，桐城被​​陷，乘勝至舒城，賢基戰不利，死之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year Tongcheng fell; the victors came on to Shucheng; Xianji fought poorly and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year Tongcheng fell. The enemy pressed on to Shucheng. Xianji fought and was beaten, and died.

sentences.zh: 圖悃猶力戰，狂呼殺賊。

translations.literal: Tukun still fought hard, wildly shouting to kill rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Tukun still fought on, roaring to kill rebels.

sentences.zh: 久之，賊至益眾，援兵不至，歿於陣。

translations.literal: After a long time rebels came ever more numerous; reinforcements did not arrive, and he perished in formation.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels kept coming. Relief never came. He fell in the line.

sentences.zh: 圖悃前以助餉贈知府，至是歿，舒人義之，相與私諡曰仁惠。

translations.literal: Tukun had earlier been granted nominal prefect for aiding supplies; on this death the people of Shucheng honored him, and together privately posthumously titled him Benevolent and Kind.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier been given nominal prefect rank for helping with funds. When he died the people of Shucheng honored him and together gave him the private posthumous title Benevolent and Kind.

sentences.zh: 宣統初，補諡莊潔。

translations.literal: In early Xuantong a supplementary posthumous title was given: Solemn and Pure.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuantong reign a further posthumous title was added: Solemn and Pure.

sentences.zh: 程葆，歙縣人。

translations.literal: Cheng Bao was a native of She county.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Bao came from She county.

sentences.zh: 道光十三年進士，以主事分工部。

translations.literal: A presented scholar of the thirteenth year of Daoguang, he served as a director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination in the thirteenth year of Daoguang and served as a director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年六月，外授廣東肇慶府知府。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Xianfeng he was appointed in the outer service as prefect of Zhaoqing in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Xianfeng he was sent out as prefect of Zhaoqing in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 時粵匪麕集皖境，謀犯浙江，葆赴任，道經杭州，巡撫何桂清奏令回籍治鄉團助剿。

translations.literal: At that time Taiping bandits gathered thick in Wan and plotted to invade Zhejiang. Bao went to his post, passed Hangzhou en route, and Governor He Guiqing memorialized ordering him to return home to organize rural corps and aid suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping rebels were massing in Anhui and meant to strike Zhejiang. Bao was on his way to his post when he passed Hangzhou. Governor He Guiqing memorialized that he should return home, raise militia, and help suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 五年，賊陷休寧，葆率民團出境援，與官軍會擊於東、南二門，斃賊目，賊驚退入城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year rebels took Xiuning; Bao led civilian corps beyond the border to aid, joined government troops striking at the east and south gates, killed a rebel chief, and rebels startled retreated into the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the rebels took Xiuning. Bao led local militia out to help. With the regular troops he struck the east and south gates, killed a rebel officer, and drove the enemy back inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 諸軍連夜進攻，賊由西門遁，遂拔休寧，乘勝克復石埭。

translations.literal: All armies attacked through the night; rebels fled by the west gate; thus Xiuning was recovered, and pressing the victory they recovered Shiting.
translations.idiomatic: The allied forces attacked through the night. The rebels slipped out the west gate. Xiuning was retaken, and the victors went on to recover Shiting.

sentences.zh: 自是葆益激勵鄉團，屢助官軍勦賊，徽郡肅清。

translations.literal: From then Bao further stimulated rural corps, repeatedly aided government troops in suppressing rebels, and the Huizhou region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: After that Bao roused the militia again and again, helped the regular army crush rebels, and Huizhou was cleared.

sentences.zh: 旋檄赴杭助守，城陷，死之。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to Hangzhou to aid defense; the city fell, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to Hangzhou to help hold the city. The city fell, and he died.

sentences.zh: 彭壽頤，字子文，江西萬載人。

translations.literal: Peng Shouyi, style Ziwen, was a native of Wanzai in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shouyi, courtesy name Ziwen, came from Wanzai in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 道光二十九年舉人。

translations.literal: A presented scholar of the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang.
translations.idiomatic: He became a presented scholar in the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，粵匪連破江西郡縣，知縣李峼棄城遁，壽頤率團練禦賊，追剿上高、新昌，皆捷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng Taiping bandits repeatedly broke Jiangxi prefectures and counties; Magistrate Li Kun abandoned the city and fled; Shouyi led militia against rebels, pursued suppression at Shanggao and Xinchang, and won every fight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianfeng Taiping rebels overran one Jiangxi county after another. Magistrate Li Kun abandoned his post and ran. Shouyi led militia against them and chased them through Shanggao and Xinchang, winning every fight.

sentences.zh: 以籌餉忤李峼，峼袒奸民，壽頤揭前棄城事。

translations.literal: For raising supplies he offended Li Kun; Kun shielded wicked civilians; Shouyi exposed Kun's prior abandonment of the city.
translations.idiomatic: He raised funds for the war and crossed Li Kun. Kun protected local bullies. Shouyi brought out the record of Kun's earlier flight from the city.

sentences.zh: 巡撫陳啟邁夙諱賊，恐上聞，以蜚語誣捕壽頤，欲致死滅口。

translations.literal: Governor Chen Qimai had long dreaded reports of rebels, fearing the throne would hear; he used slanderous talk to falsely arrest Shouyi, wanting death to silence him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Chen Qimai had always hated to hear of rebels and feared the court would learn the truth. He spread lies, seized Shouyi, and meant to kill him to seal his mouth.

sentences.zh: 欽差大臣曾國籓奏言：「數年以來，諭旨諄諄，飭行團練，多無實效。

translations.literal: Imperial Commissioner Zeng Guofan memorialized: "For several years the edicts have been earnest, ordering militia training, yet mostly without real effect.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Commissioner Zeng Guofan wrote, "For years the throne has urged militia training, yet in most places it has come to nothing.

sentences.zh: 惟湖南平江縣、江西義寧州以本地捐款練本地壯丁，屢殲悍黨，為賊深畏。

translations.literal: Only Hunan's Pingjiang county and Jiangxi's Yining prefecture, using local donations to drill local stalwarts, repeatedly annihilated fierce factions and were deeply feared by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Only Pingjiang in Hunan and Yining in Jiangxi, drilling local men on local funds, broke fierce bands again and again. The rebels feared them.

sentences.zh: 四年，義寧之捷，巡撫陳啟邁冒功濫保，遍私親暱，人心解體，團練遂散。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, at Yining's victory, Governor Chen Qimai stole merit and broadly recommended private favorites; hearts scattered, and militia then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after the victory at Yining, Governor Chen Qimai claimed the credit and stuffed his reports with kin and friends. Morale collapsed, and the militia melted away.

sentences.zh: 賊再攻州，抵拒經月，省兵竟無援救，城陷，屠民數万。

translations.literal: Rebels again attacked the prefecture; resistance lasted a month; provincial troops ultimately had no rescue; the city fell, and civilians were slaughtered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came again. The town held for a month. Provincial troops never came. The city fell, and tens of thousands of civilians were butchered.

sentences.zh: 向使練丁尚存，何致慘禍如此？

translations.literal: Had the drill soldiers remained, how could such cruel calamity have come?
translations.idiomatic: If those militiamen had still stood, how could disaster have fallen so hard?

sentences.zh: 五年，饒州、廣信之失，鄱陽、興安之失，陳啟邁通融入奏，寬減處分。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, with the loss of Raozhou and Guangxin and the loss of Poyang and Xing'an, Chen Qimai memorialized smooth falsehoods and received leniently reduced penalties.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Raozhou and Guangxin fell, then Poyang and Xing'an. Chen Qimai sent in smooth lies and saw his punishment eased.

sentences.zh: 萬載之失，知縣李峼有避賊重咎，舉人彭壽頤有勦賊殊功，奸民彭三才有餽賊實據，陳啟邁竟袒庇屬僚，架誣團練義士。

translations.literal: At the loss of Wanzai, Magistrate Li Kun had grave guilt for avoiding rebels, Presented Scholar Peng Shouyi had extraordinary merit in suppressing rebels, and wicked civilian Peng Sancai had solid evidence of feeding rebels—yet Chen Qimai sheltered subordinates and framed militia righteous men.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanzai fell, Magistrate Li Kun deserved blame for fleeing the rebels, Peng Shouyi deserved honor for fighting them, and the rogue Peng Sancai had proof of supplying the enemy. Yet Chen Qimai shielded his men and framed the militia heroes.

sentences.zh: 餽賊不斥，避賊不劾，獨於勦賊者，目為豺狼，指為逆黨。

translations.literal: Feeding rebels was not denounced; avoiding rebels was not impeached—only toward those suppressing rebels did he call them wolves and point to them as a rebel faction.
translations.idiomatic: Men who fed the rebels went untouched. Men who ran from them were not punished. Only those who fought the rebels he called wolves and traitors.

sentences.zh: 臬司惲光宸，逢迎喜怒，褫革逮拘，酷暑重刑，百端凌虐。

translations.literal: Provincial judge Yun Guangchen courted moods of joy and anger, stripped rank, arrested and detained him, imposed heavy punishment in midsummer heat, and abused him in a hundred ways.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial judge Yun Guangchen played to every whim. He stripped Shouyi of rank, seized him, tortured him in the summer heat, and tormented him without end.

sentences.zh: 臣以壽頤才識卓越深沉，疊商留營效用，陳啟邁堅僻不悟，釀成冤獄。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that Shouyi's talent and insight were outstanding and profound, that repeated deliberation had kept him in camp to good effect, yet Chen Qimai remained obstinate and unrepentant and brewed a miscarriage of justice.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that Peng Shouyi was a man of rare depth and ability, whose worth the army had proved again and again; Chen Qimai's stubborn blindness turned that merit into a wrongful conviction.

sentences.zh: 義寧之團，以保舉不公毀於前；

translations.literal: The Yining militia had already been ruined before by unfair recommendations;
translations.idiomatic: First the Yining corps was broken by biased promotions;

sentences.zh: 萬載之團，又以訟獄顛倒毀於繼。

translations.literal: the Wanzai militia was in turn ruined afterward by lawsuits and judgments turned upside down.
translations.idiomatic: then the Wanzai corps was undone by lawsuits and verdicts stood on their head.

sentences.zh: 人心何由固結？

translations.literal: How can hearts be bound firm?
translations.idiomatic: How then can loyalty be knit together?

sentences.zh: 大局恐致貽誤。」

translations.literal: The larger situation may suffer delay and harm.
translations.idiomatic: The wider war effort may be put at grave risk.

sentences.zh: 奉諭：「陳啟邁革職，惲光宸交新任巡撫文俊查辦。」

translations.literal: Imperial command: 'Chen Qimai is dismissed from office; Yun Guangchen is handed over to the new governor Wen Jun for investigation.'
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered: Chen Qimai stripped of his post; Yun Guangchen remanded to the incoming governor Wen Jun for inquiry.

sentences.zh: 壽頤早以刑斃矣。

translations.literal: Shouyi had long since been put to death by execution.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shouyi had already been executed.

sentences.zh: 南昌梅啟照嘗云：「國籓雅度無怒容，惟於壽頤逮獄，深為憤痛。」

translations.literal: Mei Qizhao of Nanchang once said: 'The Prince carried himself with easy grace and never showed anger, yet when Shouyi was seized and imprisoned he was deeply aggrieved.'
translations.idiomatic: Mei Qizhao of Nanchang recalled: 'Our Prince was mildness itself—yet the arrest of Shouyi filled him with bitter grief.'

sentences.zh: 七年，劉長佑敗，新喻、袁州三縣民率丁壯助軍，軍复振，世益以此思壽頤。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Liu Changyou was defeated; the people of Xinyu and the three counties of Yuanzhou led able-bodied men to aid the army, and the army revived; the world increasingly thought of Shouyi on this account.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, after Liu Changyou's defeat, the men of Xinyu and Yuanzhou rallied their young men to the colors and the army rose again—and men everywhere remembered what Shouyi might have done.

sentences.zh: 陳介眉，山東濰縣人。

translations.literal: Chen Jiemei, a native of Weixian in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jiemei was from Weixian, Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道光十八年拔貢生，朝考用知縣，發江蘇，署宿遷、鹽城等縣，擢通州知州。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Daoguang he was selected as a tribute student; the palace examination appointed him magistrate; he was posted to Jiangsu, acted as magistrate of Suqian, Yancheng, and other counties, and was promoted to prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Made a tribute student in Daoguang 18, he passed the palace examination for the magistracy, served in Jiangsu at Suqian and Yancheng among other posts, and rose to prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 屢獲海洋巨盜，擢知府，授河南歸德府知府。

translations.literal: He repeatedly captured great sea pirates, was promoted to prefect, and was appointed prefect of Guide Prefecture in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He took major pirates on the coast more than once, was raised to prefect, and received Guide Prefecture in Henan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，捻匪竄虞城之楊家集，介眉督兵追殲三百餘，生擒二百餘。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng Nian rebels raided Yangjiaji in Yucheng; Jiemei led troops in pursuit and annihilated more than three hundred and took more than two hundred alive.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 the Nian struck Yangjiaji in Yucheng; Jiemei pursued them, killed over three hundred, and captured more than two hundred.

sentences.zh: 粵賊陷歸德，褫職回籍。

translations.literal: Taiping rebels captured Guide; he was stripped of office and returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taiping took Guide he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 十一年，捻匪竄山東，抵濰縣，介眉迎剿，與候選訓導陳威鳳、武舉譚占元等，均力竭陣亡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Nian rebels raided Shandong and reached Weixian; Jiemei met them in suppression; with the candidate instructor Chen Weifeng, the military graduate Tan Zhanyuan, and others, all exhausted their strength and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Nian entered Shandong and came to Weixian; Jiemei went out to fight them alongside Chen Weifeng and Tan Zhanyuan—and all died where they stood when strength failed.

sentences.zh: 復原官，卹贈太僕寺卿銜，賞世職，建專祠，並祀威鳳、占元及同日陣亡之武生千總銜陳執蒲等。

translations.literal: His original rank was restored; he was posthumously given the rank of vice minister of the Imperial Stud, granted a hereditary office, and a dedicated temple was built; Weifeng, Zhanyuan, and the military student with battalion-commander rank Chen Zhipu, who fell the same day, were enshrined with him.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was restored, he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, granted a hereditary title, and given a temple of his own; Chen Weifeng, Tan Zhanyuan, and Chen Zhipu, who died the same day, were worshipped beside him.

sentences.zh: 同縣人亓祈年，道光五年舉人，截取知縣。

translations.literal: A fellow townsman, Qi Qinian, a provincial graduate in the fifth year of Daoguang, selected for appointment as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Of the same county was Qi Qinian, juren in Daoguang 5, on the list for a magistracy.

sentences.zh: 捻匪熾，祈年治西鄉團練，匪竄縣境，祈年登圩固守。

translations.literal: When the Nian grew fierce, Qinian organized militia training in the western townships; when rebels raided the county border he mounted the stockade and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: As the Nian flared, Qinian drilled the western townships; when they crossed the border he manned the stockade and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 圩破，率眾巷戰，力竭被縛，罵賊不屈死，侄文豐等同時陣亡。

translations.literal: The stockade was breached; he led the crowd in street fighting; his strength spent, he was bound; he cursed the rebels and died unbowed; his nephew Wenfeng and others fell in battle at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: The wall gave way; he fought house to house until spent, was taken, and reviled the rebels to his last breath; his nephew Wenfeng and others died with him.

sentences.zh: 卹贈道銜，賞世職，建專祠，文豐等附。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given circuit-intendant rank, granted a hereditary office, and a dedicated temple was built; Wenfeng and others were attached in worship.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made a circuit intendant, given a hereditary office and a temple; Wenfeng and the rest were honored there as well.

sentences.zh: 唐守忠，鉅野人。

translations.literal: Tang Shouzhong, a native of Juye.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shouzhong was from Juye.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，為平陽屯々官。

translations.literal: In the early Xianfeng period he served as an official of the Pingyang garrison colony.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng he held office in the Pingyang garrison lands.

sentences.zh: 四年，粵賊陷鉅野，土匪竊發，守忠聞警馳歸，遭匪劫，僅以身免。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Taiping rebels captured Juye and local bandits rose in secret; Shouzhong heard the alarm and galloped home, was robbed by bandits, and barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Taiping took Juye while local bandits stirred; Shouzhong raced home on the news, was waylaid, and barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 與鄉人生員張桂梯、職員姚鴻傑等議舉團練，為守衛計。

translations.literal: With the fellow townsman student Zhang Guidi, the clerk Yao Hongjie, and others he discussed raising militia training as a plan for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He met with the student Zhang Guidi, the clerk Yao Hongjie, and other townsmen to raise a militia for the county's defense.

sentences.zh: 旬日集義勇五千餘人，分三隊，捕斬土匪數十名，賊遂遁，嘉祥、鉅野間悉平。

translations.literal: Within ten days he gathered more than five thousand braves, divided them into three companies, captured and beheaded dozens of local bandits, the rebels then fled, and the region between Jiaxiang and Juye was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In ten days he mustered five thousand volunteers in three columns, hunted down dozens of bandits, drove the rebels off, and cleared the country between Jiaxiang and Juye.

sentences.zh: 土匪懼，以所劫物展轉還守忠，並乞隨團勦賊，誓不為亂，守忠察其誠，納之。

translations.literal: The local bandits feared; they returned what they had looted to Shouzhong by roundabout means and begged to follow the militia in suppressing rebels, swearing not to rebel again; Shouzhong perceived their sincerity and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits, afraid, sent back their plunder and asked to march with the militia against the rebels, vowing never to rise again; Shouzhong judged them sincere and took them in.

sentences.zh: 時年飢人乏食，守忠使子錫齡偕張桂梯各村勸捐助賑，富出貲，貧出丁，括計餘糧，計月分給，謂之均糧，而團練之勢愈固。

translations.literal: At the time it was a famine year and people lacked food; Shouzhong sent his son Xiling with Zhang Guidi village by village to urge donations for relief; the rich gave money, the poor gave men; surplus grain was tallied and apportioned monthly—called 'equalized grain'—and the militia grew ever firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Famine had emptied the granaries; Shouzhong sent Xiling and Zhang Guidi from village to village to levy relief—the wealthy in cash, the poor in labor—pooling grain for monthly shares called junliang, and the militia's hold tightened.

sentences.zh: 曹州、濟寧兩屬鄉團來附，賊不得逞，去。

translations.literal: Township militias of Caozhou and Jining came to attach; the rebels could not prevail and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Militias from Caozhou and Jining joined him; the rebels found no opening and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五年，河決銅瓦廂，鄆城、鉅野、嘉祥等縣當其衝，守忠聞豐工黃水下游淤涸成灘，官出示招墾，因率災民數万人南下認種。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Yellow River broke at Tongwaxiang; Yuncheng, Juye, Jiaxiang, and other counties bore the brunt; Shouzhong heard that below the Fenggong works the Yellow River's waters had silted up and dried into shoals, the government posted notices inviting reclamation, and he therefore led tens of thousands of disaster victims south to claim land for planting.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the river burst at Tongwaxiang and Yuncheng, Juye, and Jiaxiang lay in its path; learning that below the Fenggong works the Yellow River had silted into dry shoals and the authorities were calling for settlers, he led tens of thousands of refugees south to open new fields.

sentences.zh: 仿屯田法，以教諭王孚、千總唐振海等分領之，名曰湖團，亙二百餘裡，濬溝築圩，編保甲，嚴守望。

translations.literal: Modeling on the garrison-field system, with the instructor Wang Fu, the battalion commander Tang Zhenhai, and others dividing command, it was named the Lake Militia; it spanned more than two hundred li, dredged ditches, built stockades, organized baojia, and kept strict watch.
translations.idiomatic: On the model of military colonies he put Wang Fu, Tang Zhenhai, and others in charge of sections called the Lake Corps, two hundred li long—ditches dug, walls raised, baojia registered, watches kept night and day.

sentences.zh: 徐州、蕭、碭、豐、沛等縣人聞賊警，則相率投避，得免於難者數年。

translations.literal: When people of Xuzhou, Xiao, Dang, Feng, Pei, and other counties heard rebel alarms they would band together to seek refuge and were spared disaster for several years.
translations.idiomatic: For years, at the first rumor of rebels, families from Xuzhou, Xiao, Dang, Feng, Pei, and the rest fled to the Lake Corps and were spared.

sentences.zh: 八年，捻匪來犯，守忠率團遮擊，擒賊樊三、丁豹等斬之，敘功給五品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Nian rebels came to attack; Shouzhong led the militia to intercept, captured the rebels Fan San and Ding Bao and others and beheaded them, and his merit was recorded with a fifth-rank hat button.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Nian attacked; Shouzhong met them, took Fan San and Ding Bao and other rebel chiefs and beheaded them, and was rewarded with a fifth-rank button.

sentences.zh: 十年，欽差大臣僧格林沁令守忠隨官軍助剿，敗賊大劉莊。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the imperial commissioner Senggelinqin ordered Shouzhong to follow the regular armies in assisting suppression; he defeated the rebels at Daliuzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Senggelinqin had him march with the regulars; he helped rout the rebels at Daliuzhuang.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，捐助軍餉，又捐已墾熟田為魚台書院經費。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he contributed military funds and also donated already reclaimed mature fields for the expenses of Yutai Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1 he gave money to the army and set aside reclaimed farmland to endow the Yutai Academy.

sentences.zh: 二年，白蓮池教匪由滕縣偷渡湖西，守忠截擊，生擒賊目陳周等多名，餘匪悉遁。

translations.literal: In the second year White Lotus sect rebels from Teng county secretly crossed west of the lake; Shouzhong intercepted them, took alive the rebel leader Chen Zhou and many others, and the remaining rebels all fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year sect rebels from Teng slipped west across the lake; Shouzhong cut them off, seized Chen Zhou and other chiefs alive, and the rest scattered.

sentences.zh: 四年九月，捻匪張總愚、任柱等悉眾來攻，守忠集丁堵禦，一再請援兵不至，力戰六日，眾寡不敵，死之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year the Nian leaders Zhang Zong'en, Ren Zhu, and others mustered all their forces to attack; Shouzhong gathered men to block them, repeatedly requested reinforcements that did not arrive, fought fiercely for six days, was outnumbered, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year Zhang Zong'en and Ren Zhu brought the full Nian host; Shouzhong walled up with what men he had, called again and again for help that never came, fought six days against hopeless odds, and fell.

sentences.zh: 方守忠被圍，賊數使招降，守忠誓死拒之。

translations.literal: While Shouzhong was besieged the rebels repeatedly sent to summon his surrender; he swore to die and refused.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege tightened the rebels sent envoys to offer terms; he vowed to die rather than yield.

sentences.zh: 及戰敗，與族叔千總振海、子生員錫彤同被執。

translations.literal: When the battle was lost, he, his clan uncle the battalion commander Zhenhai, and his son the student Xitong were seized together.
translations.idiomatic: When the line broke, he was taken with his kinsman Zhenhai, a battalion officer, and his son Xitong, a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 賊舁至銅山袁家廟，多方脅之降，守忠罵不絕口，遂並見害。

translations.literal: The rebels carried them to Yuanjia Temple in Tongshan and from many sides coerced them to surrender; Shouzhong cursed without cease, and all were then killed.
translations.idiomatic: They were dragged to Yuanjia Temple in Tongshan and pressed from every side to submit; Shouzhong never stopped reviling them, and all three were slain.

sentences.zh: 江督曾國籓疏請優恤，建祠立傳，從之，贈道銜。

translations.literal: Jiangsu Governor Zeng Guofan memorialized requesting superior condolence, a temple, and a biography; the request was granted and circuit-intendant rank was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan asked the throne for full honors, a shrine, and a biography; the court agreed and made him a circuit intendant posthumously.

sentences.zh: 子錫彤，照四品以下陣亡例議卹，給世職。

translations.literal: His son Xitong, according to the regulations for death in battle below the fourth rank, was considered for condolence and granted a hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xitong was mourned under the rules for officers below the fourth rank who die in battle and given a hereditary title.

sentences.zh: 尋在沛縣捐建專祠。

translations.literal: Soon afterward a dedicated temple was built by donation in Pei county.
translations.idiomatic: A private temple was later raised for him in Pei county.

sentences.zh: 吳山，字岩青，河南光山人。

translations.literal: Wu Shan, style Yanging, a native of Guangshan in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shan, styled Yanging, came from Guangshan in Henan.

sentences.zh: 生三日喪父，母周守節撫孤，家極貧，紡績供山讀書。

translations.literal: Three days after his birth his father died; his mother Zhou kept her widowhood and raised the orphan; the family was extremely poor; she spun to supply Shan's studies.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at three days old; his mother Zhou kept her chastity and reared him in bitter poverty, spinning to pay for his books.

sentences.zh: 道光二十五年，舉於鄉，會試不第，留京三載，與袁保恆、裴季芳相切磋，聲譽日起。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang he passed the provincial examination; he failed the metropolitan examination, stayed in the capital three years, and with Yuan Baoheng and Pei Jifang sharpened one another; his reputation rose day by day.
translations.idiomatic: He became a provincial graduate in Daoguang 25, failed the palace exam, and spent three years in Beijing studying with Yuan Baoheng and Pei Jifang until his name was widely known.

sentences.zh: 時光山有匪患，山以寡母在堂，二子尚幼，又無期功強近之親，就揀選知縣職，倉卒歸。

translations.literal: At the time Guangshan had a bandit scourge; Shan, because his widowed mother was alive, his two sons were still young, and he had no close kin of mourning grade, took a selected magistrate post and returned in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was rife in Guangshan; with an aged mother, small sons, and no near kin to rely on, he accepted a magistracy on the selection list and hurried home.

sentences.zh: 先是，邑民郭三，兇黠。

translations.literal: Earlier, a townsman named Guo San was fierce and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Before this a local man, Guo San, had been violent and sly.

sentences.zh: 兄弟七人，郭五、郭六尤悍。

translations.literal: There were seven brothers; Guo Wu and Guo Liu were especially fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Seven brothers in all—Guo Wu and Guo Liu the fiercest.

sentences.zh: 郭三充縣皁役，滿佈黨與。

translations.literal: Guo San served as a county runner and spread his partisans everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Guo San held a post as county runner and filled the yamen with his men.

sentences.zh: 知縣水安瀾恇懦，為郭三等挾制，無所不至。

translations.literal: Magistrate Shui Anlan was timid and weak and was controlled by Guo San and others; nothing was beyond them.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Shui Anlan was a coward in Guo San's grip; nothing was beyond their reach.

sentences.zh: 彼時有「郭滿城」之謠。

translations.literal: At that time there was a saying: 'Guo fills the city.'
translations.idiomatic: People said in those days, 'Guo owns the town.'

sentences.zh: 郭三充臥龍臺鄉保，倡首為匪，向四楞子、曾傳佐等，皆領桿頭目，肆行劫掠，並至各鄉按畝加糧供食，並勾通亳、壽各州各匪，謀殺官起事。

translations.literal: Guo San served as baojia head at Wolongtai and took the lead as a bandit; Xiang Silengzi, Zeng Chuanzuo, and others were all gang-pole leaders who plundered at will, went to each township levying grain per mu for food, and colluded with bandits of Bozhou, Shouzhou, and various prefectures, plotting to kill officials and raise a rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: As headman at Wolongtai he led the outlaws; Silengzi, Zeng Chuanzuo, and others commanded armed bands, extorted grain from every village, and conspired with ruffians in Bozhou and Shouzhou to murder officials and rise in revolt.

sentences.zh: 山有鄉望，眾舉為團首，倡辦團練，地方恃以安，而郭三忌之。

translations.literal: Shan had standing in the countryside; the people elected him militia head and he initiated militia training; the locality relied on this for peace, but Guo San resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Shan was respected in the district and was made head of the militia; the country rested easier for it, and Guo San hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年四月，郭三糾眾突至小向店派糧，山拒而不納，尋，集鄉團與之抗。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Xianfeng Guo San gathered a crowd and suddenly came to Xiaoxiangdian to levy grain; Shan refused to accept it; soon he gathered the township militia to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Xianfeng 4, Guo San marched on Xiaoxiangdian to seize grain; Shan turned him away and mustered the township guard to fight.

sentences.zh: 匪巢臥龍台，距小向家集僅十二里，郭三揚言非殺山不可。

translations.literal: The bandit nest was at Wolongtai, only twelve li from Xiaoxiangjiaji; Guo San proclaimed that unless Shan was killed it would not do.
translations.idiomatic: Their stronghold at Wolongtai lay only twelve li from Xiaoxiangjiaji; Guo San swore Shan must die.

sentences.zh: 或有勸山走避者，山曰：「我所以觸匪怒者，原以抗匪派糧，若臨難而逃，任匪所為，則初志謂何？

translations.literal: Some urged Shan to flee; Shan said: 'The reason I provoked the bandits' anger was originally to resist their grain levy; if at the crisis I flee and let the bandits have their way, what becomes of my first intent?
translations.idiomatic: Friends begged him to run; he answered: 'I angered them by refusing their levy—if I bolt now and leave the countryside to them, what was the point?

sentences.zh: 今日之事，有死而已。」

translations.literal: Today's affair admits only death.
translations.idiomatic: Today there is nothing left but to die.'

sentences.zh: 遂挺身督鄉團與戰，眾寡不敵，被擒，山罵不絕口，匪怒戕之。

translations.literal: He then personally led the township militia into battle; outnumbered, he was captured; Shan cursed without cease, and the bandits in anger killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He led the militia out himself, was overwhelmed and taken, and cursed them to the end; they slew him in fury.

sentences.zh: 後俞御史劉毓楠奏建專祠。

translations.literal: Later Censor Liu Yunan memorialized to build a dedicated temple.
translations.idiomatic: Later Censor Liu Yunan asked that a temple be built to him.

sentences.zh: 俞焜，字昆上，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Yu Kun, style Kunshang, a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kun, styled Kunshang, was from Qiantang, Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十五年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A graduate of the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing; transferred to Hanlin bachelor; appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi in Jiaqing 25; entered the Hanlin as a bachelor and became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 道光十三年，遷御史，奏請申明律義，以正倫紀，略言：「律載'弟妹毆同胞兄姊死者皆斬'。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang he was transferred to censor and memorialized requesting clarification of the law's meaning to rectify human relations, stating in summary: 'The Code provides: younger siblings who beat full-blood elder brother or sister to death—all are decapitated.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 13 he became a censor and urged that the law be stated plainly to uphold the bonds of kin, writing in part: 'The Code says that a younger brother or sister who beats a full sibling to death shall be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 注云：'毆死期親尊長，若分首從，則倫常斁矣。

translations.literal: The annotation states: 'Beating to death a senior of the mourning grade—if one distinguishes principal and accessory, then the normal relations are overturned.'
translations.idiomatic: The commentary explains: 'To beat to death a senior within the mourning circle—if one splits ringleader from follower, the moral order itself is undone.'

sentences.zh: '此古今定律，所以維名教也。

translations.literal: This is the fixed law of ancient and modern times, by which orthodox teaching is maintained.
translations.idiomatic: That statute, old as the dynasties, is what holds civilization upright.

sentences.zh: 其聽從尊長，毆死以次期親尊長之犯，向律擬斬，定案時夾簽聲請，疊經改為斬監候，歸入服制情實。

translations.literal: Offenders who obeyed a senior and beat to death the next senior of the mourning grade were under the Code originally subject to decapitation; at sentencing a folded petition might be submitted; repeatedly this was changed to suspended decapitation and entered under mourning-grade substantial circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Those who, obeying an elder, killed the next senior in line were once sentenced to immediate beheading; memorials on folded slips had again and again commuted that to imprisonment, treating the case as a matter of family obligation.

sentences.zh: 自道光三年御史萬方雍奏，將聽從尊長，毆死以次期親尊長，下手傷輕之卑幼，均科傷罪。

translations.literal: From the memorial of Censor Wan Fangyong in the third year of Daoguang, juniors who obeyed a senior and beat to death the next senior of the mourning grade but whose own blows were light were all sentenced merely as assault.
translations.idiomatic: Since Daoguang 3, when Censor Wan Fangyong proposed it, a junior who struck lightly while obeying an elder and killed the next senior was punished only as for ordinary assault.

sentences.zh: 刑部定為條例，至今沿之。

translations.literal: The Board of Punishments fixed this as a sub-statute, and it has been followed to this day.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice made that a regulation, and it has stood ever since.

sentences.zh: 因思例從律出，例因時變通，律一成不易。

translations.literal: Reflecting that sub-statutes derive from the Code, sub-statutes vary with the times, but the Code once fixed does not change.
translations.idiomatic: Sub-statutes grow out of the Code and may bend with the age; the Code itself does not bend.

sentences.zh: 致死尊長，豈得仍論傷之重輕？
