translations.literal: When a senior has been killed, how can one still weigh the lightness or heaviness of the wounds?
translations.idiomatic: When a kinsman lies dead, can the court still weigh how hard the blow was?

sentences.zh: 今以勉從尊長，下手傷輕，止科傷罪，則與'死者皆斬'之律未符。

translations.literal: Now, because one reluctantly obeyed a senior and one's own blows were light, to impose only an assault sentence is incompatible with the Code's 'all who die are decapitated.'
translations.idiomatic: To punish reluctant obedience with a light hand as mere assault is to empty the words 'all who die are beheaded.'

sentences.zh: 此例既百無一抵，何以肅典​​刑而正人心？

translations.literal: Since this sub-statute matches scarcely one case in a hundred, how can canonical punishment be solemnized and hearts rectified?
translations.idiomatic: A rule that almost never applies cannot awe the realm or set men's hearts right.

sentences.zh: 請仍遵不分首從本律，夾簽聲請，以昭平允。」

translations.literal: I request that the original Code without distinction of principal and accessory still be followed, with folded petitions submitted, to manifest fairness.'
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the original statute be restored without distinction of roles, with mercy sought by memorial as of old, so that justice may be seen to be even-handed.'

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The ministry discussed and implemented it.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries deliberated and carried his recommendation into effect.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授河南彰德府知府，以東河大工勞最，用道員，擢永定河道。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed prefect of Zhangde in Henan; for foremost labor on the great Eastern River works he was used as a circuit intendant and promoted to superintendent of the Yongding River.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he became prefect of Zhangde in Henan; his work on the Eastern River earned him a circuit post and then the Yongding River superintendency.

sentences.zh: 調衡永郴桂道，緣事降調。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Heng-Yong-Chen-Gui circuit and, on account of an affair, was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the Heng-Yong-Chen-Gui circuit and later reduced in rank after a dispute.

sentences.zh: 咸豐九年，督辦團練，操防勤奮，復道銜。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xianfeng he supervised militia training; drill and defense were diligent and assiduous, and his circuit-intendant rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 9 he took charge of the militia, drilled them tirelessly, and regained his circuit rank.

sentences.zh: 十年，粵賊亂熾，焜商遣駐防軍守獨松關，李秀成犯杭，焜與侍郎戴熙登陴拒守二十餘日。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Taiping rebellion burned fierce; Kun consulted and dispatched garrison troops to hold Dusong Pass; Li Xiucheng attacked Hangzhou; Kun with Vice Minister Dai Xi mounted the walls and held defense for more than twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, as the Taiping flared, Kun posted garrison troops at Dusong Pass; when Li Xiucheng struck Hangzhou he and Vice Minister Dai Xi held the walls for more than twenty days.

sentences.zh: 城陷，巡撫羅遵殿殉之。

translations.literal: The city fell; Governor Luo Zundian died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell and Governor Luo Zundian perished with it.

sentences.zh: 焜憑柵堵禦，與滿城犄角，復相持五日。

translations.literal: Kun relied on the palisade to block the enemy, supported the Manchu city at a corner, and held on another five days.
translations.idiomatic: Kun fought from the barricades in concert with the Manchu quarter and held out five days more.

sentences.zh: 彈盡，柵毀，賊眾，焜猶手刃數賊，矛洞胸，歿於陣。

translations.literal: Ammunition was spent, the palisade destroyed, rebels were numerous; Kun still personally slew several rebels; a spear pierced his chest and he died in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Shot and timber gone, the rebels pressing in, he still cut down several with his own hand before a spear took him in the chest.

sentences.zh: 明日，張玉良援師入，將軍瑞昌會擊，賊卻而焜已死。

translations.literal: The next day Zhang Yuliang's relief army entered; General Ruichang joined the attack; the rebels retreated, but Kun was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Zhang Yuliang's relief came up and General Ruichang struck together; the rebels drew off—but Kun was already dead.

sentences.zh: 論者謂滿城之存，焜有力焉。

translations.literal: Commentators say that the Manchu city's survival owed much to Kun's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Men said the Manchu city still stood because Kun had held the line.

sentences.zh: 賜諡文節，建專祠。

translations.literal: He was granted the posthumous name Wenjie and a dedicated temple was built.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave him the posthumous name Wenjie and a temple of his own.

sentences.zh: 同殉之繼室陳氏，女蘊祺、蘊璿附祀。

translations.literal: His second wife Chen, who died with him, and his daughters Yunqi and Yunxuan were attached in worship.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Chen and his daughters Yunqi and Yunxuan, who died with him, were honored in the same shrine.

sentences.zh: 同縣戴煦，字鄂士。

translations.literal: A fellow townsman, Dai Xu, style Eshi.
translations.idiomatic: Of the same county was Dai Xu, styled Eshi.

sentences.zh: 增貢生。

translations.literal: Enrolled tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: An enrolled tribute student.

sentences.zh: 候選訓導。

translations.literal: Candidate instructor.
translations.idiomatic: A candidate for instructor.

sentences.zh: 精算術。

translations.literal: Expert in mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: A master of mathematics.

sentences.zh: 西人艾約瑟見煦所著求表捷術，心折之。

translations.literal: The Western scholar Joseph Edkins, reading Xu's Composition on Quick Methods for Finding Tables, was deeply impressed.
translations.idiomatic: The missionary Joseph Edkins read his Quick Methods for Finding Tables and was overcome with admiration.

sentences.zh: 又工畫，神似倪迂，評者謂出乃兄熙上。

translations.literal: He was also skilled at painting, in spirit akin to Ni Zan; critics said he surpassed his elder brother Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He painted too, in the manner of Ni Zan; connoisseurs held him above his brother Xi.

sentences.zh: 熙既投水殉節，聞之歎曰：「吾兄得死所矣！」

translations.literal: Xi having drowned himself to die for principle, Xu heard it and sighed: 'My elder brother has found the place to die!'
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Xi had drowned himself in martyrdom, Xu sighed: 'My brother has found the death that suits him!'

sentences.zh: 亦投井死。

translations.literal: He too threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself down a well and followed him.

sentences.zh: 著有莊子順文，陶靖節集註，四元玉鑑細草，對數簡法諸書。

translations.literal: He authored Zhuangzi Shunwen, Annotated Collected Works of Tao Qian, Fine Draft of the Jade Mirror of the Four Origins, Brief Method of Logarithms, and other books.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include Zhuangzi Shunwen, notes on Tao Qian, a commentary on the Jade Mirror of the Four Origins, and treatises on logarithms.

sentences.zh: 熙自有傳。

translations.literal: Xi has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Xi has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 張洵，字肖眉，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xun, style Xiaomei, a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun, styled Xiaomei, was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年進士，改庶吉士，授編修，命在上書房行走，文淵閣校理。

translations.literal: A graduate of the second year of Xianfeng; transferred to Hanlin bachelor; appointed compiler; ordered to serve in the Upper Study Hall; collator of the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi in Xianfeng 2; Hanlin bachelor; compiler; attached to the Upper Study Hall and the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 十年，粵匪由安徽竄浙江，杭州省城被圍，巡撫羅遵殿奏入，洵請假省親。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Taiping from Anhui raided Zhejiang; the Hangzhou provincial city was besieged; Governor Luo Zundian's memorial arrived; Xun requested leave to visit his family.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Taiping swept from Anhui into Zhejiang and besieged Hangzhou; when Luo Zundian's report reached court, Xun asked leave to go home.

sentences.zh: 上召見，垂詢浙省軍情。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned him for audience and inquired about the military situation in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor received him and questioned him closely on Zhejiang's armies.

sentences.zh: 洵抵浙江，杭州失而旋复。

translations.literal: Xun reached Zhejiang; Hangzhou had been lost and was soon recovered.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Xun arrived, Hangzhou had fallen and been retaken.

sentences.zh: 先是洵母談氏，因賊逼杭城，率洵妻施氏，洵子惇典、從典、敘典、念典，女喜姑闔門赴水，被救得不死。

translations.literal: Earlier Xun's mother, of the Tan clan, because rebels pressed Hangzhou, led Xun's wife Shi, his sons Dundian, Congdian, Xudian, and Niandian, and his daughter Xigu—the whole household into the water; they were rescued and did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Before that, when the rebels closed on Hangzhou, his mother Lady Tan led his wife Lady Shi, their sons Dundian, Congdian, Xudian, and Niandian, and their daughter Xigu into the river; all were pulled out alive.

sentences.zh: 施氏即命惇典、念典等護其姑出城。

translations.literal: Lady Shi immediately ordered Dundian, Niandian, and the others to escort their mother-in-law out of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shi at once sent Dundian, Niandian, and the rest to guard their mother-in-law out of the city.

sentences.zh: 賊至，施氏遣喜姑先投井死，自率敘典躍池中殉焉。

translations.literal: When rebels arrived, Shi sent Xigu first to throw herself into a well and die; she herself led Xudian to leap into a pool and die with her.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels came, Lady Shi sent Xigu first into a well, then led Xudian into a pool and died beside her.

sentences.zh: 杭州將軍瑞昌以聞，上嘉施氏孝義兼全，下部旌卹。

translations.literal: The Hangzhou general Ruichang reported it; the Emperor praised Shi's perfect fulfillment of filial piety and righteousness and ordered commendation and posthumous grants from the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: General Ruichang of Hangzhou reported the matter; the throne praised Lady Shi's perfect filial piety and righteousness and ordered the ministry to honor and comfort her kin.

sentences.zh: 尋，洵母自以老需人侍奉，為洵繼娶勞氏。

translations.literal: Before long, Xun's mother, considering herself old and in need of attendance, secured a second wife for Xun, of the Lao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Xun's mother, finding herself old and in need of care, arranged a second marriage for him to a woman of the Lao clan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁母憂，洵省城無房產，僦居於仁和縣之永泰鎮。

translations.literal: Not long after, he entered mourning for his mother; Xun had no property in the provincial city and rented a dwelling in Yongtai Town, Renhe County.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was in mourning for his mother; he owned no house in the capital and rented lodgings in Yongtai Town, Renhe County.

sentences.zh: 十一年，賊大股复犯浙江，餘杭、蕭山相繼失陷，省城被圍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year a large rebel force again invaded Zhejiang; Yuhang and Xiaoshan fell in succession, and the provincial city was besieged.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year a great rebel column struck Zhejiang again; Yuhang and Xiaoshan fell one after another, and the provincial city was besieged.

sentences.zh: 洵念受恩至重，不忍坐視，乃自永泰鎮挈眷赴省，與官紳籌守禦；

translations.literal: Xun, remembering how deeply he had been favored, could not bear to sit idle; he brought his family from Yongtai Town to the capital and joined officials and gentry in planning defense;
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of the depth of favor he had received, Xun could not sit idle; he led his household from Yongtai Town to the city and joined officials and gentry in planning its defense;

sentences.zh: 並謀諸巡撫王有齡，會合駐防兵，力通江路。

translations.literal: and also consulted the governor Wang Youling, mustering the garrison troops to force open the river route.
translations.idiomatic: and consulted Governor Wang Youling to gather the garrison troops and break the river line.

sentences.zh: 顧賊勢張甚，圍城兩月餘，城陷，洵與勞氏、惇典、從典、念典皆死之。

translations.literal: But rebel strength was overwhelming; after more than two months' siege the city fell, and Xun, Lady Lao, Dundian, Congdian, and Niandian all died.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rebel strength was overwhelming; after more than two months the city fell, and Xun, Lady Lao, Dundian, Congdian, and Niandian all perished.

sentences.zh: 洵兄濂之妻李氏及女九姑，亦先後殉焉。

translations.literal: The wife of Xun's elder brother Lianzhi, née Li, and her daughter Jiugu, also martyred themselves in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's sister-in-law, née Li, wife of his elder brother Lianzhi, and her daughter Jiugu likewise died for principle, one after another.

sentences.zh: 方城之垂陷也，洵聞警，即索衣冠北向叩頭畢，賦詩三絕，有「白雲堆裡吾將去，前輩風流有戴公」之句。

translations.literal: As the city was on the verge of falling, Xun heard the alarm, immediately sought out cap and gown, kowtowed to the north, finished three quatrains, including the line "Into the heap of white clouds I shall go—the elder generation's grace had Dai Gong."
translations.idiomatic: As the city neared its fall, Xun heard the alarm, donned cap and gown, kowtowed toward the north, and wrote three quatrains, one line reading: "Into the heap of white clouds I shall go—among the elders' grace there was Dai Gong."

sentences.zh: 書竟，授僕張昇，遂投井死。

translations.literal: When the writing was done, he handed it to his servant Zhang Sheng, then threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished writing, he gave the poems to his servant Zhang Sheng and threw himself down a well.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，太常寺卿許彭壽以聞，以「一門六口，同時殉難，實屬深明大義，忠烈可嘉」褒之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Minister of Rites Xu Pengshou reported it, praising with the words "six mouths in one household martyred together—truly deep understanding of great principle, loyalty and valor worthy of praise."
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1, Xu Pengshou of the Ministry of Rites reported the case, commending "six of one household martyred together—truly a grasp of great principle, loyalty and valor worthy of praise."

sentences.zh: 八年，國子監司業孫詒經復請加恩予諡建祠，允之，諡文節。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Vice-Director of the Imperial Academy Sun Yijing again requested added grace, a posthumous title, and a memorial hall; it was granted, with the posthumous title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Sun Yijing, vice-director of the Imperial Academy, again petitioned for added honors, a posthumous title, and a shrine; the request was granted, and he was given the posthumous title Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 鍾世耀，字嘯溪，仁和人。

translations.literal: Zhong Shiyao, style Xiaoxi, a native of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Shiyao, styled Xiaoxi, was from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年進士，改庶吉士，散館，授兵部主事。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the twenty-first year of Daoguang; transferred to Hanlin bachelor; after leaving the academy, appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi in Daoguang 21; Hanlin bachelor; after leaving the academy he was made a principal secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 移疾歸，負鄉望，城再陷，賊將授以偽官，絕粒殉節。

translations.literal: He returned on grounds of illness, bearing the town's esteem; when the city fell again, rebels were about to grant him a false office; he starved himself to die for principle.
translations.idiomatic: He went home on grounds of illness, a man of standing in his county; when the city fell again the rebels offered him a post in their regime; he starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 孫義，字樸堂，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Sun Yi, style Putang, a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yi, styled Putang, was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 道光九年進士，官福建仙遊縣知縣，有循聲。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the ninth year of Daoguang; served as magistrate of Xianyou County in Fujian, with a reputation for benevolent rule.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi in Daoguang 9; magistrate of Xianyou in Fujian, with a reputation for humane government.

sentences.zh: 告歸後，課徒自給，同時殉難。

translations.literal: After requesting leave to return home, he taught pupils to support himself and at the same time martyred himself.
translations.idiomatic: After he retired he taught pupils to live on and died a martyr when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 汪士驤，字鐵樵，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Wang Shixiang, style Tieqiao, a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shixiang, styled Tieqiao, was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 襲世職，授杭州營千總。

translations.literal: He inherited a hereditary office and was appointed company commander of the Hangzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited a hereditary post and was appointed company commander of the Hangzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 擅詩名，工篆隸，晚年作小楷尤精。

translations.literal: Renowned for poetry, skilled in seal and clerical script; in his later years his small regular script was especially fine.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed for poetry and skilled in seal and clerical script; in later years his small regular hand was especially fine.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十一年，賊再至，先以年老休致，居危城中，神色自若，日以忠義訓家人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng rebels came again; he had earlier retired on grounds of age; he dwelt in the endangered city with composed countenance, daily instructing his household in loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 11 the rebels returned; he had already retired on grounds of age, yet lived in the besieged city with unshaken composure, daily schooling his household in loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 賦詩有「我死家人生，辱家即辱我」等語。

translations.literal: In his poems were lines such as "If I die, my household lives; to shame the house is to shame me."
translations.idiomatic: In his poems he wrote lines such as: "If I die, my household lives; to shame the house is to shame me."

sentences.zh: 城破，全家皆躍水死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the whole household leapt into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, the whole household leapt into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 錢松，字叔蓋，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Qian Song, style Shugai, a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Song, styled Shugai, was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 嗜金石篆刻，有文譽。

translations.literal: Fond of bronze and stone and seal carving, with a literary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He loved bronzes, stones, and seal carving, and had a literary reputation.

sentences.zh: 賊初陷杭垣，先期具藥汁，誓死。

translations.literal: When rebels first took the Hangzhou walls, he had prepared draughts in advance, vowing death.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels first took Hangzhou, he had prepared poison in advance, resolved to die.

sentences.zh: 家傍清波門，賊從此入，遂與家人同仰藥，麾侍者還其室，曰：「今日得死所，而男女顛僕一室可乎？」

translations.literal: His home lay beside Qingbo Gate; rebels entered from there; he then drank the draught with his family, waved attendants back to their quarters, and said: "Today I have found the place to die—yet men and women should tumble together in one room, can that be?"
translations.idiomatic: His home stood by Qingbo Gate, where the rebels entered; he and his family drank the poison together, then sent the servants back to their quarters, saying: "Today I have found the death that suits me—yet should men and women lie heaped together in one room?"

sentences.zh: 語定而絕。

translations.literal: With the words settled, he expired.
translations.idiomatic: With that he fell silent and died.

sentences.zh: 毛雝，字西堂，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Mao Yong, style Xitang, a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Yong, styled Xitang, was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate.

sentences.zh: 事親孝。

translations.literal: Filial in serving his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He was filial toward his parents.

sentences.zh: 年十三，能作大字。

translations.literal: At thirteen he could write large characters.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he could write large characters.

sentences.zh: 工書，得潤筆盡給貧乏。

translations.literal: Skilled at calligraphy; whatever he received for brushwork he gave entirely to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at calligraphy, he gave every fee he earned to the poor.

sentences.zh: 督辦東北隅團練，城再陷，自縊死。

translations.literal: He supervised militia drill in the northeast quarter; when the city fell again, he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised militia drill in the northeast quarter; when the city fell again he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 魏謙升，字滋伯，仁和人。

translations.literal: Wei Qiansheng, style Zibo, a native of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qiansheng, styled Zibo, was from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 九歲能文，弱冠后雄長壇坫。

translations.literal: At nine he could compose essays; after coming of age he dominated the literary arena.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he could write essays; after coming of age he dominated the literary world.

sentences.zh: 尤工書。

translations.literal: Especially skilled at calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled at calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 以廩貢生選仙居縣訓導，不就。

translations.literal: As a senior licentiate he was selected for instructor of Xianju County but did not take the post.
translations.idiomatic: As a senior licentiate he was selected instructor of Xianju but declined.

sentences.zh: 家居西馬塍，以著述自娛，垂五十年，有書三味齋稿。

translations.literal: He lived at home in Ximacheng, amusing himself with writing for nearly fifty years; he had the book Drafts of the Three-Flavors Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at Ximacheng, amusing himself with writing for nearly fifty years; his works include Drafts of the Three-Flavors Studio.

sentences.zh: 賊自湖州逼省城，家當其衝，或諷宜移居避之，不應。

translations.literal: Rebels from Huzhou pressed the provincial city; his home lay in their path; some hinted he should move to avoid them; he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels from Huzhou pressed the capital, his home lay in their path; some urged him to move away, but he would not.

sentences.zh: 賊火其廬，乃挈妻子走靈隱山中。

translations.literal: Rebels burned his house; he then led wife and children to flee into Lingyin Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels burned his house; he led his wife and children into Lingyin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 賊退，僑寓城中，嘯歌不輟，自號無無居士。

translations.literal: When rebels withdrew, he lodged in the city, singing without cease, styling himself the Recluse of No-Nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels withdrew he lodged in the city, singing without cease, and styled himself the Recluse of No-Nothing.

sentences.zh: 城再陷，謙升方老病，驅至萬安橋下死，妻周氏同時殉節。

translations.literal: When the city fell again, Qiansheng was already old and ill; he was driven to Wan'an Bridge and died there; his wife, of the Zhou clan, martyred herself at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell again Qiansheng was old and ill; he was driven to Wan'an Bridge and killed; his wife Lady Zhou died with him.

sentences.zh: 週能書，世以鷗波夫婦擬之。

translations.literal: Zhou could write; the world compared them to the Ou Bo couple.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhou could write as well; people likened them to the Zhao Mengfu couple.

sentences.zh: 金鼎燮，字承高，秀水人。

translations.literal: Jin Dingsie, style Chenggao, a native of Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Dingsie, styled Chenggao, was from Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate.

sentences.zh: 咸豐季年，署臨安訓導兼教諭。

translations.literal: In the closing years of Xianfeng he served as acting instructor of Lin'an, also holding the post of director of studies.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Xianfeng he served as acting instructor and director of studies at Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 以事詣省城，寇至，圍久，糧絕，至煮篋上革以食。

translations.literal: On business he went to the provincial city; bandits came; the siege was long; grain ran out, until they boiled leather from trunks to eat.
translations.idiomatic: On business he went to the capital; when the rebels came the siege dragged on until food ran out and they boiled leather from trunks to eat.

sentences.zh: 城破，雜難民中出，至臨安，率鄉團禦寇，死之。

translations.literal: When the city fell he slipped out among refugees, reached Lin'an, led local militia to resist bandits, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he slipped out among the refugees, reached Lin'an, led local militia against the rebels, and died.

sentences.zh: 庚辛之役，省城再陷，杭人殉難者至眾，而旗營死事尤烈。

translations.literal: In the Gengxin campaigns the provincial city fell again; Hangzhou people who martyred themselves were very many, but the banner garrison's deaths in service were especially fierce.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaigns of 1860–61 the capital fell again; martyrs among the people of Hangzhou were countless, but the banner garrison's deaths were especially fierce.

sentences.zh: 其著者：協領巴圖蘭布等守花市營門，佐領德克登額、佛爾國納、德勒蘇等守錢塘門，呼松額、格勒蘇、印福等督隊出湧金門，皆迎戰，奮刀殺賊，先後陣亡。

translations.literal: Notable among them: Assistant Commandant Batulanbu and others held Huashi Camp Gate; Vice Commandants Dekedenge, Foerguona, Delesu, and others held Qiantang Gate; Husonge, Gelesu, Yinfu, and others led detachments out Yongjin Gate—all met the enemy, wielded blades fiercely to kill rebels, and fell in battle one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Among the most noted: Assistant Commandant Batulanbu and others held Huashi Camp Gate; Vice Commandants Dekedenge, Foerguona, and Delesu held Qiantang Gate; Husonge, Gelesu, and Yinfu led troops out Yongjin Gate—all met the enemy, cut down rebels with their blades, and fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 又協領賽沙畚、連生等，佐領薩音納、伊勒哈春等，防禦貴祥、明阿納等，驍騎校志善、佛爾奇納等，文職如知府伊麗亨等，武職千總安忻保等，皆陣亡。

translations.literal: Also Assistant Commandants Saishaben, Liansheng, and others; Vice Commandants Sayinna, Yilehachun, and others; Defense Officers Guixiang, Mingana, and others; Brave Cavalry Captains Zhishan, Foerqina, and others; civil officials such as Prefect Yiliheng; military officers such as Company Commander Anxinbao—all fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Commandants Saishaben and Liansheng, Vice Commandants Sayinna and Yilehachun, Defense Officers Guixiang and Mingana, Brave Cavalry Captains Zhishan and Foerqina, the civil official Prefect Yiliheng, the military officer Company Commander Anxinbao—all likewise fell.

sentences.zh: 合營縱火自焚，男婦死者八千餘人。

translations.literal: The whole camp set fires and burned themselves; men and women who died numbered more than eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The whole camp set fires and burned themselves; more than eight thousand men and women died.

sentences.zh: 包立身，諸暨人。

translations.literal: Bao Lishen, a native of Zhuji.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Lishen was from Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 家五十八都之包村，世業農。

translations.literal: His family lived in Bao Village of the fifty-eighth district; for generations they farmed.
translations.idiomatic: His family lived in Bao Village in the fifty-eighth district and had farmed for generations.

sentences.zh: 性樸魯，裡黨莫之重。

translations.literal: By nature plain and dull; the neighborhood did not esteem him.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and slow by nature, his neighbors thought little of him.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，忽能言休咎，多奇中。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he suddenly could speak of fortune and misfortune, often hitting strangely true.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 10 he suddenly began foretelling fortune and misfortune, often with uncanny accuracy.

sentences.zh: 節食茹素，夜則結跏趺坐。

translations.literal: He ate sparingly and took a vegetarian diet; at night he sat cross-legged.
translations.idiomatic: He ate sparingly and kept a vegetarian diet; at night he sat cross-legged in meditation.

sentences.zh: 時賊氛漸偪，人懷憂懼，爭奔詢，立身惟以行善為勗。

translations.literal: As rebel atmosphere gradually pressed close, people bore worry and fear and rushed in crowds to inquire; Lishen only exhorted them to do good.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels drew near, people came in crowds, anxious and afraid; Lishen urged only that they do good.

sentences.zh: 人疑信參半，不知其嫺武略也。

translations.literal: People were half in doubt and half in belief, not knowing he was skilled in military arts.
translations.idiomatic: People were half in doubt and half in belief, not knowing he was skilled in the arts of war.

sentences.zh: 十一年九月，賊陷紹興府，他賊復自金華來，諸暨亦陷。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eleventh year rebels took Shaoxing Prefecture; other rebels again came from Jinhua, and Zhuji also fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eleventh year rebels took Shaoxing; others came from Jinhua, and Zhuji fell as well.

sentences.zh: 於是首倡義旗，從者響應。

translations.literal: Thereupon he first raised the banner of righteousness, and followers answered in echo.
translations.idiomatic: He was the first to raise the banner of resistance, and followers answered from every side.

sentences.zh: 村踞山，三面皆水田，惟一路由塍埒達村。

translations.literal: The village perched on a hill; on three sides were all paddy fields; only one path by ridge-banks reached the village.
translations.idiomatic: The village stood on a hill, ringed on three sides by paddies; only one path along the dikes led in.

sentences.zh: 賊焚掠至其地，立身以靜待動，入者輒為所斃。

translations.literal: Rebels burned and plundered to that place; Lishen met motion with stillness; those who entered were at once killed by him.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels burned and plundered their way there, Lishen met force with stillness; whoever entered was cut down.

sentences.zh: 避賊者麕投之，棲止無隙地。

translations.literal: Those fleeing rebels crowded in like deer; there was no spare ground to lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees from the bandits crowded in until no space remained.

sentences.zh: 乃益選壯勇成勁旅，賊來攻，數不勝。

translations.literal: He then further selected stout brave men to form a crack force; rebels came to attack and several times could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: He picked still more stout fighters for a crack corps; the rebels attacked again and again without success.

sentences.zh: 立身不出村勦賊，賊至則戰，戰則身先，當其鋒立踣。

translations.literal: Lishen did not leave the village to pursue rebels; when rebels came he fought, and in fighting he took the lead—standing in their charge, foes fell on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Lishen did not leave the village to pursue rebels; when they came he fought, and in fighting he took the lead—standing in their charge, foes fell on the spot.

sentences.zh: 眾見賊易擊，雖文弱者亦揮戈從事，間諜入村者，罔弗獲。

translations.literal: The crowd saw rebels were easy to strike; even the weak in letters also swung spears to join; spies who slipped into the village were without exception captured.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd saw rebels were easy to strike; even men weak in letters swung spears to join; spies who slipped into the village were without exception taken.

sentences.zh: 無事則焚香默坐，有所指揮，從之必勝，遠近驚以為神。

translations.literal: When there was no affair he sat silently burning incense; whatever he directed, following it was sure victory—near and far marveled, thinking him divine.
translations.idiomatic: When there was no fighting he sat silently burning incense; whatever he directed, following it meant victory—near and far marveled, thinking him divine.

sentences.zh: 賊憚甚，使素稔立身者招降，立斬之。

translations.literal: Rebels feared him greatly and sent one who knew Lishen well to offer surrender; he beheaded him at once.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels feared him greatly and sent one who knew him well to offer surrender; he beheaded the envoy at once.

sentences.zh: 乃悉糾數郡悍黨，更番進攻，而往者輒衄。

translations.literal: They then altogether gathered fierce bands from several prefectures and attacked in rotation, but those who went were repeatedly repulsed.
translations.idiomatic: They mustered fierce bands from several prefectures and attacked in relays, yet each assault was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 群賊聞調攻包村，如就死地。

translations.literal: When bandits heard they were ordered to attack Bao Village, it was like being sent to the place of death.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits heard they were ordered against Bao Village, it was like being sent to their death.

sentences.zh: 相持八九月，大小數十戰，斃賊十餘萬，精銳強半盡。

translations.literal: For eight or nine months they held on, with dozens of battles great and small, killing more than a hundred thousand rebels until half their crack troops were gone.
translations.idiomatic: For eight or nine months they held on, fighting dozens of battles great and small, killing more than a hundred thousand rebels until half their crack troops were gone.

sentences.zh: 賊目有周姓者，眇而通形家言，乃週覽村外，悉其川源山脈。

translations.literal: Among rebel commanders was one surnamed Zhou, one-eyed but versed in the geomancer's arts; he then made a circuit outside the village and knew every stream source and mountain pulse.
translations.idiomatic: A one-eyed rebel commander named Zhou, skilled in geomancy, surveyed every stream and ridge around the village.

sentences.zh: 會旱，溪流弱，賊壅其上流，遂無涓滴。

translations.literal: A drought came; stream water was weak and rebels dammed the upper reaches, so not a trickle remained.
translations.idiomatic: Drought came; the streams ran low and rebels dammed the upper reaches until not a trickle remained.

sentences.zh: 村外井水，賊舉腐屍填之，出汲，則先以火器越井而陣，後人出屍乃得汲，腥穢不可飲，然且難得。

translations.literal: Wells outside the village—the rebels heaped them with rotting corpses; to draw water one had first to array fire-weapons across the well, then men hauled out corpses before they could draw—foul and undrinkable, yet even that was hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Wells outside the village—the rebels filled them with rotting corpses; to draw water one first had to array fire-weapons over the well, then haul out corpses before drawing—foul and undrinkable, and even that was hard to obtain.

sentences.zh: 人眾食寡，賊又四面斷糧道，不得達，賊遂索戰無已時。

translations.literal: Many mouths and little food; rebels also cut grain routes on all sides so none could get through; rebels then challenged battle without respite.
translations.idiomatic: Many mouths and little food; rebels also cut grain routes on all sides so none could get through; they then challenged battle without respite.

sentences.zh: 每合陣，所損相當，勢不能久持，終無一人言降者。

translations.literal: Each time formations closed the losses were equal; they could not long hold out, yet in the end not one person spoke of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Each time the lines closed the losses were equal; they could not hold out long, yet in the end not one spoke of surrender.

sentences.zh: 賊遂陰穿隧道而以金鼓聲亂之，立身不之省。

translations.literal: The rebels then secretly bored tunnels and used gong and drum sounds to confuse them—Lishen did not take notice.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dug tunnels in secret and masked them with gongs and drums—Lishen never caught on.

sentences.zh: 七月朔日，賊穴隧道自村社廟出，即縱火焚廟，眾出不意，大亂。

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month rebels tunneled out from beneath the village temple, set fire and burned the temple; the crowd rushed out unprepared and fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the seventh month rebels tunneled out from beneath the village temple, set fire and burned it; the crowd rushed out unprepared and fell into great disorder.

sentences.zh: 賊遇人即殺，未遇賊者亦倉皇圖盡。

translations.literal: Rebels killed whoever they met; those who did not meet rebels also frantically sought to end their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels killed whoever they met; those who did not meet rebels also frantically took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 立身見事敗，與其妹鳳英率親軍數千人死戰，潰圍出，至馬面山。

translations.literal: Lishen saw affairs were lost; with his sister Fengying he led several thousand of the personal guard in desperate battle, broke the encirclement, and reached Maimian Hill.
translations.idiomatic: Lishen saw the cause was lost; with his sister Fengying he led several thousand of his guard in desperate battle, broke the encirclement, and reached Maimian Hill.

sentences.zh: 賊躡之，圍數匝，鏖戰不得脫，中砲死。

translations.literal: Rebels followed hard, surrounded them in many rings, fought fiercely without escape—he was struck by cannon and died.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels followed hard, surrounded them in many rings, and fought until there was no escape—he was struck by cannon fire and died.

sentences.zh: 鳳英亦力竭自刎死，全家皆遇害，從者亦無一得脫。

translations.literal: Fengying too, strength exhausted, killed herself with a sword; the whole family suffered harm, and none of their followers escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Fengying too, her strength exhausted, killed herself with a sword; the whole family perished, and none of their followers escaped.

sentences.zh: 合村死者，蓋六十餘萬人。

translations.literal: The dead of the whole village amounted to more than six hundred thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: The dead of the whole village amounted to more than six hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 王玉文，字緯堂，金華人。

translations.literal: Wang Yuwen, style Weitang, a native of Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuwen, styled Weitang, was from Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 性強毅，好談經濟。

translations.literal: Strong and resolute by nature, fond of discussing statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Strong and resolute by nature, he loved to discuss statecraft.

sentences.zh: 道光二年舉人。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the second year of Daoguang.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial graduate in Daoguang 2.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，授於潛教諭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng appointed instructor of Yuqian.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 4 he was appointed instructor of Yuqian.

sentences.zh: 會粵寇據金陵，數上書當道論兵事，指陳兩浙形勢甚悉。

translations.literal: When the Guangdong bandits held Jinling he repeatedly sent up memorials to those in authority discussing military affairs, pointing out and stating the situation of the two Zhejiangs with great thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: While the Taiping held Nanjing he wrote again and again to the authorities on military affairs, mapping the peril facing both Zhejiangs in painstaking detail.

sentences.zh: 既而浙壤告警，奉檄領兵守天目山，又令塹於潛、臨安山谷，防賊闌入。

translations.literal: When Zhejiang territory sounded alarm, he received orders to lead troops to hold Tianmu Mountain, and was also commanded to dig trenches in the valleys of Yuqian and Lin'an to prevent rebels slipping in.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhejiang sounded the alarm, he was ordered to lead troops to hold Tianmu Mountain and to dig trenches in the valleys of Yuqian and Lin'an to keep rebels from slipping through.

sentences.zh: 既至，躬自履視，得某關廢阯，實為要隘，因建言修之。

translations.literal: On arrival he went in person to survey the ground and found an abandoned pass site that was truly a strategic choke point, and memorialized to repair it.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he surveyed the ground himself and found an abandoned pass that was truly a strategic choke point; he memorialized to repair it.

sentences.zh: 初偕昌化教諭高文祿行團練，於潛令素與玉文忤，多方撓之。

translations.literal: At first he joined with Changhua instructor Gao Wenlu to conduct militia drill; the Yuqian magistrate had long been at odds with Yuwen and obstructed him in every way.
translations.idiomatic: At first he joined Changhua instructor Gao Wenlu in militia drill; the Yuqian magistrate had long been at odds with Yuwen and obstructed him at every turn.

sentences.zh: 及是議築關，益譁然以為多事，而玉文銳於自任，不之顧。

translations.literal: When this proposal to build the pass arose, the uproar grew louder that he was making needless trouble, but Yuwen was keen to take the burden on himself and paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: When the plan to build the pass arose, the uproar grew that he was making needless trouble, but Yuwen was keen to shoulder the task himself and paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 十年，賊陷杭州，玉文將百人扼關，欲乘賊歸擊其惰，文祿力讚之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year rebels took Hangzhou; Yuwen with a hundred men held the pass, intending to strike the rebels on their return when slack—Wenlu strongly approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year rebels took Hangzhou; Yuwen with a hundred men held the pass, intending to strike the rebels when they returned weary—Wenlu strongly approved.

sentences.zh: 於是昌化、臨安、新城及本境山氓，咸持梃原受節度，官紳交阻之，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Then men of Changhua, Lin'an, Xincheng, and local hillfolk of his own district, all with clubs, willingly placed themselves under his command; officials and gentry together blocked it, and the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Then men of Changhua, Lin'an, Xincheng, and hillfolk of his own district, all with clubs, were ready to place themselves under his command; officials and gentry together blocked it, and the matter was shelved.

sentences.zh: 玉文恚甚，乞病歸，甫束裝，聞寇至，歎曰：「臨難而去，非夫也！」

translations.literal: Yuwen was deeply aggrieved; he begged leave on grounds of illness and was about to pack when he heard bandits had arrived; he sighed: "To leave in face of peril—that is not the act of a man!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen was deeply aggrieved; he begged leave on grounds of illness and was about to pack when he heard bandits had come; he sighed: "To flee when peril is at hand—that is not the act of a man!"

sentences.zh: 乃輟行。

translations.literal: He then stopped his journey.
translations.idiomatic: With that he stayed his journey.

sentences.zh: 適援軍至，玉文戒以守關毋出，不聽，戰五晝夜，眾寡不敵，棄關走。

translations.literal: Just then relief troops arrived; Yuwen warned them to hold the pass and not go out—they would not listen; they fought five days and nights, were outmatched, abandoned the pass and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Relief troops arrived; Yuwen urged them to hold the pass and not sally forth, but they would not listen; after five days and nights of fighting, outnumbered, they abandoned the pass and fled.

sentences.zh: 賊入城，官皆遁，有門下士偕二輿夫、一擔者來迎，玉文堅不去，迎者旋散。

translations.literal: Rebels entered the city; officials all fled; a follower with two sedan-bearers and one porter came to welcome him; Yuwen firmly would not leave, and the welcomers soon dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels entered the city; officials all fled; a follower with two sedan-bearers and a porter came to fetch him, but Yuwen would not leave, and they soon dispersed.

sentences.zh: 乃朝服挾刃坐，一賊當先入，格殺之，即舉火自焚。

translations.literal: He then sat in court dress with a blade in his lap; one rebel was about to enter first—he struck and killed him, then set fire and burned himself.
translations.idiomatic: He put on court dress, blade in hand, and sat waiting; when the first rebel entered he cut him down, then set fire and burned himself.

sentences.zh: 遺書付其子曰：「天熱，吾清白之體，不可俾鬱蒸，有鹽硝，舉以自化，汝曹毋過悲痛也！」

translations.literal: He left a letter to his son, saying: "The weather is hot; my spotless body must not be made to steam and suffocate—there is saltpeter; use it to consume me; you must not grieve too deeply!"
translations.idiomatic: He left a letter for his son: "It is hot; my spotless body must not be left to molder—there is saltpeter; use it to reduce me to ash; do not grieve beyond measure!"

sentences.zh: 寇退，得其屍池水中，朝服爇去，跣一足，眾哭殮之。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew his corpse was found in the pool; his court dress had burned away; one foot was bare; the crowd wept and laid him out.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits withdrew his body was found in the pool; his court dress was burned away and one foot bare; the people wept and laid him out for burial.

sentences.zh: 以其先有告病牒，大吏不以殉難聞，士民咸以為冤。

translations.literal: Because he had earlier a memorial of illness on file, the high officials did not report him as dying a martyr's death; scholars and commoners all thought it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had earlier filed for sick leave, senior officials did not report him as a martyr; scholars and commoners alike called it an injustice.

sentences.zh: 孫文德，嘉善人。

translations.literal: Sun Wende, a native of Jiashan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wende was from Jiashan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，年八歲，賊陷嘉善，家人攜出城，遇賊，相失，獨至村舍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng, aged eight, when rebels took Jiashan his family carried him out of the city; they met rebels and were separated; he alone reached a village house.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 10, when he was eight, rebels took Jiashan; his family carried him out but met rebels and were separated; he alone reached a farmhouse.

sentences.zh: 薄暮，十餘賊入舍就炊，將休矣，文德潛乞砒毒於賣藥人何桂生，密啟釜置之。

translations.literal: At dusk more than ten rebels entered the house to cook and were about to rest; Wende secretly begged arsenic from the medicine seller He Guisheng and quietly opened the pot and placed it in.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk a dozen rebels entered to cook and rest; Wende secretly begged arsenic from the apothecary He Guisheng and slipped it into the pot.

sentences.zh: 飯熟，賊方飢，食之，斃九人。

translations.literal: When the rice was cooked the rebels were hungry and ate; nine died.
translations.idiomatic: When the meal was ready the hungry rebels ate, and nine died.

sentences.zh: 二人未食，大駭，考掠文德，奮身大罵，賊殺之。

translations.literal: Two had not eaten and were greatly alarmed; they tortured Wende, who sprang up and cursed loudly; the rebels killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Two had not eaten; terrified, they tortured him; Wende sprang up and cursed them; the rebels killed him.

sentences.zh: 李貴元，字祥枝，永康人。

translations.literal: Li Guiyuan, style Xiangzhi, a native of Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guiyuan, styled Xiangzhi, was from Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 事母孝，以強有力聞。

translations.literal: He served his mother with filial piety and was known for great strength.
translations.idiomatic: Filial toward his mother, he was famed for his strength.

sentences.zh: 賊至，年已八十，乃出其大鐵鐧擊賊。

translations.literal: When rebels came he was already eighty and brought out his great iron mace to strike rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels came he was already eighty; he brought out his great iron mace and struck at them.

sentences.zh: 賊懼不敢動，貴元從容登樓。

translations.literal: The rebels feared and dared not move; Guiyuan calmly went up to the upper floor.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were afraid to advance; Guiyuan calmly went upstairs.

sentences.zh: 及群賊擁至，貴元遂遇害。

translations.literal: When a crowd of rebels pressed in, Guiyuan was harmed and died.
translations.idiomatic: When a crowd of rebels pressed in, Guiyuan was killed.

sentences.zh: 越日，其子求遺骸以出，賊亦不之罪也。

translations.literal: The next day his son sought the remains to bring them out; the rebels did not punish him either.
translations.idiomatic: Next day his son came for the body; the rebels did not harm him.

sentences.zh: 時錢塘汪玉璋、義烏金士玉、長興副貢生王泰東，均年逾八十，先後預於難。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Yuzhang of Qiantang, Jin Shiyu of Yiwu, and Wang Taidong of Changxing, a deputy tribute student—all over eighty—also met calamity in turn.
translations.idiomatic: About then Wang Yuzhang of Qiantang, Jin Shiyu of Yiwu, and Wang Taidong of Changxing, a deputy tribute student—all past eighty—also died in the calamity.

sentences.zh: 富陽瞽者陳小福，避山中，從賊者識其神卜也，囚之。

translations.literal: Chen Xiaofu, a blind man of Fuyang, hid in the mountains; rebels who knew his divinatory skill imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xiaofu, a blind diviner of Fuyang, hid in the hills; rebels who knew his gift imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 官兵攻急，賊勢蹙，乃命之卜。

translations.literal: Government troops pressed the attack hard; rebel strength was cramped, and they ordered him to divine.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops pressed hard; the rebels' position tightened, and they ordered him to divine.

sentences.zh: 小福曰：「若輩必盡死，無遺類，何卜為？」

translations.literal: Xiaofu said: "Your sort will all die, not one left—why divine?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofu said: "You will all die to the last man—why bother to divine?"

sentences.zh: 賊怒，剜其目，磔之。

translations.literal: The rebels were enraged, gouged out his eyes, and dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in rage gouged out his eyes and dismembered him.

sentences.zh: 皮匠某，逸其姓名。

translations.literal: A certain leatherworker—his name is lost.
translations.idiomatic: A leatherworker whose name is lost.

sentences.zh: 十一年，圍急，閩兵絕糧，不欲戰，巡撫王有齡登陴泣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the siege was desperate; Fujian troops were out of grain and unwilling to fight; Governor Wang Youling climbed the wall and wept.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the siege grew desperate; Fujian troops had no grain and would not fight; Governor Wang Youling wept upon the wall.

sentences.zh: 匠忽手百金至，叩首曰：「小人勸苦，蓄得百五十金，今留五十金自贍，餘請助餉。」

translations.literal: The craftsman suddenly came forward with a hundred taels of gold, kowtowed, and said: "This humble man toils hard and saved one hundred fifty taels; I keep fifty for myself and offer the rest to help pay the troops."
translations.idiomatic: The craftsman came forward with a hundred taels of gold, kowtowed, and said: "I am a poor worker who saved a hundred and fifty taels; I keep fifty for myself and offer the rest for the army's rations."

sentences.zh: 有齡為榜示轅門示勸。

translations.literal: Youling posted a notice at the yamen gate to encourage others.
translations.idiomatic: Youling posted a notice at the yamen gate to encourage the example.

sentences.zh: 城陷，匠自經死。

translations.literal: When the city fell the craftsman hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell the craftsman hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 羅正仁，湖南郴州人。

translations.literal: Luo Zhengren, a native of Chenzhou in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zhengren was from Chenzhou, Hunan.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，土匪蜂起，三月十四日夜半，突有賊數百人攻入城，戕知州胡禮箴。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng local bandits rose everywhere; on the fourteenth day of the third month at midnight, suddenly several hundred rebels burst into the city and killed Prefect Hu Lizhen.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 bandits rose; on the night of the fourteenth of the third month several hundred rebels burst into the city and killed Prefect Hu Lizhen.

sentences.zh: 正仁急起，倡辦團練，獲賊二十餘人，殺之。

translations.literal: Zhengren rose in haste, took the lead in organizing militia drill, captured more than twenty rebels, and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengren rose at once, organized militia, captured more than twenty rebels, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 由是各處效法，不數日，諸匪咸撲滅，餘黨恨正仁刺骨。

translations.literal: Thereupon every place followed the model; within a few days all bandits were suppressed; the remnant party hated Zhengren to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: Other places followed his lead; within days the bandits were crushed; survivors hated Zhengren bitterly.

sentences.zh: 會粵匪陷州城，土寇與合，正仁复率團要擊之。

translations.literal: When Cantonese rebels took the prefectural city, local bandits joined them, and Zhengren again led militia to intercept them.
translations.idiomatic: When Cantonese rebels took the city, local bandits joined them, and Zhengren again led militia to strike.

sentences.zh: 賊懸賞購正仁，正仁走避。

translations.literal: Rebels put a price on Zhengren's head; Zhengren fled and hid.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels offered a bounty for Zhengren; he went into hiding.

sentences.zh: 久之，聞母病，歸，賊偵知。

translations.literal: After a long while he heard his mother was ill and returned; rebels detected it.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he heard his mother was ill and returned home; rebels learned of it.

sentences.zh: 一日昧爽，突有賊三人至其家，正仁猝無所備，乃率二子春官等御之。

translations.literal: One day at dawn three rebels suddenly came to his house; Zhengren, caught unprepared, led his two sons Chunguan and the others to resist.
translations.idiomatic: One dawn three rebels came to his door; caught unprepared, he led his sons Chunguan and the others to fight.

sentences.zh: 俄賊眾奔至，眾寡莫敵，遇害。

translations.literal: Before long a rebel host rushed up; they could not match numbers and he was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a rebel host arrived; outnumbered, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 二子亦受重創，佯死得免。

translations.literal: His two sons also received grave wounds but feigned death and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons were badly wounded but played dead and escaped.

sentences.zh: 後春官痛父，更集團，日以剿匪為事。

translations.literal: Later Chunguan, grieving his father, gathered militia again and made daily suppression of bandits his business.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chunguan, grieving his father, raised militia again and made hunting bandits his daily work.

sentences.zh: 五年，城再陷，率團復攻之，每戰奮不顧身，多斬馘，為鄉里所倚庇。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the city fell again; he led militia to attack once more, fighting each battle without regard for his body, cutting down many heads, and was relied on by the countryside for protection.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the city fell again; he led militia to retake it, fighting recklessly and taking many heads, and the countryside leaned on him for protection.

sentences.zh: 同州人陳起書，字通甫，幼從兄起詩講求經世學，由附貢生候選訓導。

translations.literal: A fellow townsman, Chen Qishu, style Tongfu, in youth followed his elder cousin Qishi in studying statecraft; from enrolled tribute student he was a candidate instructor.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow townsman Chen Qishu, styled Tongfu, had studied statecraft with his cousin Qishi in youth and was a candidate instructor on enrolled tribute status.

sentences.zh: 道光十三年，逆瑤趙金龍叛，起書條陳禦瑤策，知州姚華佐多采用之，州城得無患。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang the rebellious Yao Zhao Jinlong rose; Qishu laid out plans to resist the Yao; Magistrate Yao Huazuo adopted many of them, and the prefectural city was unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 13 the Yao rebel Zhao Jinlong rose; Qishu memorialized plans to resist the Yao; Magistrate Yao Huazuo adopted many, and the city was spared.

sentences.zh: 金田賊起，起書謂西粵一隅地，賊不能久居，必竄楚。

translations.literal: When the Jintian rebels rose, Qishu said that western Guangdong was a corner of land—the rebels could not long stay and would surely flee into Chu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taiping rose at Jintian, Qishu said western Guangdong was a corner of land—they could not hold it long and would flee into Hunan.

sentences.zh: 竄楚，則大軍必扼衡州，郴、桂將首受禍。

translations.literal: If they fled into Chu, the great army would surely choke Hengzhou, and Chen and Gui would be first to suffer disaster.
translations.idiomatic: If they fled into Hunan, the main army would choke Hengzhou, and Chenzhou and Guizhou would suffer first.

sentences.zh: 遂畫守御之計，州牧不能用。

translations.literal: He then drew up plans for defense, but the prefect could not use them.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up defensive plans, but the prefect would not adopt them.

sentences.zh: 乃糾同志自集團丁於觀音寨、大頭隴，並築堡、修牆為堅壁計。

translations.literal: He then rallied like-minded men to gather militia at Guanyin Stockade and Datou Ridge, also building forts and repairing walls as a plan of stout walls and clear fields.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied comrades to gather militia at Guanyin Stockade and Datou Ridge, building forts and walls for a stout-walls strategy.

sentences.zh: 無何，賊果至，聞州境有備，遂引去。

translations.literal: Before long rebels indeed came; hearing the prefecture was prepared, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebels came; hearing the border was prepared, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時土寇邱倡道煽亂，擾及閭里，上官檄官軍剿之，不獲。

translations.literal: At that time the local bandit Qiu Changdao stirred disorder and disturbed the neighborhoods; superiors ordered government troops to suppress him without success.
translations.idiomatic: Then the local bandit Qiu Changdao stirred trouble; government troops were ordered to suppress him but failed.

sentences.zh: 起書命次子善墀、戚張樹榮依計誘擒之，並獲賊渠黃中鳳，事平。

translations.literal: Qishu ordered his second son Shanchi and kinsman Zhang Shurong to lure and capture him by plan, also seizing the bandit chief Huang Zhongfeng, and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Qishu sent his second son Shanchi and kinsman Zhang Shurong to lure and capture him, also taking the chief Huang Zhongfeng, and the trouble ended.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年四月，廣東賊何祿寇宜章，五月，州城陷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng, fourth month, the Guangdong rebel He Lu raided Yizhang; fifth month, the prefectural city fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Xianfeng 5 the Guangdong rebel He Lu raided Yizhang; in the fifth month the city fell.

sentences.zh: 起書率團練扼北鄉，賊不敢犯。

translations.literal: Qishu led militia drill to hold the north countryside; rebels dared not invade.
translations.idiomatic: Qishu led militia to hold the north countryside; rebels dared not enter.

sentences.zh: 有東鄉戚黨招起書為畫守禦策，祿適湘鄉王珍率師由衡州來援，乃命善墀迎師，自往東鄉，行抵塘溪，擬聯絡瑤嶺鄉民以拒之。

translations.literal: An eastern-country kinsman invited Qishu to draw up defense plans; Lu happened to have Wang Zhen of Xiangxiang leading troops in relief from Hengzhou; he therefore ordered Shanchi to welcome the army while he himself went to the east countryside, reaching Tangxi, intending to link Yao-ridge villagers to resist.
translations.idiomatic: An eastern kinsman asked Qishu to plan the defense; He Lu was met by Wang Zhen of Xiangxiang marching from Hengzhou; Qishu sent Shanchi to welcome the army while he went east to Tangxi to rally Yao-ridge villagers.

sentences.zh: 而土匪咸通賊，偵其往，中道要劫之，遂被執。

translations.literal: But local bandits all communicated with rebels; detecting his going, they waylaid him on the road and he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Local bandits were in league with rebels; learning his route, they ambushed him on the road and took him.

sentences.zh: 群賊久耳起書名，擁於坐，宛轉誘降，起書罵不絕口，抵死不降，賊遂計議俟何祿至，乃縛其手，日夜環守之。

translations.literal: The rebel host had long heard Qishu's name; they crowded him in the seat and coaxingly urged surrender; Qishu cursed without cease and would not yield to death; the rebels then planned to wait until He Lu arrived, bound his hands, and guarded him day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels had long heard his name; they crowded round and urged him to yield; he cursed without cease and would not submit; they bound his hands and guarded him day and night until He Lu should come.

sentences.zh: 起書於八月七日絕粒，死之。

translations.literal: Qishu on the seventh day of the eighth month stopped eating grain and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the eighth month Qishu stopped eating and died.

sentences.zh: 陳景滄，字少海，龍陽人。

translations.literal: Chen Jingcang, style Shaohai, a native of Longyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingcang, styled Shaohai, was from Longyang.

sentences.zh: 父永皓，直隸長垣知縣，有聲於時。

translations.literal: His father Yonghao was magistrate of Changyuan in Zhili and had a reputation in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yonghao had been magistrate of Changyuan in Zhili and was well regarded.

sentences.zh: 景滄幼凝重，守道義，留心經世之務。

translations.literal: Jingcang from youth was grave and steady, kept to righteousness, and attended to affairs of statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jingcang was grave and steady, held to righteousness, and minded affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 以咸豐元年舉人官內閣中書。

translations.literal: As provincial graduate in the first year of Xianfeng he served as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate of Xianfeng 1, he served as secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 粵亂作，湖北巡撫胡林翼治楚軍備賊，徵闢賢俊，以景滄佐軍事。

translations.literal: When the Guangdong turmoil arose, Huguang Governor Hu Linyi organized Chu armies against rebels and summoned worthy men; Jingcang assisted in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Cantonese rebellion broke out, Governor Hu Linyi of Hubei organized armies against the rebels and summoned talent; Jingcang assisted in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 積功保知府，命籌餉岳、灃。

translations.literal: By accumulated merit he was recommended for prefect and ordered to raise funds in Yue and Fen.
translations.idiomatic: By merit he was recommended for prefect and ordered to raise funds in the Yue and Fen regions.

sentences.zh: 景滄剔除宿弊，事集而民不擾，嘗曰：「籌餉病民，已非善政；

translations.literal: Jingcang eliminated long-standing abuses; affairs were gathered and the people were not disturbed; he once said: "Raising funds harms the people—that is already not good government;
translations.idiomatic: Jingcang cut out old abuses; work was done without troubling the people; he once said, "Fund-raising already harms the people—that is not good government;

sentences.zh: 若更貪其利，是官民交病，吾不為也！」

translations.literal: if one further greedily takes profit from it, that is officials and people both harmed—I will not do it!"
translations.idiomatic: if one then profits from it, officials and people are both harmed—I will not do it!"

sentences.zh: 不數年，以親老辭歸里，閉戶山中，侍養之餘，以讀書為樂。

translations.literal: Within a few years, on account of aged parents he resigned and returned home, shut his door in the mountains, and apart from serving them took pleasure in reading.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he resigned for aged parents, shut his door in the hills, and apart from caring for them took joy in books.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，閩浙總督左宗棠調往福建，湖南巡撫劉琨亦強起景滄，景滄咸謝不赴。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tongzhi, Fujian-Zhejiang Governor Zuo Zongtang summoned him to Fujian; Hunan Governor Liu Kun also strongly raised Jingcang—all Jingcang declined.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 6 Governor Zuo Zongtang summoned him to Fujian; Hunan Governor Liu Kun also pressed him—all invitations Jingcang declined.

sentences.zh: 八年，丁父憂，哀毀廬墓，益遠人事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he entered mourning for his father, grieved ruinously at the tomb hut, and drew still farther from worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he mourned his father, grieving at the tomb, and withdrew further from public life.

sentences.zh: 初，軍興，募民為勇，越境擊賊，湖南尤盛。

translations.literal: At first, when armies arose, civilians were recruited as braves to strike rebels across borders—Hunan was especially flourishing in this.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when war began, civilians were recruited as braves to fight rebels across borders—Hunan led in this.

sentences.zh: 暨賊平，勇散歸，不事生業，相率入哥老會。

translations.literal: When rebels were pacified the braves scattered home, took up no livelihood, and in groups entered the Gelaohui.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels were pacified the braves went home without livelihood and in bands joined the Gelaohui.

sentences.zh: 哥老會者，起四川，異姓相約為昆弟，同禍福，結盟立會，千里相應。

translations.literal: The Gelaohui arose in Sichuan; men of different surnames pledged as sworn brothers, shared fortune and misfortune, formed alliances and lodges, and answered one another a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: The Gelaohui began in Sichuan: unrelated men swore brotherhood, shared fortune and woe, formed lodges, and answered one another across a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 其盟長之大者，輒擁眾數千人，橫行郡邑，吏莫敢詰，良懦憚之，則入會求庇。

translations.literal: The greater lodge chiefs often mustered thousands of men, rampaged through prefectures and districts, and officials dared not inquire; the good and timid feared them and entered the society to seek protection.
translations.idiomatic: Greater chiefs mustered thousands, rampaged through counties, and officials dared not challenge them; the timid joined for protection.

sentences.zh: 入者既眾，勢乃益厚，流行湘、楚間。

translations.literal: Once entrants were many the power grew thicker and spread through Hunan and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: As membership swelled their power grew and spread through Hunan and Hubei.

sentences.zh: 初但為奸盜，均其財，繼焚掠村市，抗官兵，窺城邑。

translations.literal: At first they were only thieves sharing loot; later they burned and plundered villages and markets, resisted government troops, and eyed cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: At first they were mere thieves sharing plunder; then they burned villages, fought government troops, and eyed walled towns.

sentences.zh: 長沙、衡州諸屬，屢撲屢熾。

translations.literal: Under Changsha and Hengzhou they were repeatedly suppressed and repeatedly flared up.
translations.idiomatic: Around Changsha and Hengzhou they were crushed again and again yet kept flaring up.

sentences.zh: 十年，益陽何春台，龍陽劉鳳儀、劉繼漢等，率會眾為亂，聚縣西安化山中，距景滄家十餘裡。

translations.literal: In the tenth year He Chuntai of Yiyang and Liu Fengyi and Liu Jihan of Longyang led lodge members in revolt, gathering in the Anhua hills of the county, a dozen li from Jingcang's home.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year He Chuntai of Yiyang and Liu Fengyi and Liu Jihan of Longyang led lodge men in revolt, gathering in Anhua hills a dozen li from Jingcang's home.

sentences.zh: 景滄聞變急，密告巡撫，巡撫檄益陽、龍陽兩縣往捕，會眾方傳檄諸州縣黨人，約同時發難。

translations.literal: Jingcang heard the alarm in haste and secretly informed the governor; the governor ordered the magistrates of Yiyang and Longyang to arrest them; the lodge members were just circulating proclamations to party men in every prefecture and county, agreeing to rise together.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the alarm, Jingcang secretly informed the governor, who ordered Yiyang and Longyang to arrest them; the lodge was circulating calls to rise in every county.

sentences.zh: 未至期，捕者適至，遂先舉事，犯益陽。

translations.literal: Before the date arrived the arresting party happened to come; they therefore rose first and invaded Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before the appointed day the arresting party arrived; they rose early and struck Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 途中值景滄，執之，景滄責以大義，數其罪。

translations.literal: On the road they met Jingcang, seized him; Jingcang rebuked them with the great principle and counted their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: On the road they seized Jingcang; he rebuked them with righteousness and recounted their crimes.

sentences.zh: 被數刃，罵不絕口，賊群斫之。

translations.literal: He received many blades, cursed without cease, and the rebel host hacked him.
translations.idiomatic: They cut him many times; he cursed without cease, and the rebels hacked him to death.

sentences.zh: 長子克枟、次子克權從行，以身障景滄，並及於難。

translations.literal: His eldest son Keyun and second son Kequan followed on the journey, shielding Jingcang with their bodies, and also met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Keyun and Kequan, traveling with him, shielded him with their bodies and died as well.

sentences.zh: 景滄長身玉立，恂恂孝友。

translations.literal: Jingcang was tall as jade standing, dutiful and brotherly in manner.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and straight as jade, he was dutiful and brotherly in manner.

sentences.zh: 與人交，訥然若不出口，至論古今忠孝及國政得失，輒慷慨流涕，義形於色。

translations.literal: In meeting others he was tongue-tied as if he could not speak; but when discussing loyalty and filial piety through the ages and gains and losses in national policy he would weep freely, righteousness showing in his face.
translations.idiomatic: With others he seemed tongue-tied; yet on loyalty, filial piety, or the nation's fortunes he wept freely, righteousness plain on his face.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈道員，給世職。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported he was posthumously made a daoyuan and granted a hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: When the news reached court he was posthumously made a daoyuan and granted a hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 何霖，字雨人，廣西興安人。

translations.literal: He Lin, style Yuren, a native of Xing'an in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He Lin, styled Yuren, was from Xing'an, Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 少讀書，以諸生食廩餼。

translations.literal: In youth he read books and as a licentiate lived on grain stipend.
translations.idiomatic: He read in youth and lived on his licentiate's grain stipend.

sentences.zh: 抗志高尚，不屑屑治章句。

translations.literal: His ambition was lofty; he disdained to fuss over parallel prose and exegesis.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty in ambition, he disdained to fuss over parallel prose and commentary.

sentences.zh: 性沈毅，有膽略。

translations.literal: By nature deep and resolute, he had courage and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Deep and resolute by nature, he had courage and stratagem.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，興安盜王苟滿、趙廷蘭等作亂，陷縣城，囚官吏。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng the Xing'an bandits Wang Gouman, Zhao Tinglan, and others made disorder, took the county seat, and imprisoned officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 the Xing'an bandits Wang Gouman, Zhao Tinglan, and others rebelled, took the county seat, and imprisoned officials.

sentences.zh: 霖聞變，匿老弱，自與族弟進賢急詣省求援，中道遇賊，為所劫。

translations.literal: Lin heard the alarm, hid the old and weak, and with his clansman Jinxian hurried to the province to seek aid; on the road they met rebels and were seized.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the alarm, Lin hid the old and weak and hurried with his cousin Jinxian to seek aid; on the road rebels seized them.

sentences.zh: 霖詭辭脫進賢，入見賊酋，賊素重霖，以上賓禮之。

translations.literal: Lin with deceitful words freed Jinxian, entered to see the rebel chief; rebels had long esteemed Lin and treated him with guest-of-honor ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Lin spoke deceitfully to free Jinxian, then saw the rebel chief, who had long esteemed him and treated him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 霖謬為甘言，飲啖自若。

translations.literal: Lin falsely spoke sweet words and ate and drank as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Lin spoke sweet words and ate and drank at ease.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，因說賊酋曰：「君等舉大事，宜先收人望，蔣方第諸人，邑之豪俊，原假良馬利劍為君輩致之，非常之業可圖也！」

translations.literal: When wine was warm he therefore said to the rebel chief: "You gentlemen undertake a great affair and should first win men's regard—Jiang Fangdi and the others are the county's eminent men; I beg fine horses and sharp swords to bring them to you gentlemen—a extraordinary enterprise can be plotted!"
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was warm he told the chief: "You undertake a great affair and must win men's regard—Jiang Fangdi and others are the county's leading men; lend me horses and swords to bring them to you, and a great enterprise is within reach!"

sentences.zh: 賊喜，如約。

translations.literal: The rebels were pleased and agreed as promised.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were pleased and agreed.

sentences.zh: 霖遂以方第等六人至，留賊中，賊信不疑。

translations.literal: Lin then brought Fangdi and six others; they remained among rebels, and rebels trusted without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Lin then brought Fangdi and six others to stay among the rebels, who trusted them completely.

sentences.zh: 霖陰謀方第間賊黨，將乘間舉事，會官軍擊賊靈川，屢勝，賊分兵攻金州亦敗，眾稍稍引散。

translations.literal: Lin secretly plotted with Fangdi to sow discord among rebel factions and would seize an opportunity to act; government troops struck rebels at Lingchuan and won repeatedly; rebels divided troops to attack Jinzhou and also lost; the host gradually dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Lin secretly plotted with Fangdi to divide the rebels and strike when chance came; government troops beat them at Lingchuan; a thrust at Jinzhou failed; the host began to scatter.

sentences.zh: 霖遁歸，偕方第一夜集鄉兵，盡縛北鄉諸賊。

translations.literal: Lin slipped home, and with Fangdi in one night gathered village soldiers and bound all rebels of the north countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Lin slipped home; with Fangdi he gathered village soldiers in one night and bound every rebel of the north countryside.

sentences.zh: 分守要害，號召鄰鄉團眾，分三路攻城。

translations.literal: They divided to hold key points, called up neighboring village militia, and attacked the city on three roads.
translations.idiomatic: They held key points, called neighboring militia, and attacked the city on three roads.

sentences.zh: 賊不為備，遂復興安，擒苟滿等。

translations.literal: Rebels were unprepared, and thus Xing'an was recovered and Gouman and others captured.
translations.idiomatic: Caught unprepared, the rebels lost Xing'an; Gouman and others were captured.

sentences.zh: 官軍至，獻捷，主兵者攘其功，賞不及霖。

translations.literal: When government troops arrived they presented the victory; the commander of troops appropriated the merit, and rewards did not reach Lin.
translations.idiomatic: When government troops came they claimed the victory; the commander took the credit, and Lin received no reward.

sentences.zh: 益與方第倡言興團練，立規約，厚佽給，人樂為用。

translations.literal: All the more with Fangdi he advocated raising militia drill, establishing regulations, generous allowances—men were glad to serve.
translations.idiomatic: He and Fangdi then urged raising militia, setting regulations, and generous pay—men were glad to serve.

sentences.zh: 賊黨謀再舉，憚霖不敢發。

translations.literal: Rebel factions plotted to rise again but feared Lin and did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel factions plotted another rising but feared Lin and held back.

sentences.zh: 四年，恭城賊陷灌陽，霖率興安團屯邊隘，賊不得逞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Gongcheng rebels took Guanyang; Lin led Xing'an militia to hold border passes, and rebels could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Gongcheng rebels took Guanyang; Lin led Xing'an militia to the border passes and kept the rebels from advancing.

sentences.zh: 相持數月，樂平賊自別道來援，霖與方第議增丁壯，移營前進，遏其鋒。

translations.literal: After several months' standoff, Leping rebels came in relief by another route; Lin and Fangdi discussed adding stalwart men, shifting camp forward to check their momentum.
translations.idiomatic: After months of stalemate, Leping rebels came by another route; Lin and Fangdi added men, moved camp forward, and checked their advance.

sentences.zh: 十一月，次茗田，賊以大隊從大風坳出犯霖壘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he halted at Mingtian; rebels with a great host came out from Dafeng'ao to attack Lin's camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he camped at Mingtian; rebels in force came through Dafeng'ao against his camp.

sentences.zh: 所部祗五百人，續調者未至，霖麾眾迎擊，奮鬥竟日，力竭戰死。

translations.literal: His command was only five hundred men; reinforcements had not arrived; Lin waved the host to meet the attack, fought fiercely all day, strength spent, and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He had only five hundred men; reinforcements had not come; Lin led a counterattack, fought all day, and died when his strength gave out.

sentences.zh: 方第暨其兄子二人並歿於陣。

translations.literal: Fangdi and his elder brother's two sons also perished in the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Fangdi and his elder brother's two sons also fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 賊再入興安，焚霖廬舍，盡殺其家人，霖父挈孫走臨桂，得免。

translations.literal: Rebels again entered Xing'an, burned Lin's house, killed his whole family; Lin's father led a grandson to flee to Lingui and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels re-entered Xing'an, burned Lin's house, and killed his family; his father fled with a grandson to Lingui and survived.

sentences.zh: 事平，興安民思其功，建祠祀之。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled the people of Xing'an remembered his merit and built a temple to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: When peace returned the people of Xing'an honored him with a temple.

sentences.zh: 蹇諤，字一士，貴州遵義人。

translations.literal: Jian E, style Yishi, a native of Zunyi in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jian E, styled Yishi, was from Zunyi, Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 道光二十六年舉人。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the twenty-sixth year of Daoguang.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial graduate in Daoguang 26.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，大挑得教職。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, in the great selection he received an educational post.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 he passed the great selection for an educational post.

sentences.zh: 明年，諤還自京，適桐梓教匪楊龍喜作亂，長驅出婁山關，逼遵義。

translations.literal: The next year E returned from the capital; it happened that the Tongzi teaching-bandit Yang Longxi rebelled, drove straight out through Loushan Pass, and pressed Zunyi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he returned from the capital just as the Tongzi sectarian Yang Longxi rebelled, marched through Loushan Pass, and threatened Zunyi.

sentences.zh: 知府硃右曾要擊，敗還。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhu Youzeng intercepted them and was beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhu Youzeng met them in battle and was driven back.

sentences.zh: 賊遂以八月十六日圍城，營郭外雷台山。

translations.literal: Rebels then on the sixteenth day of the eighth month besieged the city and camped outside the walls on Leitai Hill.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth of the eighth month the rebels besieged the city and encamped on Leitai Hill outside the wall.

sentences.zh: 是時黔中治平久，民老死不見兵革，初遭寇亂，眾洶洶欲潰。

translations.literal: At that time Qianzhong had long been at peace; the people grew old without seeing war; when they first met bandit turmoil the crowd was turbulent and about to break.
translations.idiomatic: Qian had been at peace so long that men had grown old without war; at the first alarm the people nearly panicked.

sentences.zh: 獨諤力言賊可擊，於是人心稍定。

translations.literal: E alone insisted the rebels could be struck, and thus hearts were somewhat steadied.
translations.idiomatic: E alone insisted the rebels could be beaten, and hearts steadied a little.

sentences.zh: 久之，官兵漸集，而賊亦日附。

translations.literal: After a long while government troops gradually gathered, and rebels also daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: In time government troops gathered, and the rebels also grew daily.

sentences.zh: 諤謁提督趙萬春、布政使炳綱於螺瑯堰，陳利害，請由石盤扼賊糧，拊其背，自領兵練四百人營馬家河，复募二百人益之，屢戰皆捷。

translations.literal: E called on General Zhao Wanchun and Financial Commissioner Binggang at Luolangyan, stated advantages and harms, asked to choke rebel grain by Shiban, strike their rear, himself led four hundred militia to camp at Majia River, again recruited two hundred to augment them, and won battle after battle.
translations.idiomatic: He visited General Zhao Wanchun and Commissioner Binggang at Luolangyan, laid out the situation, proposed choking rebel supplies at Shiban and striking their rear, led four hundred militia to Majia River, raised two hundred more, and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 賊酋李七王者尤獷悍，以千餘人入貴陽大道，踞龍坪水口寺，諤率所部圍攻，盡殲之。

translations.literal: Rebel chief Li the Seventh King was especially fierce; with more than a thousand men he entered the Guiyang highway and held Longping Shuikou Temple; E led his command to surround and attack and annihilated them all.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chief Li the Seventh King was especially fierce; with a thousand men he seized Longping Shuikou Temple on the Guiyang road; E surrounded and destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 七王自焚死，賊氣奪。

translations.literal: The Seventh King burned himself to death; rebel spirit was broken.
translations.idiomatic: The Seventh King burned himself; rebel morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，官兵破東路櫻桃丫，賊憑險拒戰，不即克，諤以兵從中坪繚其後，大破之，乘勝進克羊耳丫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month government troops broke the eastern route at Yingtao Pass; rebels held the terrain and fought, not quickly taken; E with troops from Zhongping wound behind them, broke them greatly, and pressing the victory took Yang'er Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month troops broke the eastern Cherry Pass; rebels held the heights; E outflanked them from Zhongping, routed them, and took Yang'er Pass.

sentences.zh: 賊退屯金錢山，引渠灌田，計死守。

translations.literal: Rebels withdrew to camp at Jinqian Hill, led channels to irrigate fields, planning to die holding fast.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back to Jinqian Hill, flooded fields by canal, and prepared to hold to the death.

sentences.zh: 諤令健卒負草涉凍薄而焚之，於是官兵攻雷台益急，蜀兵亦進复桐梓，龍喜蹙，遂焚巢夜遁。

translations.literal: E ordered stalwart soldiers to carry grass across the thin ice and burn it; thereupon government troops pressed Leitai harder; Shu troops also advanced to recover Tongzi; Longxi was cramped and burned his nest and fled by night.
